contexts.title: Travel and entry — leave a way home
read: The shop’s back room smells of paper and damp stone. Below the floor hatch, a line of steps disappears beyond the lantern’s reach. Evin leaves a chalk mark beside the latch. “This stays clear,” they say. “Whatever is down there, this is how we come back.”

The hatch and chalk mark provide a return point before the stairs take you out of the shop's light. The smell of damp grows nearer below. You can check the opening and keep the landing clear before deciding who descends first.
run:
Follow the actual city route and agreed permissions. No extra travel fee, elapsed day or unexpected magical transport is applied.

Inspect light, rope and the stair from above. Evin identifies the support carrying the shop floor; nobody has to test it with their weight.

Map the direct stair and optional coal chute. The chute is a slower alternate entry after its brittle rung is supported; opening it does not bypass private tenants’ rooms.

Confirm a check-in and the decision that ends today’s work: uncertain load, water reaching the first landing or a person asking to stop. These are proposed precautions, not hazards already occurring.

A rest upstairs is available by agreement with the current host. No rest or recovery is automatically granted.

No check for a safe inspected ladder and patient descent. If a character knowingly rushes the unbraced chute, DC 13 Investigation first spots the brittle rung; a failure means a noisy reachable landing and 1d6 bludgeoning damage, once, after warning. A rope and brace avoid it.

contexts.title: Room 1 — the forgotten stair
read: At the foot of the stair, the lantern catches a patch of stone worked rougher than the wall around it. Letters once stood here. Across the threshold lie empty desks, blank book spines and dust that has settled undisturbed beneath their legs.

The rough patch interrupts the wall where writing has been removed. Dust beneath the desks records a quieter history than a spoken explanation would. You can examine the threshold, stone, and books without deciding who erased the letters.
run:
Retain original room key 1. The chisel marks are visible with ordinary light; a rubbing records erased lettering without identifying its author.

Allow the party to sketch the threshold, shelf positions, water stain and exit before touching anything. Evin’s present building sketch can be compared later but does not date the original society.

An inventory tag behind an ordinary shelf places one offered deposit in a recognizable numbered group. Patient inspection finds it; it establishes a correspondence to Ressa’s inventory, not her ownership of the whole archive.

The absence of occupants is a present observation. Do not decide whether they died, fled, were displaced or survived somewhere.

Use conditional sensory description: if someone moves a lamp, one chair seems to keep a faint second shadow briefly. Record only what actual witnesses notice; no one automatically gains a vision or hears Halaster.

DC 13 Investigation can find the shelf tag immediately; a systematic ten-minute search finds it without a roll. A mason’s-tools comparison distinguishes deliberate chiseling from water wear without revealing who did it.

contexts.title: Room 2 — the listening desks
read: The first desk swallows the edges of your voice. A step away, the sound returns. Under its lamp rests a brass arm poised above an empty page, as if the reader had only just stepped out.

A single step separates the altered sound from ordinary speech. The brass arm and empty page remain visible beneath the lamp. You can mark that boundary and compare voices from either side without putting a hand into the mechanism.
run:
Retain original room key 2. Sounds become faint close to the desk; this is not the Silence spell and does not cancel verbal components. Written notes, gestures and moving away work.

Place a plain sheet beneath the arm and its ordinary contact releases Catalogue Leaf Nine. If the party avoids the arm, a mechanical catch can be opened slowly with tools.

Leaf Nine shows one larger center and eight satellites. One outer identity is blank. The counting evidence concerns a nine-site catalogue, not a geography map, portals or a proof that each entry is active.

Explain where the leaf was found and its condition. A copy and the leaf are one underlying source, however many people repeat its words.

No medallion, token, attunement, blood or character-specific ability is needed. If a personally held object is voluntarily compared, its response is a separate observation and does not disclose its owner automatically.

DC 14 Investigation or Arcana finds the indexing rhythm quickly; failure jams the arm until ten minutes of careful cleaning. The leaf remains accessible either way.

observed: One outer identity is unentered.

observed: Sound weakens near a desk and returns when moved away, if tested.

claimed: The catalogue calls these entries sites.

contexts.title: Room 3 — the circular table
read: Eight small name-slips surround a broad central hollow. Beside them, two columns have survived the damp: one headed “recorded,” the other “sounding.” Several rows end in space that nobody has filled.

The headings name two different columns, and the hollow leaves space at their center. You can copy the arrangement exactly, including the empty rows. Nothing in the surviving words tells you to fill those spaces or name whoever belongs there.
run:
Retain original room key 3. The central hollow is part of the diagram, not a lock demanding a medallion. Edge shapes let the group count damaged slips without inserting anything.

Provide visible separation between recorded identity and observed activity. A named place can be dormant. Never count an inlay filling as network activation.

The slips include several generations of handwriting; exact dates remain uncertain pending comparison. They do not prove one society built every site.

Show a damaged row whose missing edge has no matching fragment. Invite the players to label it unknown, compare an offered external inventory or make a clearly marked hypothesis. No answer has to fill the gap.

If a reconstruction-related label is encountered at the approved stage, it is an incomplete cross-reference to environmental restoration notes, not instant proof of family identity or successful resurrection.

No roll to count edges and distinguish the two column headings. DC 14 History recognizes different generations of writing; failure leaves dating open for Selise’s later comparison. DC 14 Investigation saves ten minutes matching damaged edges; careful arrangement still succeeds.

contexts.title: Room 4 — the sealed folio
read: A waxed packet waits behind glass. The latch beside it is plain brass. Farther back, a second rod bears a warning in careful letters: “A reading is not a summons.” The two mechanisms are clearly separate.

The glass, latch, and warning rod offer three features to inspect separately. The words on the rod are readable before anything is moved. You can ask which mechanism holds the packet without treating its contents as permission to operate the other.
run:
Retain original room key 4. Opening the mechanical glass panel is harmless. Distinguish that latch from the optional test rod before anyone acts. Copying through glass, opening the latch or dismantling the panel all work.

The packet holds incomplete coastal bearings and a description of pale ground in a living valley. These are leads to Observatory and Scar, not exact modern routes. Vess or independent surveys must confirm them.

At Act III research readiness, include an incomplete restoration index naming a project labeled Looking Glass and directing a reader to deposited design revisions. It supports a research lead; the full project purpose needs comparison with actual dungeon records.

A loose binding receipt references an old repair and an external customer ledger. Keep maker/name details unexpanded until the actual collection and period are prepared. Nessa can compare craft later; do not conjure Ilyra’s name from style or make every document Halaster’s.

Optional rod test: disclose that moving it produces a local sound/label response audible in the shop, then ask whether everyone nearby consents. On use, dust rises and desks repeat previously spoken words; several worn

labels become briefly readable. Copy them as one observed local response. Release the rod to stop.

The test neither activates the Nine nor empowers Halaster. A curious customer may ask a question if actually present upstairs; any rumor depends on what they saw and later chose to say. Passive routes contain all essential clues.

No check to use the simple latch, copy through glass or understand the warning. DC 14 Arcana or appropriate tools identifies how to hold the rod for a short local test; failure means using the visible stop/release and asking Orren to inspect later, with no damage or lost folio.

observed: Operating the optional rod repeats local speech and briefly restores worn labels, only if actually tested.

contexts.title: Decision — preserve, copy or relocate
read: Back at the landing, a bead of water gathers under the lowest shelf. Selise holds out blank tags. Ressa has left space for signatures beneath her inventory. There is room for more than one name on each receipt.

The gathering water gives the shelf a practical concern, while the blank tags leave handling undecided. You can name an owner, a keeper, and what each may do. More than one signature can preserve responsibility without making every object communal.
run:
If the party has not entered, frame this as planning from the inspection report rather than a return with found objects.

Show the ordinary conservation trade-off: copying is quick but incomplete, moving fragile pages protects them but separates them from place, and in-situ protection requires work and continuing access. No choice makes every stakeholder disappear.

Offer a modest initial materials estimate of 10 gp for dry wrapping, tags and removable shelf blocks, subject to a real quote. The party can use available gear, negotiate work, or leave the decision to the custodians. No automatic coin deduction.

Ressa accepts private-name redaction and numbered receipts if offered a way to compare her claim. Selise accepts leaving disputed leaves sealed while public technical material is copied. Evin accepts a clear passage and no heavy new load on the support. These are negotiating positions, not compulsory acceptance of unreasonable demands.

Record each moved original’s find-spot, temporary holder, permitted readers and return terms. Select who actually learned each clue; copied private names are not automatically public.

If a genuine dispute remains, agree a neutral custodian or

preserve the status quo while checking authority. No involuntary curse, chase or combat is necessary.

Reasonable specific terms and evidence resolve ordinary concerns without a persuasion gate. DC 14 Persuasion may reduce the number of meetings or improve a bounded access schedule; failure leaves the stated conditions available.

contexts.title: Arrival · a place with its own day
read: Beyond the passage, a bucket knocks softly against the well’s rim. Someone has laid a cloth over a half-finished repair. Two neighbors pause beside a heavy press: one measures the space it needs, while the other measures the space everyone else will have left.

The well and covered repair occupy a space people already share, while the press narrows the passage between them. You can see why both neighbors are measuring. An introduction can begin with a greeting before it becomes an offer to move something.
run: If tr-courtyard and tr-neighbors already happened, begin with recognition and the actual unresolved lodging question. Do not replay first meetings or the press favor.
Introduce only Nessa and Orenna. Nessa can offer the available rooms under the proposed subletting arrangement; Dracuseth introduces people but does not decide terms.
Show the simple court plan privately, then show on TV only when this location is actually introduced. The plan is illustrative, with no hidden tactical feature.
Explain access, shared spaces and the private doors. A neighbor can say where things are without listing every resident or their future hooks.
If the party helps with the press, a safe plan and enough willing help suffice. No compulsory strength test, injury or debt.

contexts.tv: Preview the Mending Court plan; show it deliberately after the arrival is in play.
choices: Inspect the available rooms.
Talk briefly and arrange a later visit.
Keep the introduction and choose other lodgings.

contexts.title: Lodging · agree what home means for now
read: Nessa opens both doors and waits outside while you look. The larger room has space to sleep; the smaller could become several different things. “Tell me what you need first,” she says. “Then we can see whether these rooms can provide it.”

Two open doors give you a chance to inspect the rooms before discussing a bargain. The smaller space has no purpose assigned to you yet. You can ask about access, privacy, storage, and shared use while Nessa waits for your needs.
run: Use the ten lodging fields. Fill only agreed terms; unknown amounts and dates remain blank. Nessa’s authority to sublet is part of this proposed arrangement to confirm, not a deed already granted.
Discuss a trial stay, recurring rental, or message address. Five people need a deliberate bedding plan; Pebble can ask for a sturdy ground-floor place and anyone may ask for a private corner.
Rent, deposit, purchases and repayment are separate reviewed transactions. This card does not subtract currency, award property, replace stored item custody or start a rest.
The party chooses what goes into storage. No one is required to display a private object or hand over a key. Ordinary locks are not guaranteed containment for an unknown hazard.
Orenna can check accessible passage and delivery space. Her advice creates no obligation to perform unpaid work for residents.
private: Original Echo Below proposal and read-aloud. No meeting, rental, promise, discovery or return has happened merely because this card exists.
contexts.tv: The plan may remain visible; rental notes stay private until selected for sharing.
choices: Agree a short trial with a review date.
Negotiate continuing rooms and ordinary access rules.
Use only a consensual message address.
Decline and leave the rooms available.

contexts.title: First evening · one small choice
read: The court settles into evening sounds: a shutter, a last bucket of water, the scrape of a chair beneath the awning. There is no ceremony waiting for you. There is simply enough room for someone else to sit down.

The awning shelters a place to sit while the day's last chores finish around it. The scrape of a chair leaves the choice of joining to you. A first evening need not become a public account of everything in your packs.
run: Offer one brief invitation to each character, not five required speeches. A practical preference is as useful as an emotional answer.
Use the character opportunity cards only when welcome. Keep private clue content off the communal table and phones unless its owner chooses disclosure.
A request for a shelf, curtain, stronger seat or writing space becomes a proposed improvement. Agree materials, permission, cost and help; do not mark it built now.
If they chose other lodgings, make this a short visit or supper invitation. No one is insulted if they go elsewhere to rest.
Keep the entire evening ordinary. No ominous sound, figure, missing resident or prophetic dream is required.
private: Original Echo Below proposal and read-aloud. No meeting, rental, promise, discovery or return has happened merely because this card exists.
contexts.tv: Use the ordinary courtyard plan and low town ambience; no mystery overlays.
choices: Share a small preference or practical task.
Spend time quietly alongside the neighbors.
Leave for another appointment or rest.

contexts.title: First return · recognition without a reward speech
read: Orenna moves her basket from the passage as you approach. “There is room,” she says. From the bindery, Nessa looks up long enough to offer a greeting, then sets her work safely aside. The court has had a day of its own while you were gone.

The clear passage lets you bring equipment in without interrupting the bindery's work. Nessa sets that work aside carefully rather than abandoning it. You can ask what changed here before choosing which news from below to share.
run: Use after an actual return. Choose the success, retreat, hard-return or unresolved variant from confirmed events; returning alive is not proof a contract succeeded.

If a real delivery or message was expected and someone agreed to receive it, describe that parcel with sender, recipient and seal. Otherwise offer an empty place for future deliveries rather than inventing a letter.
Nessa still has a deadline; Orenna still has errands. They can offer a short welcome without abandoning their own lives.
Let the party clean gear in an agreed area and decide what stays in storage. No automatic loot sale, healing, rest or opening of sealed property.
If the party wants to improve home, use mc-improvement. A small earned preference is enough; no compulsory spending or gratitude.

contexts.tv: Ordinary court view; only deliberately shared account text belongs on TV.
choices: Give a public account with private details omitted.
Ask for quiet or a practical service.
Check a real promised delivery or message.

contexts.title: A later supper · meet the Fen siblings
read: Jori sets two bowls down, counts the chairs, and asks before bringing any more. Pellan is trying to fold a stall cloth around a basket that plainly disagrees with him. “We are considering a better stall,” Jori says. “Apparently the basket intends to stay here.”

The chairs and bowls give Jori a practical count to make. Pellan's awkward basket offers a problem small enough to discuss over supper. You can offer a hand or an opinion without taking responsibility for their whole livelihood.
run: Introduce Jori and their adult brother Pellan together after the first residents are familiar. Pellan is not Pell from the Gilded Compass.
Their independent need is a better stall. Jori wants financial security; Pellan wants to test a new route before the good location goes. Both concerns are reasonable.

Offer a small bounded task: compare two accessible routes, help repair a rain cover, look over clearly shared figures, or sample suitable ordinary food. These are optional and do not require funding the business.
If the party declines, the siblings can ask a coworker, make a smaller trial or defer. No stall is lost automatically because a hook was ignored.
The family’s historical account stays in later private prep. Do not place the unnamed boy, Tavin or Halaster in this first supper conversation.
private: Original Echo Below proposal and read-aloud. No meeting, rental, promise, discovery or return has happened merely because this card exists.
contexts.tv: Ordinary courtyard view; a short public introduction is optional, not automatic.
choices: Offer one limited piece of help.
Give an opinion without taking responsibility.
Enjoy supper and leave business with the siblings.

contexts.title: Second return · life has continued
read: One chair has acquired a new peg. A line of washing has moved to make better use of the sun. The table is occupied by ordinary work, but a space is cleared when you arrive. Someone asks how long you can stay before your next errand.

The new peg and moved washing are changes you can see without asking anyone to explain them. The cleared space offers room for an account when you are ready. Your next errand is still a question, not a schedule the household has chosen.
run: Use the relationship record to choose one meaningful follow-up, not a tour of every resident. If no promise exists, choose an independent routine or modest request.
Only mention a finished repair, delivered letter, paid fee or improved stall if approved. The new chair peg is harmless background dressing; it is not the party’s completed project.
A kept promise can earn specific trust: permission to use a work space, a named introduction, or a warm invitation. It does not unlock everyone’s secrets.
An unkept promise prompts a factual question about scope and timing. Allow explanation and renegotiation before interpreting a delay as betrayal.
If a genuine letter from Dianna or another personal contact is ready, use the owner’s private channel and the established correspondence source. No unsolicited public reading.
private: Original Echo Below proposal and read-aloud. No meeting, rental, promise, discovery or return has happened merely because this card exists.
contexts.tv: Court scene only; private letters and promises stay in their selected channels.
choices: Follow up on one real obligation.
Offer a bounded contribution to a neighbor’s work.
Keep the return quiet and arrange another time.

contexts.title: Aven’s request · share the day fairly
read: At the landing desk, Aven starts a line again, stops, and puts the chalk down. “Could I borrow half an hour of quiet?” they ask. “I can move the practice after that. I am trying to pass this without keeping everyone awake.”

The chalk rests beside an unfinished line at the landing desk. Aven's request has a time limit and a reason you can understand. You can agree, suggest another place, or ask what noise would make practice possible for everyone.
run: Aven’s request is ordinary study and scheduling. Discuss alternatives rather than treating one person’s need as a command.
Aven needs a better schedule and examination practice. Donavan or Aldric may offer to listen, compare a mundane note or suggest a study routine; none must become a teacher.
Trista can suggest a quiet corner, Pebble can notice a rattling work surface, Ringgo can negotiate shared hours, and any player may have a better idea. Let nonmagical contributions work.

No player gives away a spell, prepares different magic, spends a resource or rolls an ability check without choosing to. Aven passes or fails only when the later outcome is actually played or approved.
If the party declines, Aven can use a different hour or workspace. Keep goodwill independent of compulsory labor.
private: Original Echo Below proposal and read-aloud. No meeting, rental, promise, discovery or return has happened merely because this card exists.
contexts.tv: No magical effect is required for this ordinary conversation.
choices: Agree a trial quiet period.
Find another location or schedule.
Offer advice or leave Aven to study.

contexts.title: Third return · something familiar
read: Evening finds the court midway through its usual argument with unfinished work. A chair is turned toward the light. Someone has saved a place at the table, with no assumption about how long you will stay. For a moment, returning is an ordinary thing.

The turned chair catches what remains of the evening light, while work still waits around the table. A saved place offers company without claiming your whole night. You can sit, help with a task, or ask for a quiet corner.
run: Choose two residents whose recorded relationships make this return relevant; the npc list is an available cast, not everyone speaking at once.
Refer to an actual preference, improvement or kept promise if one exists. If it does not, use neutral routine and let familiarity grow now.
Give residents good news, a modest frustration or a plan grounded in approved changes. Unapproved business outcomes remain suggestions for DM review.
Let each interested character choose a contribution without assigning a personality role. Silence, paying fairly, keeping a promise and choosing a comfortable chair all count as living here.

End this scene normally. The optional disturbance is a separate deliberate choice, available only after at least three approved ordinary returns and an ordinary evening. Deferring it indefinitely is valid.

contexts.tv: Ordinary court with restrained ambience. Do not add ominous effects by default.
choices: Spend a quiet evening in company.
Review one actual promise or improvement.
Keep the evening entirely ordinary.

contexts.title: Make a mark · one useful improvement
read: There is room for a shelf here, or a curtain, or perhaps nothing more complicated than a seat that fits its owner. The space does not have to become grand to become more useful.

A shelf needs space, a curtain needs an agreed boundary, and a useful seat needs someone who wants it there. You can ask the people sharing this corner before beginning work. Improving a home can start with one ordinary change.
run: Offer a broad doorway mat and gear rack, sturdy chair, writing shelf, privacy curtain, shared route board or rain repair. Players may propose something else.
Check whether it affects rented rooms, shared space or another resident’s property. Obtain the relevant agreement before work.
Review materials, cost, responsible people, timeline and whether ownership changes when the rental ends. No silent spending or instant completion.
Manual skill, hiring a worker, buying an ordinary item or choosing a smaller solution are equally valid. A character is not obliged to prove usefulness through class abilities.
After approved completion, record the physical change by layout space. Future return narration can reference that exact improvement without publishing who stores a secret nearby.
private: Original Echo Below proposal and read-aloud. No meeting, rental, promise, discovery or return has happened merely because this card exists.
contexts.tv: Plan may stay visible. Label a change only after it is approved and selected for sharing.
choices: Plan an improvement with a reviewed cost.
Offer time for a resident’s chosen repair.
Keep the current arrangement and revisit later.

contexts.title: Optional later disturbance · a doorway that was not there
read: For several breaths, the patched wall beyond the table shows the frame of a different doorway. Its edge is clear enough to draw. Then the patch is simply a patch again, while the ordinary sounds of the court continue.

The brief outline has vanished, leaving the repaired wall available to examine. You can compare sketches or ask who saw the same edge. The ordinary sounds do not explain the doorway, and its appearance gives no instruction to open it.
run: Hold until at least three ordinary returns are approved and the party has had a normal evening. The app must never trigger this automatically from time, a scene visit or a quest stage.
Choose two plausible witnesses in the scene when it occurs; do not retroactively give everyone the same observation. No one is harmed and no possession goes missing.
Describe only the visual discrepancy and its duration. Halaster’s intent, the apparatus, historical ownership and a returned person are not established by this sight.

A sketch and independent accounts can preserve evidence. If Aven offers an explanation, label it an inference with a possible way to test it. Nessa recognizes no binding and Jori tells no family story merely because the wall changed.
If the party declines investigation, record an unresolved observation for its witnesses. No escalation punishes disinterest; the next home scene can be ordinary again.
The courtyard remains a place with real people and everyday needs. Do not burn it down, kidnap a neighbor or make them secret agents to force attachment.
private: Original Echo Below proposal and read-aloud. No meeting, rental, promise, discovery or return has happened merely because this card exists.
Later mystery connection follows the approved campaign outline. Jori’s family account and Nessa’s binding comparison remain separate future evidence, requiring actual access and corroboration.
contexts.tv: Use ordinary court or a deliberately approved text description. No automatic flashing, secret labels or scene replacement.
choices: Record separate accounts and a sketch.
Ask a chosen specialist using only approved details.
Keep the observation private and defer investigation.

contexts.title: Before play
run: Open the player screen on the table TV, check it shows the cover with no DM information, then make a pre-session restore point and confirm the backup is available.

Party: Trista, Donavan, Ringgo, and Pebble are level 1. Aldric joins in Session 1 as a level-1 wizard with a DM-built sheet. Confirm his prepared spells and current resources with Bowman. Check everyone’s current HP and resources before play.
Start with the printed enemy counts, then judge pacing for five actual PCs once the new sheets are known. Do not increase enemy damage to compensate for party size.
Immediate objective: locate Gundren and Sildar. No party member begins with secret knowledge of the Echo.
private: Use milestone advancement. The PCs can reach level 2 after the hideout is resolved; do not require a full cave clear if rescue or negotiation resolves its stakes.
contexts.tv: Start with the campaign cover. Keep the hideout map and route schematic private.

contexts.title: On the road · a wheel that will not turn
read: A loaded wagon leans into the verge, one wheel sunk at an awkward angle. Two travelers have spread a blanket for the unloaded goods. A third holds up a broken length of wood and gives it a look no amount of optimism is going to improve.

The blanket keeps the goods out of the dirt while the tilted wagon blocks an easy return to travel. The broken wood gives you something concrete to inspect. You can ask what assistance is wanted before lifting, repairing, or choosing to pass on.
run: Optional original complication on a road segment the DM selected. Edda Vale, a practical independent carrier, wants to protect her cargo and workers; she is neither an ambusher nor secretly an Echo agent.

The visible problem is a cracked wheel support after a deep rut. A competent practical plan, available materials and help can work without a roll; use a fitting check only when the outcome is uncertain and failure has a clear consequence.
Possible approaches: unload and brace for a short move to safety; carry a request to the next established stop; offer a suitable spare; negotiate paid labor; wait together; politely continue.
Before a roll or expenditure, state the time, materials and risk. Failure costs an agreed delay or needs a different repair; it does not suddenly cause lethal injury.

News from Edda is a dated traveler’s claim with a named source, not confirmation of every Phandalin event. If the party helps, she can later recognize them in the city; record the actual name and promise.
No stat block or combat encounter is required. If the party provokes violence, pause to stage a suitable encounter using existing creature tools and actual participants.
private: Original Echo Below scene and dialogue; future preparation, not an event that has happened.
This traveler is a new optional NPC proposal, not an existing friend. Helping does not create a permanent debt or a free cargo reward.
contexts.tv: Use the campaign cover as neutral road staging. Existing ambush art contains misleading bodies/enemies; do not reuse it as an empty road.
choices: Repair or stabilize the wagon.
Arrange assistance and keep moving.
Decline with or without sharing road information.

contexts.title: A night on the journey · what travels with you
read: At the night’s stopping place, boots are set within reach and tomorrow’s route is checked once more. Beyond the small circle of conversation, the world continues without asking for an explanation. For a little while, there is time for an ordinary question.

The checked route and reachable boots keep tomorrow close without filling the whole evening. There is room to choose a watch and agree how to wake one another. A conversation here can be ordinary, private, or left until morning.
run: Use a stop actually chosen: a safe camp, rented room or caravan halt. Adjust the description to weather and shelter; do not require a fire or trigger Aldric’s smoke distress without Bowman’s participation.

Offer a single spotlight to someone who has had less attention. Donavan may write Dianna a bounded observation; Pebble can compare the route with his sketch; Ringgo can define useful honest work; Trista can keep or share a thought voluntarily; Aldric may choose a practical act of care or a private records question.
No memory, secret revelation or fellowship speech is required. The remaining players may respond or let the moment pass.
Review guards, light, supplies and rest using the existing group-rest tool. A scene change does not heal anyone or restore resources.

Compress uneventful remaining legs into a brief travel account once route, elapsed time and supplies are reviewed. If weather changes, offer shelter, pace or delay choices rather than adding combat by default.
private: Original Echo Below scene and dialogue; future preparation, not an event that has happened.
The BELOW token stays private unless Trista discloses it. Aldric’s family and resurrection truths remain unrevealed.
contexts.tv: Use neutral cover art or black screen. Keep private letters and character questions off TV; ambience is optional.
choices: A short conversation or private note.
A rest with actual recovery review.
Skip uneventful travel to the next chosen stop.

contexts.title: 1 · Gundren rides ahead
read: The wagon is loaded with mining supplies and road provisions. Gundren Rockseeker checks the straps one last time while Sildar waits beside their horses. The dwarf grins, but he seems impatient to get to Phandalin. “Take this to Barthen’s Provisions. I’ll meet you there.”

Gundren turns to Donavan. “If the mine holds anything unusual, write down what you actually see before anyone decides what it is worth.” To Trista, he adds, “Make sure I come back to read his account.” To Ringgo: “Choose the safe camp over the fast one. I hired you to bring people through.”
run: Gundren and Sildar ride ahead; the party escorts the wagon from Neverwinter toward Phandalin. The published wagon-delivery payment is 10 gp per character.
Pebble joined the escort to reach Phandalin’s mines without getting lost. Aldric also joins from the start; ask Bowman why he chose this job rather than assigning a reason.
private: Gundren once paid a dangerous debt for Trista and gave her another chance. He trusts her. He hired Donavan for careful field records and Ringgo for legitimate escort work.
Do not reveal or hand over Echo’s Whisper here. Its future custody follows play.
contexts.tv: Show Gundren’s departure scene. After he leaves, ask for marching order.

contexts.title: 2 · Dead horses and ambush
read: The trail bends between close woods. Two horses lie across the road ahead, dead and pierced by black-feathered arrows. Their saddlebags hang open. Neither rider is in sight.

The open saddlebags and arrows give you more to examine than the bodies alone. Beyond the bend, trunks and tangled growth break up the view into the woods; anyone moving closer will have to choose where to stand and what to watch.
run: Four goblins hide in the woods, two on each side. Roll one goblin Stealth check at +6 and compare it with each traveler’s passive Perception for surprise.
On their first turn, two goblins rush forward while two shoot from cover. Goblins can Hide or Disengage as a bonus action. If three fall, the last tries to flee toward the hideout.
Goblin: AC 15, HP 7, speed 30 ft.; scimitar or shortbow +4 to hit, 1d6+2 damage. Passive Perception 9.
All five player characters choose their own opening actions. Track initiative, cover, and who is actually visible to the goblins.
private: Do not show goblin positions on the TV until spotted or until they attack. Stage them on your map with “On TV” unchecked if useful.
contexts.tv: Show The empty horses first. After goblins are seen or attack, use Road ambush · revealed; switch to the gridded road map when positions matter.
choices: Let them pick targets, use cover, capture a goblin, pursue a runner, or secure the wagon.
If combat is easy, let it be a clean win. The real problem is finding the missing travelers.

contexts.title: 3 · Clues after the road fight
read: The woods settle. The two horses still block the road. Broken brush and small tracks lead north, away from the wagon and into thicker trees.
Among the goblins’ castoffs is a rough dark stone token. One side bears a single worn word: BELOW. The other carries part of a circle rubbed almost smooth.
run: Any inspection of the ambush area reveals the goblin trail north of the road. A DC 10 Survival check adds that about a dozen goblins used it and two human-sized captives were dragged away. Following a fleeing goblin or questioning a captive also establishes the lead.
A captive goblin knows that the dwarf and his map were sent toward Cragmaw Castle; it can lead or direct the party toward the hideout.
If they miss the BELOW token, move it to the hideout. It is optional and never required to continue.
private: The token is not Echo’s Whisper. It has no power or key function. Donavan may think its mark resembles damaged research notation but cannot solve it.
After a distant boom, anyone studying it notices it feels cooler. No roll is needed.
contexts.tv: Leave the road map up while they search, or use a black screen for a quiet conversation.
choices: If they take the wagon to Phandalin, Barthen says Gundren has not arrived and urges investigation. Bring the trail lead back through local concern rather than ending the rescue plot.

contexts.title: 5 · Cave mouth and approach
read: The trail ends below a wooded hill. A shallow stream runs from a dark cave mouth, with a narrow path beside it. Briars crowd the bank. Cold water murmurs over stone.

The stream and the strip of dry ground offer different approaches to the same black opening. From outside, you can study the banks and the briars before stepping beneath the hill; the sound of running water makes the darkness beyond seem deeper.
run: Area 1 is the cave mouth, 2-foot-deep stream, and briars. A noisy arrival can alert the bored goblin lookouts in area 2. The streamside thickets give half cover; cave chambers beyond areas 1–2 are dark.
Switch to the interior map once they enter. Reveal only what their position and light allow. One interior map square equals 5 feet.
private: The cave opening is ordinary stone. Do not show a portal, visible Echo effect, or secret room layout.
contexts.tv: Show the cave-mouth art. Use the cave approach battle map only if exact positions outside matter.

contexts.title: Area 2 · Goblin blind
read: Across the stream, the briars are thick enough to swallow the path. A board creaks faintly behind them, then goes still.

The vegetation interrupts your view of whatever lies beyond it. The stream remains an obvious landmark beside the approach, but the brief creak gives you a reason to watch the cover rather than hurry past it.
run: Two goblins wait in a hollowed-out blind on the east side of the stream. The surrounding thickets give half cover. They can fire from cover and may surprise careless intruders.
If the party made loud noise at the entrance, the lookouts notice and shoot through the briars. Do not automatically alert every cave room.
Goblin: AC 15, HP 7, attack +4 for 1d6+2, bonus-action Hide or Disengage.
contexts.tv: Show Area 2 · Goblin blind beside the fogged map. Reveal the streamside briars first; place the two goblins only when seen or when they attack.
choices: Stealth, scouting, a rush across the stream, a distraction, or retreat can all change the position of this fight.

contexts.title: Area 3 · Kennel and wolves
read: A sharp animal smell cuts through the damp cave air. Chains scrape against stone. Three pairs of eyes turn toward you from the dark, and low growls fill the cramped chamber.

The scrape of the chains marks the animals' movements more clearly than the dim light does. There is little room to spread out here, and the growling rises when attention turns toward them. You can stop at the edge of the chamber before choosing how to approach.
run: Three wolves are chained here. They cannot initially reach someone who stays back on the entrance steps, but barking can carry.
DC 15 Animal Handling calms them; food can distract them with a DC 10 check. No fight is required.

The narrow chimney to area 8 is at the back of the kennel, beyond the wolves’ normal chain reach from the entrance. Reaching it requires a plan for the wolves. Climbing calls for DC 10 Athletics; a poor fall can deal 1d6 bludgeoning damage.
Wolf: AC 13, HP 11, speed 40 ft.; bite +4 for 2d4+2 piercing, DC 11 Strength save or prone. Pack Tactics gives advantage when an ally is beside the target.
private: Do not release all three wolves just because a character steps inside. Their chains and the goblins’ reactions matter.
contexts.tv: Show Area 3 · Kennel as the characters enter or illuminate it, beside the fogged map. Place three wolf icons.

contexts.title: Area 4 · Steep passage
read: The main passage climbs steeply beside the stream. Spray darkens the stone, and loose rubble shifts underfoot. Above the noise, you can make out another passage crossing high overhead.

Water follows the slope past your boots, leaving the rising stone slick and dark. The crossing overhead is separate from the route at your feet; from here, you can judge the climb and look for movement above without knowing where either passage ends.
run: Rubble is difficult terrain. The fragile ledge collapses under more than 100 pounds; DC 10 Dexterity save, taking 2d6 bludgeoning on a failure or half on a success. Failure also knocks the creature prone.

Route at a glance: the stream climbs toward the overpass (area 5); a higher side passage west reaches Yeemik’s den (area 6); the den connects east across the bridge to the twin pools (area 7), then south to Klarg (area 8). The kennel chimney is a separate shortcut to area 8.
Noise from nearby goblins may be heard by careful listeners. Show the hazard through crumbling stone and spray before asking for a risky crossing.
contexts.tv: Show Area 4 · Steep passage beside the fogged map. Reveal the rising passage and stream gradually; the bridge should appear only when it comes into view.

contexts.title: Area 5 · Overpass and flood
read: A rickety bridge crosses the passage high above the water. A small figure shifts against the shadowed ceiling. Farther upstream, the sound of pooled water presses through the cave.

The bridge's boards and supports stand out against the rock when your light catches them. Below, the stream continues along the climbing passage. The figure above and the louder water ahead give you two different things to watch as you decide whether to advance.
run: One goblin guards the bridge about 20 feet above the stream. If it spots the party, it signals area 7; the first flood arrives on the following round on the pool goblins’ initiative count.

Telegraph a flood with a physical roar and rising water. In the surge’s path, DC 10 Dexterity save to avoid being swept away; a caught creature can try DC 15 Strength to hold on. Failure washes it toward area 1 and deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage.
The goblins at the pools can release a second surge if still able. The bridge can also break; a fall from it is dangerous.
Goblin: AC 15, HP 7, attack +4 for 1d6+2, bonus-action Hide or Disengage.
private: That second sensation is the campaign’s Echo beat. It causes no save, damage, or immediate explanation.
contexts.tv: Show Area 5 · Overpass when the party can see the bridge, beside the fogged map. Keep the guard hidden until spotted or until it signals the pools.

contexts.title: Area 6 · Yeemik and Sildar
read: A cooking fire lights an uneven cavern. Goblins look up from their meal. On a higher ledge, a battered human man is held upright by one of them. He can barely stand.
One goblin raises a hand for the others to hold. “You want the human? Then we have something to discuss.”
run: Six goblins occupy the den: Yeemik has 12 HP, and the five ordinary goblins have 7 HP each. Sildar is alive at 1 HP, unarmed, and without armor.
Yeemik wants Klarg removed. He may promise Sildar in exchange, then press for ransom rather than honoring his word. Do not force the party to accept.
If openly threatened, Yeemik can shove Sildar from the ledge; the fall deals 1d6 damage unless the party intervenes or heals him. Make his position and danger legible before the decision.
All six use goblin attacks: AC 15, +4 to hit for 1d6+2, bonus-action Hide or Disengage. Yeemik has 12 HP; each other goblin has 7 HP. Yeemik carries three gold teeth worth 1 gp each and 15 sp.
contexts.tv: Show Area 6 · Goblin den only when the den comes into view. Reveal the higher ledge and place Yeemik, five other goblins, and Sildar once visible.
choices: Talking, trickery, sneaking, rescue, retreat, and combat are all valid. The five players lead the negotiation and decide how to protect Sildar.

contexts.title: Area 7 · Twin pools
read: Two dark pools fill much of the cavern. Water presses against rough stone-and-timber dams. The waterfall’s echo makes quieter movement hard to place.

The rough barriers hold back a great deal of water, and the noise fills the space around them. You can inspect their visible supports, look for ground that stays out of the current, or study the onward route before putting someone beside a dam.
run: Three goblins guard the water controls. If warned by the bridge goblin, they can release a pool into the main passage. The water must actually be present to release.
Noise here can warn Klarg in area 8; one goblin may run to him if a fight breaks out.
Goblin: AC 15, HP 7, attack +4 for 1d6+2, bonus-action Hide or Disengage.
private: Keep the physical water hazard separate from the fleeting magical pressure. The pressure is atmosphere, not a second attack.
contexts.tv: Show Area 7 · Twin pools when seen, beside the fogged map. Place the three goblins according to how they respond to alarms.

contexts.title: Area 8 · Klarg’s cave
read: Sacks and crates fill the far side of the cave. Smoke from a low fire climbs toward an opening above. Behind the stolen supplies, a hulking figure rises, morningstar in hand, while a wolf bares its teeth.

The stacked goods divide the cavern into patches of cover and narrow sightlines. Firelight catches the raised weapon and the wolf's teeth, while smoke drifts toward the opening overhead. The way you entered remains behind you as you choose how to answer this reception.
run: Klarg the bugbear has AC 16 and 27 HP. Morningstar +4 to hit, 2d8+2 piercing. Ranged javelin +4, 1d6+2. If he surprises someone and hits in round one, add 2d6.
Ripper is a wolf: AC 13, HP 11, bite +4 for 2d4+2 and DC 11 Strength save or prone. Two goblins also fight here.
The fire pit deals 1 fire damage when entered, or 1d6 to a creature that falls prone in it. Supply piles give half cover.
If warned, Klarg and his group use the supply piles as cover. If Ripper dies, Klarg may flee down the chimney toward area 3.
Treasure: 600 cp, 110 sp, two potions of healing, and a jade frog statuette with golden eyes worth 40 gp. Returning the stolen Lionshield Coster goods in Phandalin earns 50 gp.
contexts.tv: Show Area 8 · Klarg’s cave only when the supply cave is entered. Place Klarg, Ripper the wolf, and two goblins as they become visible.
choices: Klarg is the sharpest damage spike for a level-1 PC. Give tracks, noise, or frightened goblins as warning. Reassess only after seeing the five actual character sheets.

contexts.title: After rescue · What Sildar knows
read: Once he can sit and breathe, Sildar looks toward the cave passage. “Gundren was taken away from here. They wanted him—and the map he carried.”

The passage is still close enough that a voice raised here could carry farther than intended. Sildar's words give you a name and an object to ask about, but not a destination. There is time to hear him out, check what help he needs, and decide where to take the conversation.
run: Gundren and his map were sent toward Cragmaw Castle. Sildar does not know where the castle is.
The goblins said someone called the Black Spider wanted Gundren captured. Sildar does not know the Spider’s identity.
Sildar also came toward Phandalin to investigate missing wizard Iarno Albrek. He wants to reach town and offers 50 gp if escorted there safely.
At 1 HP and without his equipment, Sildar is not ready to lead a fight. If he receives healing and gear, he may help briefly while retaining his own goals.
private: Do not have Sildar interpret the BELOW token or name the Echo. His information advances Gundren’s rescue, not the later cosmology.
contexts.tv: Use the current map or a black screen for a conversation. Do not put future locations on the TV.

contexts.title: 4 · Goblin trail and traps
read: The goblin trail narrows under the trees. Broken twigs and churned earth show several small creatures passed this way, with heavier marks among them. The road disappears behind you.

Each disturbed patch offers a place to slow down and look, while the thicker growth limits what you can see ahead. You can keep the heavier marks in view, check the ground before committing your weight, or pause to decide how closely you want to follow.
run: The hideout is about five miles from the ambush. Roughly ten minutes along the trail is a snare: the lead character notices automatically with passive Perception 12 or higher; otherwise DC 12 Perception. If triggered, DC 10 Dexterity save to avoid being hoisted 10 feet and restrained. A character cut down carelessly takes 1d6 bludgeoning.

Another ten minutes along is a concealed 10-foot-deep pit: the lead notices automatically with passive Perception 15 or higher; otherwise DC 15 Perception. If triggered, DC 10 Dexterity save to avoid the fall; falling deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage.

A careful physical plan, tool, familiar, or probing pole can avoid a trap without a roll. Trista and Ringgo can scout; Donavan can document tracks; invite Pebble and Aldric to add their own methods. Pebble may remember mountain terrain but is uneasy about losing the route.
A short rest is possible if the party secures a defensible place. It costs time, and enemies may respond to noise.
contexts.tv: Show Goblin trail. Use Snare · discovered and Pit · discovered only after each trap is noticed or triggered. Do not show the cave image until they reach it.
choices: If the party chooses a different route, keep their rescue lead available through tracks, captives, or Phandalin.
