If triggered, DC 10 Dexterity save to avoid being hoisted 10 feet and restrained. A character cut down carelessly takes 1d6 bludgeoning.

Another ten minutes along is a concealed 10-foot-deep pit: the lead notices automatically with passive Perception 15 or higher; otherwise DC 15 Perception. If triggered, DC 10 Dexterity save to avoid the fall; falling deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage.

A careful physical plan, tool, familiar, or probing pole can avoid a trap without a roll. Trista and Ringgo can scout; Donavan can document tracks; invite Pebble and Aldric to add their own methods. Pebble may remember mountain terrain but is uneasy about losing the route.
A short rest is possible if the party secures a defensible place. It costs time, and enemies may respond to noise.
contexts.tv: Show Goblin trail. Use Snare · discovered and Pit · discovered only after each trap is noticed or triggered. Do not show the cave image until they reach it.
choices: If the party chooses a different route, keep their rescue lead available through tracks, captives, or Phandalin.

contexts.title: 4 · Goblin trail and traps
read: The goblin trail narrows under the trees. Broken twigs and churned earth show several small creatures passed this way, with heavier marks among them. The road disappears behind you.

Each disturbed patch offers a place to slow down and look, while the thicker growth limits what you can see ahead. You can keep the heavier marks in view, check the ground before committing your weight, or pause to decide how closely you want to follow.
run: The hideout is about five miles from the ambush. Roughly ten minutes along the trail is a snare: the lead character notices automatically with passive Perception 12 or higher; otherwise DC 12 Perception. If triggered, DC 10 Dexterity save to avoid being hoisted 10 feet and restrained. A character cut down carelessly takes 1d6 bludgeoning.

Another ten minutes along is a concealed 10-foot-deep pit: the lead notices automatically with passive Perception 15 or higher; otherwise DC 15 Perception. If triggered, DC 10 Dexterity save to avoid the fall; falling deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage.

A careful physical plan, tool, familiar, or probing pole can avoid a trap without a roll. Trista and Ringgo can scout; Donavan can document tracks; invite Pebble and Aldric to add their own methods. Pebble may remember mountain terrain but is uneasy about losing the route.
A short rest is possible if the party secures a defensible place. It costs time, and enemies may respond to noise.
contexts.tv: Show Goblin trail. Use Snare · discovered and Pit · discovered only after each trap is noticed or triggered. Do not show the cave image until they reach it.
choices: If the party chooses a different route, keep their rescue lead available through tracks, captives, or Phandalin.

contexts.title: Area 2 · Goblin blind
read: Across the stream, the briars are thick enough to swallow the path. A board creaks faintly behind them, then goes still.

The vegetation interrupts your view of whatever lies beyond it. The stream remains an obvious landmark beside the approach, but the brief creak gives you a reason to watch the cover rather than hurry past it.
run: Two goblins wait in a hollowed-out blind on the east side of the stream. The surrounding thickets give half cover. They can fire from cover and may surprise careless intruders.
If the party made loud noise at the entrance, the lookouts notice and shoot through the briars. Do not automatically alert every cave room.
Goblin: AC 15, HP 7, attack +4 for 1d6+2, bonus-action Hide or Disengage.
contexts.tv: Show Area 2 · Goblin blind beside the fogged map. Reveal the streamside briars first; place the two goblins only when seen or when they attack.
choices: Stealth, scouting, a rush across the stream, a distraction, or retreat can all change the position of this fight.

contexts.title: Area 3 · Kennel and wolves
read: A sharp animal smell cuts through the damp cave air. Chains scrape against stone. Three pairs of eyes turn toward you from the dark, and low growls fill the cramped chamber.

The scrape of the chains marks the animals' movements more clearly than the dim light does. There is little room to spread out here, and the growling rises when attention turns toward them. You can stop at the edge of the chamber before choosing how to approach.
run: Three wolves are chained here. They cannot initially reach someone who stays back on the entrance steps, but barking can carry.
DC 15 Animal Handling calms them; food can distract them with a DC 10 check. No fight is required.

The narrow chimney to area 8 is at the back of the kennel, beyond the wolves’ normal chain reach from the entrance. Reaching it requires a plan for the wolves. Climbing calls for DC 10 Athletics; a poor fall can deal 1d6 bludgeoning damage.
Wolf: AC 13, HP 11, speed 40 ft.; bite +4 for 2d4+2 piercing, DC 11 Strength save or prone. Pack Tactics gives advantage when an ally is beside the target.
private: Do not release all three wolves just because a character steps inside. Their chains and the goblins’ reactions matter.
contexts.tv: Show Area 3 · Kennel as the characters enter or illuminate it, beside the fogged map. Place three wolf icons.

contexts.title: Area 4 · Steep passage
read: The main passage climbs steeply beside the stream. Spray darkens the stone, and loose rubble shifts underfoot. Above the noise, you can make out another passage crossing high overhead.

Water follows the slope past your boots, leaving the rising stone slick and dark. The crossing overhead is separate from the route at your feet; from here, you can judge the climb and look for movement above without knowing where either passage ends.
run: Rubble is difficult terrain. The fragile ledge collapses under more than 100 pounds; DC 10 Dexterity save, taking 2d6 bludgeoning on a failure or half on a success. Failure also knocks the creature prone.

Route at a glance: the stream climbs toward the overpass (area 5); a higher side passage west reaches Yeemik’s den (area 6); the den connects east across the bridge to the twin pools (area 7), then south to Klarg (area 8). The kennel chimney is a separate shortcut to area 8.
Noise from nearby goblins may be heard by careful listeners. Show the hazard through crumbling stone and spray before asking for a risky crossing.
contexts.tv: Show Area 4 · Steep passage beside the fogged map. Reveal the rising passage and stream gradually; the bridge should appear only when it comes into view.

contexts.title: Area 5 · Overpass and flood
read: A rickety bridge crosses the passage high above the water. A small figure shifts against the shadowed ceiling. Farther upstream, the sound of pooled water presses through the cave.

The bridge's boards and supports stand out against the rock when your light catches them. Below, the stream continues along the climbing passage. The figure above and the louder water ahead give you two different things to watch as you decide whether to advance.
run: One goblin guards the bridge about 20 feet above the stream. If it spots the party, it signals area 7; the first flood arrives on the following round on the pool goblins’ initiative count.

Telegraph a flood with a physical roar and rising water. In the surge’s path, DC 10 Dexterity save to avoid being swept away; a caught creature can try DC 15 Strength to hold on. Failure washes it toward area 1 and deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage.
The goblins at the pools can release a second surge if still able. The bridge can also break; a fall from it is dangerous.
Goblin: AC 15, HP 7, attack +4 for 1d6+2, bonus-action Hide or Disengage.
private: That second sensation is the campaign’s Echo beat. It causes no save, damage, or immediate explanation.
contexts.tv: Show Area 5 · Overpass when the party can see the bridge, beside the fogged map. Keep the guard hidden until spotted or until it signals the pools.

contexts.title: Area 6 · Yeemik and Sildar
read: A cooking fire lights an uneven cavern. Goblins look up from their meal. On a higher ledge, a battered human man is held upright by one of them. He can barely stand.
One goblin raises a hand for the others to hold. “You want the human? Then we have something to discuss.”
run: Six goblins occupy the den: Yeemik has 12 HP, and the five ordinary goblins have 7 HP each. Sildar is alive at 1 HP, unarmed, and without armor.
Yeemik wants Klarg removed. He may promise Sildar in exchange, then press for ransom rather than honoring his word. Do not force the party to accept.
If openly threatened, Yeemik can shove Sildar from the ledge; the fall deals 1d6 damage unless the party intervenes or heals him. Make his position and danger legible before the decision.
All six use goblin attacks: AC 15, +4 to hit for 1d6+2, bonus-action Hide or Disengage. Yeemik has 12 HP; each other goblin has 7 HP. Yeemik carries three gold teeth worth 1 gp each and 15 sp.
contexts.tv: Show Area 6 · Goblin den only when the den comes into view. Reveal the higher ledge and place Yeemik, five other goblins, and Sildar once visible.
choices: Talking, trickery, sneaking, rescue, retreat, and combat are all valid. The five players lead the negotiation and decide how to protect Sildar.

contexts.title: Area 7 · Twin pools
read: Two dark pools fill much of the cavern. Water presses against rough stone-and-timber dams. The waterfall’s echo makes quieter movement hard to place.

The rough barriers hold back a great deal of water, and the noise fills the space around them. You can inspect their visible supports, look for ground that stays out of the current, or study the onward route before putting someone beside a dam.
run: Three goblins guard the water controls. If warned by the bridge goblin, they can release a pool into the main passage. The water must actually be present to release.
Noise here can warn Klarg in area 8; one goblin may run to him if a fight breaks out.
Goblin: AC 15, HP 7, attack +4 for 1d6+2, bonus-action Hide or Disengage.
private: Keep the physical water hazard separate from the fleeting magical pressure. The pressure is atmosphere, not a second attack.
contexts.tv: Show Area 7 · Twin pools when seen, beside the fogged map. Place the three goblins according to how they respond to alarms.

contexts.title: Area 8 · Klarg’s cave
read: Sacks and crates fill the far side of the cave. Smoke from a low fire climbs toward an opening above. Behind the stolen supplies, a hulking figure rises, morningstar in hand, while a wolf bares its teeth.

The stacked goods divide the cavern into patches of cover and narrow sightlines. Firelight catches the raised weapon and the wolf's teeth, while smoke drifts toward the opening overhead. The way you entered remains behind you as you choose how to answer this reception.
run: Klarg the bugbear has AC 16 and 27 HP. Morningstar +4 to hit, 2d8+2 piercing. Ranged javelin +4, 1d6+2. If he surprises someone and hits in round one, add 2d6.
Ripper is a wolf: AC 13, HP 11, bite +4 for 2d4+2 and DC 11 Strength save or prone. Two goblins also fight here.
The fire pit deals 1 fire damage when entered, or 1d6 to a creature that falls prone in it. Supply piles give half cover.
If warned, Klarg and his group use the supply piles as cover. If Ripper dies, Klarg may flee down the chimney toward area 3.
Treasure: 600 cp, 110 sp, two potions of healing, and a jade frog statuette with golden eyes worth 40 gp. Returning the stolen Lionshield Coster goods in Phandalin earns 50 gp.
contexts.tv: Show Area 8 · Klarg’s cave only when the supply cave is entered. Place Klarg, Ripper the wolf, and two goblins as they become visible.
choices: Klarg is the sharpest damage spike for a level-1 PC. Give tracks, noise, or frightened goblins as warning. Reassess only after seeing the five actual character sheets.

contexts.title: 3 · Clues after the road fight
read: The woods settle. The two horses still block the road. Broken brush and small tracks lead north, away from the wagon and into thicker trees.
Among the goblins’ castoffs is a rough dark stone token. One side bears a single worn word: BELOW. The other carries part of a circle rubbed almost smooth.
run: Any inspection of the ambush area reveals the goblin trail north of the road. A DC 10 Survival check adds that about a dozen goblins used it and two human-sized captives were dragged away. Following a fleeing goblin or questioning a captive also establishes the lead.
A captive goblin knows that the dwarf and his map were sent toward Cragmaw Castle; it can lead or direct the party toward the hideout.
If they miss the BELOW token, move it to the hideout. It is optional and never required to continue.
private: The token is not Echo’s Whisper. It has no power or key function. Donavan may think its mark resembles damaged research notation but cannot solve it.
After a distant boom, anyone studying it notices it feels cooler. No roll is needed.
contexts.tv: Leave the road map up while they search, or use a black screen for a quiet conversation.
choices: If they take the wagon to Phandalin, Barthen says Gundren has not arrived and urges investigation. Bring the trail lead back through local concern rather than ending the rescue plot.

contexts.title: 3 · Sildar’s next step
read: Sildar scans the main street. “I will ask after Iarno and find us a place to gather our thoughts. We need something firmer than a rumor before we choose a road.”

The street gives him several places to begin an inquiry, but his glance does not settle on an answer. Shops, passing residents, and the possibility of a shared meeting place lie within reach. You can accompany him or agree where to find one another after making your own inquiries.
run: Sildar is looking for Iarno Albrek, a missing Lords’ Alliance member. He can help ask questions without taking the decision away from the party.
At this table, no confirmed Gundren destination was established in Session 1. If asked, describe only what Sildar actually witnessed or learned, then let the party investigate.

After lodging at Stonehill, Sildar wants to restore order and investigate both Iarno and the missing mine. He offers 500 gp if the party can locate Cragmaw Castle; this is a future reward, not a clue to its location.
Confirm his current armor and weapons before using his equipped combat statistics.
private: Play Sildar’s spoken beat only if the party talks with him. If they split up, he can seek lodging and Iarno independently; reveal what he learns when they meet again.
Published Iarno material is on pp. 14 and 18-19. His eventual identity is DM-only until discovered.
contexts.tv: Show town arrival art or keep Barthen’s exterior; keep Sildar’s private goals on the DM screen.

contexts.title: 5 · Follow the party’s town lead
run: Lionshield Coster · Linene Graywind is brisk and wary of the gang. Say: “If you have something with a blue lion mark, bring it where I can see it.” She offers 50 gp for the stolen goods from Cragmaw Hideout once returned or located.

Alderleaf Farm · Qelline is a welcoming halfling farmer. Her son Carp found a tunnel near the manor; he can guide the party to area 8. Say: “Carp came back white as a sheet, but he remembers exactly where he went.” If asked how to find Cragmaw Castle, Qelline suggests Reidoth the druid in Thundertree, who knows the surrounding land; she cannot locate the castle herself.

Edermath Orchard · Daran is a retired adventurer who wants someone to teach the Redbrands a lesson. Say: “Bullies grow bold when decent folk look away.” He can also ask the party to investigate Old Owl Well; the Order of the Gauntlet is a later opportunity.

Townmaster’s Hall · Harbin Wester is fearful and downplays the Redbrands. His posted orc task offers 100 gp for a group that deals with the threat at Wyvern Tor. Say: “The notice is there. I would rather you looked east than stirred up trouble here.”

Miner’s Exchange · Halia Thornton offers 100 gp to remove Glasstaff and bring her his correspondence. She knows the Redbrands have a goblin who may know the castle’s location; she does not know it herself. DC 15 Insight can reveal that she wants control of the gang, not merely its end.

Shrine of Luck · Sister Garaele seeks news of Bowgentle’s spellbook through the banshee Agatha. She can offer three healing potions as payment if the party takes the errand. Say: “I need someone who can ask a delicate question and return with the answer.”

Sleeping Giant · Grista runs the rough tap house where Redbrands gather. Entering can trigger the street confrontation; the party may scout, talk, or leave. Do not start initiative merely because they approach.
private: Published locations and rewards: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 16-18. Award no quest reward until its condition occurs.
contexts.tv: Use town art for conversation. Change to black screen for private or tense exchanges if helpful.
choices: Do not require every location in one session. Follow only the lead the players choose.

If they focus on Gundren, a questioned Redbrand or Iarno’s papers can establish the gang’s role and Cragmaw Castle destination. Qelline can independently point toward Reidoth; Halia can point toward the gang’s goblin. Droop knows only a broad direction, while a captured bugbear can give a more precise castle lead. Reveal only what the party actually uncovers.
If they return to Cragmaw Hideout, Yeemik is still in charge after keeping his bargain. Play the visit as a new consequence of that deal.

contexts.title: Close · What changed in Phandalin
run: Record wagon delivery and payment only if completed; NPCs met, clues heard, Sildar’s lodging and gear, Redbrand outcome, captives, and the party’s next destination.

If they entered the hideout, record the exact room and route, fog revealed, alarms, remaining enemy groups, Droop’s status, Dendrar family safety, Iarno’s location, treasure taken, and any map secrets the players actually found.
Keep Trista’s token private unless she revealed it. Record what Donavan actually learned rather than what he suspects.
If the entire Redbrand hideout was resolved, review advancement and record the actual decision before Session 3. A partial town visit does not require a new milestone.
contexts.tv: End with a town image, journal item, or black screen. Keep private clues off the TV.

contexts.title: Lead · Check on Gundren at the inn
read: The common room is busy enough that your return draws only a few glances. Somewhere beyond it is the room where you left Gundren.

The place you left him is the first thing to check, before any questions about the wider trouble. You can ask the keeper to take you there, find out who has been nearby, or arrange for someone to watch the approach. Gundren's present condition is something you must see for yourselves.
run: Gundren was left at an unnamed inn after Glasstaff put him to sleep. His present condition, the exact spell, and what he remembers have not been reported. Establish those in play. Do not name this inn Stonehill just because the adventure has an inn by that name.

First describe only the condition the DM establishes now. If awake and willing, use a simple prepared response: “Tell me what happened after he cast that spell.” If not able to talk, describe observable signs and offer care; do not read an awake-person response.

Ask about what he saw before losing consciousness, his last memory of his brothers, and the whereabouts of his map. Use the actual account when supplied. Missing testimony stays unresolved; no new mine location or recovered map is awarded by this scene.

If he can talk, answer from what Gundren could have witnessed; do not make him omniscient about Glasstaff’s later movements. Keep the mine and his brothers’ concerns separate from an unearned castle lead.
If he cannot speak yet, care, observation, and another witness are viable approaches. Record any promise or change of custody through Outcome review.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), Phandalin pp. 14–19, Redbrand Hideout pp. 20–26; actual-play record in Campaign continuity.

Rules: PHB 2014 p. 178 (Medicine) and p. 276 (Sleep); SRD 5.1 p. 180. Only if the DM confirms the 2014 Sleep spell: it lasts one minute and ends early on damage or an action to shake/slap awake. Continued unresponsiveness needs a separate established cause; do not invent a curse. Observe obvious signs without a check; use Medicine for an uncertain diagnosis, not automatic HP restoration.
contexts.tv: Use town art or the player-safe town map. The specific inn has not been confirmed.
choices: Question Gundren if able.
Arrange care or protection.
Investigate an independent source while he rests.

contexts.title: Lead · The captured rat
read: Trista has the rat you captured in the hideout. How are you keeping it, and what do you want to try?

The rat's containment is something you can check before beginning an examination. What you know so far comes from the capture, not from any explanation it has given you. You can observe it, ask Trista what help she wants, or leave the question for another meeting.
run: Trista holds the rat. The characters’ recognition of it as a familiar or anything else is unconfirmed. Do not announce a magical nature just because the DM knows Glasstaff’s setup.

Published DM baseline (LMoP p. 25): AC 10, 1 HP, speed 20 ft, no effective attacks; it remains loyal to Iarno and may feign affection if fed. This is a behavior option, not a new event. Never make it announce a destination it did not witness.

Use observed behavior, relevant magic, or an actual witness to answer specific questions. A result may remain inconclusive; a failed check is not proof of an identity. Arcana can interpret an observed magical effect, not read memories or force loyalty.

Do not treat the rat as a tracking beacon to its master. Under 2014 Find Familiar the telepathic link works within 100 ft; possession by Trista grants no control, bond, or automatic access to its senses. Owner dismissal is possible, but remains a deliberate DM event, not a forced escape.
If custody changes, use one reviewed outcome with a custody track. Private wording can go to Trista alone; broader publication requires a deliberate audience choice.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), Phandalin pp. 14–19, Redbrand Hideout pp. 20–26; actual-play record in Campaign continuity.

Rules: PHB 2014 pp. 177–178 (Arcana, Investigation, Animal Handling), p. 231 (Detect Magic), p. 240 (Find Familiar), p. 277 (Speak with Animals); SRD 5.1 pp. 134, 143, 181. A standard familiar is a celestial, fey, or fiend, not a beast; Speak with Animals therefore does not ordinarily apply. Detect Magic is not identity, memory, or destination detection: adjudicate any aura from the specific effect, without automatically revealing the master. No automatic rat combat.
contexts.tv: Keep examination notes and possible identity private. Show only the ordinary visual the party would see.
choices: Examine it in town.
Keep it contained and seek someone qualified.
Release, transfer, or refuse to investigate it; record the actual choice.

contexts.title: 3 · Clues after the road fight
read: The woods settle. The two horses still block the road. Broken brush and small tracks lead north, away from the wagon and into thicker trees.
Among the goblins’ castoffs is a rough dark stone token. One side bears a single worn word: BELOW. The other carries part of a circle rubbed almost smooth.
run: Any inspection of the ambush area reveals the goblin trail north of the road. A DC 10 Survival check adds that about a dozen goblins used it and two human-sized captives were dragged away. Following a fleeing goblin or questioning a captive also establishes the lead.
A captive goblin knows that the dwarf and his map were sent toward Cragmaw Castle; it can lead or direct the party toward the hideout.
If they miss the BELOW token, move it to the hideout. It is optional and never required to continue.
private: The token is not Echo’s Whisper. It has no power or key function. Donavan may think its mark resembles damaged research notation but cannot solve it.
After a distant boom, anyone studying it notices it feels cooler. No roll is needed.
contexts.tv: Leave the road map up while they search, or use a black screen for a quiet conversation.
choices: If they take the wagon to Phandalin, Barthen says Gundren has not arrived and urges investigation. Bring the trail lead back through local concern rather than ending the rescue plot.

contexts.title: 2 · Barthen’s Provisions
read: Warm lamplight falls over rope, trail food, tools, and stacks of ledgers. Behind the counter, a thin shopkeeper looks up. His welcoming smile falters as he counts the faces coming through the door. “Where is Gundren?”

The shelves are arranged for practical journeys rather than impressive purchases: coils of rope, provisions, and tools ready to be carried away. The counter is a place to set down goods or ask for help, and the shopkeeper waits to hear which business brought you through his door.
run: Elmar Barthen expected Gundren but has not seen him. He mentions Nundro and Tharden Rockseeker, who have also been away. He knows no confirmed location for Gundren.
If the supplies are actually delivered, pay the published 10 gp per character and record it. If the wagon is absent or damaged, talk through what arrived before deciding payment.
Barthen can point to Stonehill Inn for lodgings. If asked about danger, he says Redbrands harass local merchants and frequent the Sleeping Giant. He does not stock armor or weapons.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 16. Barthen should not magically know where Gundren was taken.
Gundren is Trista’s benefactor. Give her room to respond without announcing that relationship or her hidden token for her.
contexts.tv: Show Barthen’s art and optionally the player-safe banner “Phandalin.” No private book map.
choices: Let Pebble ask about rare stone; Barthen knows prospectors and ore, not the Echo’s secret.
Let Trista decide whether to mention the token. Donavan does not know what she hid.

contexts.title: Lead · Business with Barthen
read: Rope coils hang beside trail rations and stacks of useful things. Barthen lays down a pencil as you approach. “Tell me what you need,” he says, looking from one face to the next.

The counter offers room to set down goods or explain what brought you here. Barthen waits for your account rather than supplying one of his own. You can ask for ordinary equipment, discuss the supplies, or tell him only as much of your recent trouble as you choose.
run: Confirm what Barthen has actually heard since his last established interaction. Give only information he could know.

Published baseline (LMoP p. 16): he knows Gundren as a friend interested in the lost mine, and knows Tharden and Nundro had been camping outside town. Their present fates are not his knowledge. Redbrands frequented the Sleeping Giant; whether they still do must reflect actual survivors. He has no castle directions.
Suggested reply if told Gundren is back: “You brought him back? Tell me where he is, and what you need.” This is dialogue preparation, not an established conversation or promise.

Barthen sells ordinary adventuring gear costing no more than 25 gp per item, not weapons or armor. Direct those purchases to Lionshield Coster. Confirm stock and any prior payment before recording a transaction.
If the players ask for a rare mineral, he can point Pebble toward prospectors or trade contacts; he cannot identify the Echo or a secret site from that request.
If the shop is declined, offer normal services or a different established contact without forcing a clue.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), Phandalin pp. 14–19, Redbrand Hideout pp. 20–26; actual-play record in Campaign continuity.

Rules: PHB 2014 pp. 150–153 for adventuring gear; p. 174 for checks; DMG 2014 pp. 244–245 for social interaction. Ordinary buying and telling him observable news need no roll. Roll only when the result is uncertain and failure matters.
contexts.tv: Show the shop art after a private preview. Keep the player map on standby for directions.
choices: Complete or defer a delivery, with the payment recorded separately.
Seek a relevant town contact or prepare for travel.
Return to the inn.

contexts.title: 6 · Redbrand confrontation · optional
read: Four people in dirty red cloaks drift into your path. One plants a boot on the boardwalk. Another watches the townsfolk make room without being asked. The first says, “Visitors usually learn how things work here before asking questions.” What do you do?

Their attention gives the encounter an immediate edge, but the street still offers space to speak or withdraw. Before anyone reaches for a weapon, you can look at where the strangers stand and decide whether to answer together, keep your distance, or let one person do the talking.
run: Trigger after the party has engaged with town trouble, visits the Sleeping Giant, or investigates the manor. Do not force it immediately outside Barthen’s.
Four Redbrand Ruffians. Each has AC 14, HP 16, initiative +2, speed 30 ft.; Multiattack makes two shortsword attacks, +4 to hit for 1d6+2 piercing each. No automatic surprise.

If three are defeated, the last tries to escape toward Tresendar Manor. A captured ruffian can confirm Redbrands abducted Gundren, but rank-and-file members do not know his destination. Protect bystanders from automatic splash damage.
private: Published trigger and flight behavior: p. 19; stat block: appendix B p. 61. Four ruffians can make eight attacks per round.
Their knowledge that Redbrands abducted Gundren is custom campaign continuity. Do not announce it unless a ruffian is questioned or other evidence emerges.
contexts.tv: Only when positions matter, show the gridless, player-safe street map. Place the four ruffians when the players see them; keep the printed DM map private.
choices: The party can de-escalate, retreat, capture, or fight. If they avoid the gang, let consequences develop later.

contexts.title: 8 · Cellar and cistern · area 1
read: Old stone steps lead below the manor. The air is cool, and dark water rests in a deep cistern. Barrels and worn flagstones crowd the cellar. A narrow door leads farther in.

The cistern and the stored goods make this a working space rather than a grand entrance. Watch where the floor leaves room to move between them. You can examine the water, check the visible doors, or establish a position before continuing farther below the manor.
run: Cistern is 10 feet deep. A waterproof satchel hidden on its south wall is found by DC 15 Perception or probing. It contains a healing potion, invisibility potion, 50 gp, and ordinary travel clothes.
Loud searching can alert the three ruffians in area 2. The southwest secret door reaches the crevasse; use the secret-door checks in the manor entry beat.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 20. Do not show the secret door or satchel on TV before discovery.
contexts.tv: Reveal just the entry and cellar. Place enemies only if they enter from the barracks.

contexts.title: 9 · Redbrand barracks · area 2
read: A lamp warms this rough sleeping room. Red cloaks hang from pegs above bedrolls and discarded boots.

The bedding and personal clutter suggest repeated use rather than a room abandoned with the house above. The space between the sleeping places is worth noting before you enter. You can look over what is plainly visible or watch the exit while someone examines the room.
run: Three Redbrand ruffians. If area 1 was noisy, they prepare an ambush; check whether the party notices them before deciding surprise. Each has AC 14, HP 16, +2 initiative; two shortsword attacks at +4 for 1d6+2 piercing each.
Their belt pouches hold 16 sp and 7 gp; 12 sp and 5 gp; and 15 ep plus two garnets worth 10 gp each. Three scarlet cloaks hang here. Award only what the party actually takes.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 21; ruffian stat p. 61.
contexts.tv: Reveal the barracks as the door opens. Deploy three ruffians if they are present.

contexts.title: 10 · Hall and hidden pit · area 3
read: A dusty stone hall runs toward copper-covered double doors. Old decorative columns break up the walls.

The hall gives you a direct way forward, but its floor deserves as much attention as its far end. Dust, joins in the stone, and the places where boots might fall are visible things to inspect. You can slow the group or check the route without assuming that the way is safe.
run: The covered floor collapses beneath 100 pounds or more. DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) spots the pit and narrow side ledges. DC 10 Dexterity (Acrobatics) skirts it. A triggering creature or one that fails to skirt can catch the edge with DC 15 Dexterity save; otherwise it falls 20 feet, takes 2d6 bludgeoning, and lands prone.
Mark the hazard only when found or triggered. The book awards 100 XP for surviving or bypassing it if you use XP rather than milestones.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 21.
contexts.tv: Reveal the corridor; show the pit only after it is detected or triggered.

contexts.title: 11 · Crypt · area 4
read: Three old stone coffins stand in a dusty crypt. Human skeletons in rusted armor are propped against them, and copper-covered double doors wait at the far end.

The stonework muffles the noise from elsewhere in the hideout, making a small movement feel unusually loud. The resting places and scattered remains offer different things to examine. You can leave them undisturbed, look for names or damage, or keep watch while another person searches.
run: Three skeletons animate when a creature comes within 10 feet of the doors to areas 5 or 6, unless that creature wears a scarlet cloak or gives the password “Illefarn.” Fighting here alerts the two guards in area 5.
Each sarcophagus contains a platinum signet ring worth 50 gp. Track which are opened; this is not automatic loot.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 22; skeleton stat: Monster Manual (2014) p. 272.
contexts.tv: Reveal the crypt; deploy skeletons only when they animate.

contexts.title: 12 · Slave pens · area 5
read: Iron bars divide the chamber into cells. Two armed Redbrands stand guard. A woman and a young woman are confined to one side; a boy is held apart from them.

The bars turn the room into a place of confinement rather than ordinary storage. The doors and the space beside them matter if anyone is to leave in a hurry. You can address whoever is actually present, inspect the locks, or check the surrounding route before promising a way out.
run: Two ruffians guard Mirna Dendrar, her thirteen-year-old son Nars, and her eighteen-year-old daughter Nilsa. If they heard fighting in area 4, they prepare at the wall by the door. The family needs rescue and a safe escort.

The cell locks require DC 10 Dexterity with thieves’ tools or DC 22 Strength to force; Iarno’s or Mosk’s key opens them. Mirna knows her husband Thel was killed; his body is in area 8. Once safe, she can tell the party about the emerald necklace hidden in the ruined alchemy shop in Thundertree. Do not place captives in splash damage automatically.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 22.
contexts.tv: Reveal guards and captives only when seen. Keep their later story private until conversation.

contexts.title: 13 · Armory and storeroom · areas 6–7
read: Weapon racks line one chamber; the next smells of leather, fur, and dust. Old storage here still serves someone.

The arrangement of the stored equipment makes it possible to examine one part of the room without disturbing everything else. You can check what is within reach, look for markings, or study the exits. Anything useful still has to be inspected before you decide to carry it away.
run: Area 6 is locked from the outside. Its racks hold 12 spears, 6 shortswords, 4 longswords, 6 light crossbows, eight quivers of 20 bolts each, and 12 red cloaks.
Area 7 stores 30 beaver pelts worth 2 gp each. Its secret routes connect to the armory and Glasstaff’s quarters; use the private map for exact doors.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 22–23.
contexts.tv: Reveal only the opened room; keep the secret route out of the player view.

contexts.title: 14 · Crevasse and nothic · area 8
read: The worked stone gives way to a raw split in the earth. Two narrow bridges cross the dark gap, and the space below is difficult to make out.

The break in the cavern floor divides your approach into separate stretches of ground. Its edges and any visible crossing deserve a careful look before someone moves ahead. You can stop to judge the drop or keep to the near side while deciding what you want to investigate.
run: Carp’s hillside tunnel enters here. The nothic hides near the west ends of the bridges. It communicates telepathically and prefers food or another useful bargain to combat; it knows the same hideout information the Redbrands do.

The south bridge collapses under more than 50 pounds. DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) notices the weak construction. The fissure is 20 feet deep; a fall deals 2d6 bludgeoning and leaves the victim prone in difficult terrain.

The nothic’s chest is in a cubbyhole at the bottom of the fissure beneath the north bridge, invisible from the edge. It contains 160 sp, 120 gp, five 15 gp malachites, two healing potions, an augury scroll, and Talon, a +1 longsword. Thel Dendrar’s body lies below.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 23. Nothic: AC 15, HP 45, two +4 claws (1d6+3 each), Rotting Gaze DC 12 Con or 3d6 necrotic.
contexts.tv: Reveal the fissure, bridges, and currently visible path. Keep the hidden chest and secret routes unrevealed.

contexts.title: 15 · Bugbears and Droop · area 9
read: Three large figures occupy the room as though it belongs to them. A goblin nearby flinches at your arrival and looks ready to disappear into the floor.

The room's sleeping places and the positions of those inside shape the space available for an approach. You have a moment to note who watches you, who avoids your gaze, and where the door sits behind you. Words are still an option before the first movement becomes an attack.
run: Three bugbears sent by the Black Spider. Droop faints when he sees the party; he remains unconscious for 1d10 minutes unless awakened. He hides if fighting starts and is not an automatic attacker.

Each bugbear has AC 16, HP 27, +4 morningstar for 2d8+2 piercing; Surprise Attack adds 2d6 on a hit against a creature it surprised in the first round. Use the five current level-3 sheets and live HP/resources when assessing risk; make retreat and bluffing possible.

Scarlet cloaks can persuade the bugbears that the characters serve Iarno; a plausible deception can use DC 15 Charisma (Deception). Droop can describe the hideout and broad northern forest direction of Cragmaw Castle, but not the route. A captured bugbear can disclose the castle’s location on a DC 15 Charisma (Intimidation) check.
Mosk carries 33 sp, a jeweled eye patch worth 50 gp, and a key that opens every locked door in the hideout.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 24; bugbear stat p. 56. Do not invent a precise castle route.
contexts.tv: Reveal the room and three bugbears when seen. Keep Droop’s allegiance ambiguous until he reacts.

contexts.title: 16 · Common room · area 10
read: Dice clatter across a scarred table. Four red-cloaked figures sit around a game, cups and coins at their elbows.

The tables and scattered possessions make this a room people spend time in, not simply a passage to somewhere else. You can take in the faces and the gaps between the furniture before answering. Whether you listen, bluff, or confront them, their reactions are something you can actually observe.
run: Four ruffians are drinking and gambling. All four have the poisoned condition from drink: disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks. They are automatically surprised if the party bursts into the room; if the approach is slower, adjudicate what they notice.

Characters in red cloaks may bluff as new recruits with a DC 10 Charisma (Deception) check, especially if they join the game. The table holds 75 cp, 55 sp, 22 ep, 15 gp, and a ruby-set gold earring worth 30 gp.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 24.
contexts.tv: Reveal the common room and four ruffians only when the party opens the way.

contexts.title: 17 · Wizard’s workshop · area 11
read: Glassware, notes, and pungent powders cover the benches.

The worktable, shelves, and unfamiliar apparatus offer several separate lines of inquiry. You can examine the written material without assuming what the equipment does, or look over the apparatus without touching it. The ordinary routes through the room remain worth keeping clear while you investigate.
run: Latest actual play overrides the first-entry setup: the party captured the rat. Keep its current custody; do not put a second rat in this room. Its familiar nature remains DM-only unless the party learned it.
In the printed first-entry setup, the rat is Iarno’s familiar and warns him telepathically as soon as it detects intruders. It has AC 10, 1 HP, speed 20 feet, and no effective attack.

The apparatus appears intended to brew invisibility potions, but Iarno has not succeeded. A Dwarvish tome describes the lost mine and Lightbringer. Three reagents—mercury, dragon bile, and powdered nightshade—are worth 25 gp each. Track what is read and taken.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 25.
contexts.tv: Reveal the workshop when entered. Do not announce the rat’s link to Glasstaff.

contexts.title: 18 · Glasstaff’s quarters · area 12
read: A better-appointed room sits beyond the rougher hideout. Papers lie beside a travel chest. Someone has been planning from here.

The desk and chest suggest different sorts of business: work done in the open and possessions kept close. You can examine what is visible, listen toward the adjoining spaces, or check the way you came. Nothing here tells you what happened after someone left without further evidence.
run: Latest actual play overrides this prepared confrontation: Glasstaff put Gundren to sleep and escaped to Cragmaw Castle; the party left Gundren at an unnamed inn and Trista holds Glasstaff’s rat. Play stopped at Barthen’s Provisions. Do not redeploy Glasstaff here, restart the fight, or present Gundren as a castle hostage. The castle destination is DM-only until discovered.
For unresolved room contents, inspect the saved scene and what the party actually took before using the printed first-entry setup below.

Iarno Albrek is Glasstaff. In the printed first-entry setup, a warning from the rat lets him flee by the secret route through areas 7, 8, and 1. Those steps are reference behavior, not a replay of the completed escape.
Evil Mage base: AC 12, HP 22, speed 30, spell save DC 13, spell attack +5. Slots: 1st level 4, 2nd level 3. Magic missile, charm person, hold person, misty step, shocking grasp, light, mage hand.

Staff of defense: +1 AC while held; 10 charges. Its printed entry spends 1 charge to cast mage armor or 2 to cast shield, using an action. Mage armor plus Dexterity and held staff makes Iarno AC 16. Track charges. Check the item entry before a shield ruling.

A search may find the Black Spider letter and an unlocked chest: 180 sp, 130 gp, five carnelians (10 gp each), two peridots (15 gp each), and one pearl (100 gp). Check what Glasstaff took and what the party found before awarding any of it.

A custom Redbrand transfer record in Iarno’s desk names Gundren Rockseeker and Cragmaw Castle. If found, it documents an earlier transfer, not Gundren’s current location. Do not treat it as discovered unless the party actually searched the desk.
Iarno knows the Spider seeks the Forge but not the cave’s location. Confirm other knowledge against actual play before giving an answer.
private: Describe Iarno and his staff only if he is still present. If he escaped, remove the scrolls from the chest and keep the staff with him.
Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 25–26; Evil Mage appendix p. 57; staff of defense appendix A p. 53.
contexts.tv: Reveal the quarters on entry. Place Iarno only if he remains; keep the Black Spider letter private until found.

contexts.title: Departure · an agreed road and a way back
read: At the edge of town, the road looks ordinary again. Packs settle, straps tighten, and the first turn waits for a choice. Behind you are people who know your names. Ahead is a city where introductions still matter.

The last familiar roofs offer a final point from which to check your direction. You can name a meeting place and the first planned stop before the road separates you from the town. A departure leaves room for messages to follow.
run: Custom default itinerary: the known road from Phandalin to the Triboar Trail, then west to the High Road and south toward Waterdeep. Confirm actual road conditions and stops before accepting it. Neverwinter or an inland Amphail visit is a deliberate detour, not a stop silently inserted into every journey.
Define route segments and distances in the existing travel planner before quoting a numeric ETA. The painting is approximate; this pack does not supply an invented total mileage or travel duration.
Agree foot, mount, wagon or a contracted caravan, pace, provisions, weather, watch plan and named stops. Vessel travel requires arranging a real departure port and passage separately.
Review responsibility for dependents, prisoners and discoveries. A caravan leader agrees any escort or guarded cargo explicitly.
Pebble may make a route mark or sketch with the group’s help. Donavan may prepare a letter; Ringgo may review terms; Trista and Aldric decide what travels privately.
Make a restore point. Begin the journey only after the table chooses it; no sheets, travel clocks or towns change merely from staging this card.
private: Original Echo Below scene and dialogue; future preparation, not an event that has happened.
Regional route is a custom itinerary using known roads, not a surveyed distance. No mandatory random fight.
contexts.tv: Use the known frontier map for the first leg only. It does not map the complete road to Waterdeep; keep unknown regional markers concealed.
choices: Travel independently by an agreed route.
Negotiate a place with a caravan.
Return to preparations or delay departure.

Optional audio cues: recorded-journey. Preview before playing.

contexts.title: Before play · carry forward what actually happened
run: If play stopped mid-hideout or mid-combat, continue the existing saved session. Do not reset fog, enemies, or token positions.
Session 1 remains fixed: Klarg died, Yeemik kept the hideout, Sildar was rescued, and Trista privately took the BELOW token. Donavan noticed concealment, not the object.

Latest actual play: Glasstaff put Gundren to sleep; the party recovered him and left him at an unnamed inn. Glasstaff escaped to Cragmaw Castle, but the party does not know his destination. Trista holds his captured rat. Play stopped at Barthen’s Provisions. Do not place Gundren or the rat at the castle.

Current confirmed levels: Trista, Pebble, and Ringgo are level 4; Donavan and Aldric are level 3. Check the saved HP, resources, and any newer sheet before combat. Scouting, retreat, and negotiation remain meaningful.
private: Sources: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 27 and 35–41; Session 1 actual recap and the recorded Session 2 outcome.
contexts.tv: Keep the town map or a neutral title on the TV while you reconcile the last session.

contexts.title: 1 · Choose the lead, not the destination
read: You have stopped at Barthen’s Provisions. Gundren is at an inn, and Trista has the rat you captured. Glasstaff escaped. What do you do next?

The shop doorway is close at hand, while the inn and the rest of town remain separate places to visit. You can settle ordinary business first, check on the companion you left behind, or give Trista room to decide what to do with her captive. The next step belongs to you.
run: The party stopped at Barthen’s Provisions; do not assume they entered or completed a delivery. If they return to the inn, confirm whether Gundren can speak and what they ask him; do not invent what he knows. If Iarno’s transfer record was actually found, it documents an earlier castle transfer, not Gundren’s present location. A captured Redbrand may establish the gang’s role without knowing Glasstaff’s route.
Qelline can suggest Reidoth near Thundertree; Halia knows the gang has a goblin with a castle lead; a captured bugbear can give a more precise lead. Agatha can answer one carefully chosen question.
If no castle lead was earned, offer a real inquiry, tracks, or an NPC the party already trusts. Never narrate the hidden destination as common knowledge.
private: The transfer record is an Echo Below campaign addition, not printed treasure. Source: adventure pp. 14–18, 27–29.
contexts.tv: Show the player-safe Phandalin map. Publish only leads the characters heard.
choices: If the castle route is earned, let the party plan travel and scouting.
If the castle route is unknown, play a chosen inquiry without revealing Glasstaff’s destination.
Another quest chosen: use the linked location scene and return to this decision when they have new evidence.

contexts.title: Close · Record the trail to the mine
run: Gundren was left at an inn and Trista holds the rat. Record his condition and safety, Glasstaff’s next observed move, and whether the party actually learned the castle route. Record the mine map’s custody separately and keep each room left unresolved.
If Gundren later chooses to make the printed offer, it is 25 gp each and a 10-percent share of a working mine. Treat it as his offer, not immediate cash or a guaranteed future.
Record XP or milestone only for accomplished events. Track healing potions, scrolls, Sildar’s gear, alarms, allies, and any Castle survivors.
Keep Trista’s BELOW token private unless she reveals it. Do not make the mine map explain the Echo mystery by itself.
private: Adventure p. 41. Session 3 outcomes must be entered after actual play, not prewritten as history.
contexts.tv: Return to the town map or a calm scene. Publish only facts the party witnessed.
choices: If the castle remains active, keep this session save for next play.
If the map is secured, the next pack is Wave Echo Cave after rest and player choice.

contexts.title: Before play · reconcile the journey to the mine
run: Trista, Pebble, Donavan, Ringgo, and Aldric currently have level-3 records. The printed mine assumes at least level 4 (2,700 XP if using XP). Opening this chapter does not level anyone up. Review earned progress before departure; if they enter at level 3, make danger and withdrawal clear.
If play ended inside an unfinished encounter, resume its existing save. Do not replace live positions, dead enemies, expended loot, or fog with a fresh chapter.

Carry forward confirmed play: Klarg died; Yeemik kept Cragmaw Hideout; Sildar was rescued; the orc camp was cleared; Hamun Kost disappeared. The latest Redbrand session left Gundren at an unnamed inn after Glasstaff put him to sleep, Trista holding the captured rat, and the party at Barthen’s Provisions. Gundren’s current condition still needs confirmation.

DM-only: Glasstaff escaped to Cragmaw Castle; the party has not learned that destination. Gundren is not a castle hostage. Trista’s BELOW token remains private unless she has since shared it; Donavan noticed concealment, not its identity.

Make a restore point, select the Wave Echo Cave chapter, check TV/phones/audio, and stage only the current room. Open Story → Wave Echo journal to record room outcomes, enemies, treasure, rests, and deadlines. This pack can span several evenings.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 42: recommended level. Session 1 outcomes and the Redbrand transfer are recorded campaign continuity; later events must come from the DM. The marked p. 43 map is DM-only.
contexts.tv: Keep a neutral town or journey map on TV. The mine location, prisoner, and final villain stay private until learned.

contexts.title: Phandalin · choose the homecoming that happened
read: Phandalin’s roofs appear beyond the fields. Someone by the road looks up, recognizes you, and hurries toward town. By the time you reach the first houses, people are waiting to hear what happened.

The places you recognize offer somewhere to begin your account, but the people who hear it will need your words. You can tell them what you witnessed, ask what changed during your absence, or settle a practical need before deciding what comes after the expedition.
run: If Gundren and Nundro live and the mine is reclaimed: play their reunion and a sober remembrance of Tharden. They can resume stewardship and offer the party a 10 percent share of future mine profits, as printed. This is a share when profits exist, not a chest of immediate gold.
If Nundro is rescued but the mine remains dangerous: let the family thank the party, provide care, and ask what practical support is needed for the return. Do not announce the mine reopened.

If only one brother lives: give that survivor the news and let the party choose memorial, protection, and next steps. Any changed management or profit agreement is a new recorded arrangement, not an automatic duplicate of the printed ending.
If both brothers died or neither returned: focus on telling the truth, returning identified possessions, and settling custody of the mine. No Rockseeker can grant a reward from beyond the grave.
If Nezznar escaped or a bargain continues: Sildar asks for the last verified sighting and terms. Let townsfolk respond to evidence rather than declaring the threat ended.
If Redbrands or Iarno remain active from earlier play, reflect that in town. Barthen, the Lionshield, rescued families, and other NPCs react only to their actual deliveries, rescues, and promises.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 51 gives the successful conclusion. The conditional loss, partial success, and escaped-villain scenes are original adaptations to actual play.
contexts.tv: Stage the neutral town map first. Use the celebratory homecoming art only if the outcome and mood support it.
choices: Public success: invite the players to describe a small celebration.
Mixed outcome: gratitude, mourning, and practical help can share the same scene.
Unfinished expedition: end on the party’s chosen plan to return.

contexts.title: Phandalin · a living Black Spider in custody
read: The cell door closes. For the first time, the Spider’s reach is measured in a few feet of stone. Outside, questions arrive faster than the guards can answer them.

The cell's closed door places a boundary between the prisoner and everyone outside. Questions can wait long enough to decide who stands watch and who speaks. Whatever answer Nezznar offers will still need to be weighed against what you have actually seen.
run: Run this branch only if Nezznar was captured alive and delivered. Sildar or the townmaster can hold him for the Lords’ Alliance escort to Neverwinter.
Record seized equipment, any spellcasting precautions actually taken, the key, guard shifts, witnesses, and who is informed. Use the character’s actual remaining abilities if an escape is attempted.

The adventure gives Halia a secret plan to extract an unguarded Nezznar for the Zhentarim. If the party posts guards, their preparation matters; if they do not, establish the opportunity and later evidence rather than narrating an unavoidable cutscene.

Nezznar can answer questions about his operation, but promises and accusations require corroboration. He cannot supply invented authoritative answers about the BELOW token, Halaster, or Aldric’s resurrection.
Count the printed doubled XP value only once for living delivery. An attempted later jailbreak does not duplicate that award.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 50. Guard procedures and investigative clues are original staging of the published custody consequence.
contexts.tv: Keep a neutral town scene. Private negotiations and planned jailbreaks stay on the DM screen.

contexts.title: After the mine · level 5 and the next chosen road
run: The printed adventure expects the heroes to reach level 5 by its end. Confirm XP or milestone progress and each character’s choices; do not edit all five sheets just because this card opens.

For level 5 and beyond, re-evaluate encounter guidance with the real party levels, numbers, resources, objectives, and terrain. Extra Attack and 3rd-level spells can change a fight sharply; a CR label alone is insufficient.

Use the expanded encounter guidance as advice, with the correct 2014 source profile. Do not increase every old enemy’s HP to erase the party’s progress; add an established objective, environment, or new opposition when the story supports it.

Optional custom continuations: Mormesk’s sewn map can lead to an agreed new dungeon; Dracuseth remains a Waterdeep contact; surviving enemies have unfinished plans. Decide which lead is real before publishing it.

Offer one personal beat each: Trista chooses whether to share the token; Pebble can seek his hammer-makers or a verified mineral lead; Donavan can test a research claim; Ringgo can reconnect with a contact; Aldric can seek evidence about his past. None is a forced secret revelation.
Close with the players’ chosen destination and a short list of unresolved facts. Preserve the finished mine as a place they can revisit.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 47 and 51: future-map hook and level-5 conclusion. Waterdeep, Dracuseth, character beats, and Echo continuations are original campaign additions. Encounter estimates do not guarantee fairness.
contexts.tv: Show only leads the players earned and agree to pursue. Do not display an undiscovered nine-site or Undermountain route.

contexts.title: Optional · Redbrand aftermath and witnesses
read: The town has not forgotten the gang. A few people watch the street carefully, and the manor stands apart from the ordinary bustle. Where do you look first?

The manor is a landmark, not an account of what remains inside it. People who were actually present may have different parts of the story. You can choose a particular witness, return along a known approach, or turn toward another town matter without settling the gang's future here and now.
run: Glasstaff escaped. Do not place him back in the hideout. His Cragmaw Castle destination is DM-only until a witness or evidence establishes it for the party.

For a return, use the existing hideout expedition’s Preview return, or select the previously played hideout session and reconcile current party resources before play. The new aftermath board is not a copy of the old fog, tokens, or occupants. Do not create a fresh Session 2 encounter pack or interpret an empty new board as cleared rooms.

Ask the DM to reconcile prisoners, treasure, and searched rooms before presenting any related fact. Reuse its saved doors, traps, containers, inhabitants, and fog; unexplained repopulation is not an outcome.

Clue menu, only if reached: an actual surviving witness can describe what they saw; the published Black Spider letter (p. 26) connects Iarno to the Spider and demands dwarven maps, but does not name Cragmaw Castle. The custom transfer record, if still present and actually found, concerns Gundren’s earlier transfer, not Glasstaff’s present route or Gundren’s current location.

For independent route-finding, Qelline can suggest Reidoth in Thundertree (p. 18). A surviving Droop offers limited directions (p. 24); interrogated Cragmaw goblins or Reidoth provide their own earned route evidence (pp. 28, 32). Survival, contact, cooperation, and discovery are prerequisites, not assumed events. Do not tell the party Glasstaff is there merely because they learn a castle route.

If a source is absent, unsearched, uncooperative, or inconclusive, say what remains unknown and offer another established contact, town business, care for Gundren, or a pause to rest. No failed check must force a destination or a fight.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), Phandalin pp. 14–19, Redbrand Hideout pp. 20–26; actual-play record in Campaign continuity.

Rules: PHB 2014 pp. 177–178 for investigation, perception and survival; DMG pp. 244–245 for social interaction. State the question and consequence before choosing a check. A castle route and Glasstaff’s whereabouts are separate discoveries.

If a new Redbrand confrontation actually occurs: use the existing Redbrand Ruffian card (AC 14, HP 16, Multiattack: two shortswords +4 for 1d6+2 piercing each; LMoP p. 61). Set number and positions from the fiction; do not respawn defeated foes. Negotiation and retreat remain available.
contexts.tv: Use the player-safe town map. Show the hideout only if they actually return, with its saved fog and occupants.
choices: Question someone who was actually present.
Return to an unresolved room in the saved hideout.
Move on and let the unresolved threat develop as a future branch.

contexts.title: Close · Record the actual changes
run: Open Outcome review. Record each distinct event with its source, who knows it, exact player-safe wording, quest step, custody, and optional map marker. Preview all linked changes before applying.
A route to Cragmaw Castle can be revealed only from a factual, party-known discovery. The private escape destination alone never publishes it.
Use the approved-event recap draft for the next opening; do not convert this runbook into history.
private: Use the existing undo and correction controls for mistakes. No unplayed branch should complete a quest.
contexts.tv: Leave the current visual in place; the closing review is DM-only.

contexts.title: Before the transition · decide what is actually known
run: Latest confirmed play leaves Gundren at an unnamed inn after Glasstaff put him to sleep; Trista holds the captured rat, Glasstaff escaped, and the party stopped at Barthen’s Provisions. Gundren’s present condition is unreported. All scenes in this pack are future branches until played; opening this pack never completes Phandelver.
Review approved outcomes for Gundren, Nundro, Nezznar, the mine, prisoners, promises and custody. Link evidence for each selected branch. Leave unknown answers unknown.

Use the homecoming appropriate to the actual return: complete success, a mixed result, unresolved expedition, or a visit for aid. Review Sildar, Iarno, Redbrands and other returning NPCs individually.
Select at most two of the four city leads to present now. Keep the others available if the party declines or cannot use one.
Recheck current character resources, real level and carried items through existing sheets. No rewards, rests, inventory transfers or elapsed days occur from staging scenes.
private: Original Echo Below scene and dialogue; future preparation, not an event that has happened.

Latest approved campaign outline supersedes older automatic Forge attention or instant medallion revelations. Only an actual relevant interaction can justify Halaster noticing remotely; this pack reveals none of that.
contexts.tv: Keep the current player display or a known town view. This preparation card is private.
choices: Continue Phandelver using its current saved state.
Prepare a conditional future return.
Run an actual return once its outcomes are approved.

source.note: Printed page; verified against the existing Wave Echo runbook.

contexts.title: Phandalin homecoming · the account before the celebration
read: The familiar roofs appear beyond the fields. A worker rests both hands on a fence and watches your approach. By the time you reach the first houses, the question has traveled ahead of you: what news have you brought?

The houses are familiar; the news you carry is not. There is space to pause before answering the first question. You can choose whose names should be spoken here and which matters deserve a quieter room.
run: Let the first available familiar resident ask for the party’s account. Use Barthen if available; use another established contact if not. Their aim is practical certainty about people, supplies and danger.

Use the chosen outcome responses without reading every possible branch. A reunion requires both people alive, present and willing; a memorial requires confirmed loss; a celebration requires a reason the town actually knows.
A successful mine claim still needs a safety and stewardship discussion. A partial return can include gratitude for someone saved and a request for help with someone still missing.
Give every player one invitation: something they say, something they keep private, or someone they seek. Passing is a valid answer.
Capture the public account as a draft recap. Do not include the private token, the castle destination before learned, or future Waterdeep theories.
private: Original Echo Below scene and dialogue; future preparation, not an event that has happened.
Existing homecoming art may imply success; a neutral town map works for every result.
contexts.tv: Start with the known Phandalin map. The celebratory lmop-phandalin-homecoming illustration is optional only after the actual mood fits.
choices: Public report at a familiar gathering place.
Separate private visits with affected people.

run: Reidoth can identify the castle’s location, but the village is a separate, larger adventure site. Do not imply the party must clear it to earn his help.

contexts.title: Waterdeep arrival
contexts.read:
The road gives way to streets that seem to have no end. Bells sound somewhere above the rooftops; below them, carts, voices and footsteps press onward. For the first time in days, the question is not where you can go, but where you want to belong.

The press of the streets gives you practical choices immediately: where to keep together, where to stop, and whom to ask for directions. Bells and calls overlap above the rolling carts. There is time to choose your first destination rather than let the crowd choose it for you.
contexts.run: Ask each player one thing they seek in the city. Confirm the actual Phandalin ending, Gundren/Nundro, promises and artifact custody; do not award Echo’s Whisper unless play did. Offer lodging, research, paid work or the well; none compulsory.

contexts.title: Waterdeep · choose a first destination

A porter lifts a parcel above the crowd and shouts an address as if everyone in the world ought to know it. For the first time in days, the route has more turns than the map can conveniently explain.

The shouted address rises over wheels and foot traffic, then disappears into the next call. You can stop clear of the busiest flow and choose a landmark before following a street. Asking directions remains an option even with a map in hand.
run: Let ordinary porters and shopkeepers have ordinary goals: finish work, give directions, charge agreed service prices. They do not recognize secret discoveries or demand a campaign confession.

contexts.title: Mending Court · a doorway they can choose
read: A passage opens into a small court shared by several doorways. Washing moves above a well. A covered table bears a repair someone has not finished, and the space smells faintly of paste, wood and somebody’s supper. Dracuseth pauses at the entrance. “People live here. See if you would like to be among them.”

The well, shared passage, and unfinished repair make the court a working home before it is anyone's opportunity. Several doors open onto the same space. You can ask about access, quiet, and lodging without assuming a room has been set aside for you.
run: Mending Court is the approved proposed name for this custom neighborhood, within walking distance of the Portal. Keep exact street and ward open until placed deliberately; it is not automatically Trollskull Manor.

Dracuseth provides the introduction. A responsible local lessor must agree any rental; he does not own the party’s home. Establish rooms, occupancy, rent/deposit, locks, storage, access and notice before moving anyone or money.
Use ordinary terms chosen at the table, reviewed against existing prices if wanted. The campaign has not already awarded a property or paid a deposit.
Introduce only Nessa Brindle and Orenna Pike now. Nessa wants steady bookbinding orders and time for an apprentice; Orenna wants deliveries and passage kept workable.
Let the party inspect and refuse. They can rent temporarily, use it as a contact address by agreement, stay at the Portal, or seek somewhere else.
Do not introduce supernatural anomalies on arrival. Establish ordinary geography, boundaries and relationships first.
private: Original Echo Below scene and dialogue; future preparation, not an event that has happened.
Nessa, Orenna, Jori/Pellan and Aven are independent people. They are not replacements for Halaster’s family or secretly agents by default.

The press is heavy enough that its position affects everyone passing through. Both neighbors have a need that can be heard before a solution is offered. There is room to help, suggest a different place, or simply introduce yourselves.
run: This is an ordinary collaborative task, not a test of worthiness. Nessa needs the press moved safely into a prepared work area; Orenna wants access wide enough for deliveries and anyone needing assistance.

contexts.title: 1 · Outside Barthen’s Provisions
read: The road ends in a street of packed earth and old stone. A trading house stands ahead, its doorway busy with local customers. Sildar slows beside you and studies the town as if trying to remember the face of an old friend. Gundren should have been here before you. He is not. What do you do?

The trading house offers an obvious place to ask questions or settle the delivery, while the street leaves you free to keep walking. Its traffic is ordinary enough that you can watch the doorway, approach together, or decide who will speak before going inside.
run: Pause for player decisions. Do not resolve the delivery until the party actually presents the supplies to Barthen.
contexts.tv: Keep the shop exterior on the TV. No battle map is needed for the opening conversation.
choices: They may speak to Barthen, seek the inn, split up, or ask Sildar for his plan. Follow the choice.

contexts.title: Opening · Barthen’s Provisions
read: The noise of Phandalin follows you to Barthen’s door: cart wheels on packed earth, a hammer somewhere farther down the street, and voices turning toward the day’s business. Gundren is at an inn behind you. Glasstaff is gone. The shop is here in front of you. What do you do?

The shop's threshold is close enough to cross, but you have not yet chosen to enter. You can begin with town business, turn back toward the inn, or stop to discuss the rat in Trista's care. For now, the street leaves each of those choices open.
run: The party stopped here; entry, delivery, payment, and a conversation with Barthen are unconfirmed. Ask before treating any of them as done.
Barthen wants the delivery settled and the Rockseeker brothers safe. He knows ordinary town business and the established published leads; he does not know Glasstaff’s escape destination.
If the actual goods are delivered, use the published 10 gp per character only after confirming the delivery and recording payment. Do not duplicate an earlier payment.

contexts.title: 4 · Stonehill Inn and rumors
read: The inn is warmer and louder than the street. Supper, wet cloaks, and low conversation crowd the common room. Several people glance toward your travel-worn gear. A child at one table stops talking mid-sentence.

Tables and travel-worn clothing break up the room, leaving conversations close enough to approach without addressing everyone at once. The child's sudden quiet is one detail among several. You can choose a seat, seek the keeper, or listen before deciding whose story you want to hear.

contexts.title: Around the table · people, promises and custody
read: A cleared table fills with the things a journey leaves behind: a folded message, a borrowed tool, a list of names. Outside, ordinary work continues. Here, you have time to decide what must happen before another road is taken.

Each object on the table points toward someone who may still be waiting. The tool can be returned, the message answered, and the list checked against your own account. None of those tasks has to be buried beneath a new destination.
run: Invite only NPCs actually available and allowed to hear this discussion. A host wants rooms and promises settled; a mine representative wants realistic access; a caregiver wants an accepted handover.

contexts.title: 5 · Follow the party’s town lead
run: Lionshield Coster · Linene Graywind is brisk and wary of the gang. Say: “If you have something with a blue lion mark, bring it where I can see it.” She offers 50 gp for the stolen goods from Cragmaw Hideout once returned or located.

Alderleaf Farm · Qelline is a welcoming halfling farmer. Her son Carp found a tunnel near the manor; he can guide the party to area 8. Say: “Carp came back white as a sheet, but he remembers exactly where he went.” If asked how to find Cragmaw Castle, Qelline suggests Reidoth the druid in Thundertree, who knows the surrounding land; she cannot locate the castle herself.

Edermath Orchard · Daran is a retired adventurer who wants someone to teach the Redbrands a lesson. Say: “Bullies grow bold when decent folk look away.” He can also ask the party to investigate Old Owl Well; the Order of the Gauntlet is a later opportunity.

Townmaster’s Hall · Harbin Wester is fearful and downplays the Redbrands. His posted orc task offers 100 gp for a group that deals with the threat at Wyvern Tor. Say: “The notice is there. I would rather you looked east than stirred up trouble here.”

Miner’s Exchange · Halia Thornton offers 100 gp to remove Glasstaff and bring her his correspondence. She knows the Redbrands have a goblin who may know the castle’s location; she does not know it herself. DC 15 Insight can reveal that she wants control of the gang, not merely its end.

Shrine of Luck · Sister Garaele seeks news of Bowgentle’s spellbook through the banshee Agatha. She can offer three healing potions as payment if the party takes the errand. Say: “I need someone who can ask a delicate question and return with the answer.”

Sleeping Giant · Grista runs the rough tap house where Redbrands gather. Entering can trigger the street confrontation; the party may scout, talk, or leave. Do not start initiative merely because they approach.
private: Published locations and rewards: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 16-18. Award no quest reward until its condition occurs.
contexts.tv: Use town art for conversation. Change to black screen for private or tense exchanges if helpful.
choices: Do not require every location in one session. Follow only the lead the players choose.

If they focus on Gundren, a questioned Redbrand or Iarno’s papers can establish the gang’s role and Cragmaw Castle destination. Qelline can independently point toward Reidoth; Halia can point toward the gang’s goblin. Droop knows only a broad direction, while a captured bugbear can give a more precise castle lead. Reveal only what the party actually uncovers.
If they return to Cragmaw Hideout, Yeemik is still in charge after keeping his bargain. Play the visit as a new consequence of that deal.

catalog.title: Redbrand confrontation
catalog.reveal: After the ruffians confront the party

contexts.title: 6 · Redbrand confrontation · optional
read: Four people in dirty red cloaks drift into your path. One plants a boot on the boardwalk. Another watches the townsfolk make room without being asked. The first says, “Visitors usually learn how things work here before asking questions.” What do you do?

Their attention gives the encounter an immediate edge, but the street still offers space to speak or withdraw. Before anyone reaches for a weapon, you can look at where the strangers stand and decide whether to answer together, keep your distance, or let one person do the talking.
run: Trigger after the party has engaged with town trouble, visits the Sleeping Giant, or investigates the manor. Do not force it immediately outside Barthen’s.
Four Redbrand Ruffians. Each has AC 14, HP 16, initiative +2, speed 30 ft.; Multiattack makes two shortsword attacks, +4 to hit for 1d6+2 piercing each. No automatic surprise.

If three are defeated, the last tries to escape toward Tresendar Manor. A captured ruffian can confirm Redbrands abducted Gundren, but rank-and-file members do not know his destination. Protect bystanders from automatic splash damage.
private: Published trigger and flight behavior: p. 19; stat block: appendix B p. 61. Four ruffians can make eight attacks per round.
Their knowledge that Redbrands abducted Gundren is custom campaign continuity. Do not announce it unless a ruffian is questioned or other evidence emerges.
contexts.tv: Only when positions matter, show the gridless, player-safe street map. Place the four ruffians when the players see them; keep the printed DM map private.
choices: The party can de-escalate, retreat, capture, or fight. If they avoid the gang, let consequences develop later.

contexts.title: 7 · If they reach Tresendar Manor
run: The printed Redbrand Hideout starts on p. 20. Use the private marked map for exact room positions. The TV map is an unmarked tactical aid, not a copy of the keyed plan.

Manor cellar reaches area 1. Carp’s tunnel reaches area 8. Oil lamps light most rooms; see the book for each exception. Most doors are unlocked: DC 10 thieves’ tools to pick a lock, DC 20 Strength to break a locked door.
A secret door is noticed with passive Perception 15 within 10 feet, or with an active DC 10 Perception check. Ask how the characters search rather than revealing hidden routes automatically.
private: No marked Phandalin or hideout map goes on the player TV.
contexts.tv: Keep the marked hideout map on the DM display. Switch to the unmarked hideout map with fog when the party enters; reveal only explored space.
