contexts.title: Nezznar · bargain, battle, escape, or capture
read: The dark elf rests one hand on a spider-carved staff. “You have cost me people, time, and secrecy. Before either of us wastes more, tell me what you believe you came here to claim.”

The words being exchanged do not settle what either side will accept. You can hold your position, ask for a specific answer, or make your own terms clear. The chamber and the route behind you remain part of the conversation, even if nobody chooses to mention them.
run: Printed motive: Nezznar wants the Forge and the mine’s secret. He admits being the Black Spider and using both the Cragmaws and Redbrands. In this campaign the Redbrands made Gundren’s capture and castle delivery; do not revert to a goblin-abduction account.

Printed approach: he asks about identities, loyalties, goals, and interests; offers surrender or joint action against the guardians; and intends betrayal once others cease being useful. An offer is not automatically accepted or believed. Let Insight examine a specific claim, and let concrete safeguards matter.

Tactical plan: let webs and actual bodyguards screen him; use cover and the spells on his card. Invisibility, darkness, staff web, and spider climb compete for concentration. Casting an attack or another spell ends ordinary invisibility as its rules specify. Spend slots, staff charges, and the healing potion visibly on the DM record.

Optional DM escape plan: if the fight is lost and a real route is open, attempt withdrawal using remaining resources and normal turns. Announce a visible retreat cue when observable; track destination, pursuit, and stolen items. No automatic teleport, replenished spells, or guaranteed survival.

Capture: decide custody, searches, staff/key removal, bindings, guard shifts, and escort. The printed alive-delivery award is double Nezznar’s XP value total, not his normal XP plus a second double award.

Printed Phandalin consequence: unless the party posts guards, Halia arranges his escape to the Zhentarim before the Lords’ Alliance escort. Stage her actual opportunity; record precautions and let intervention prevent it. If Nezznar dies or escaped earlier, this custody branch does not occur.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 49–50. Original dialogue and optional escape procedure. Nezznar has no printed connection to Halaster or the custom Echo, and cannot reveal those as established facts.
contexts.tv: Keep negotiations on the current map; never show DM tactics or the false hostage’s true identity.
choices: Captured: record who holds him and go to the custody/homecoming card.
Killed: preserve the body, clues, and actual loot; other threats remain.
Escaped: record last seen route, HP, resources, followers, and what he knows.
Temporary bargain: write exact terms, collateral, and who observed them; treat future betrayal as an event to play.

rows.title: Wave Echo Cave · Area 20 · Priests’ quarters

contexts.title: Area 20 · Rescue Nundro
read: Beyond the locked door, faded cloth hangs above a simple bed. A dwarf lies bound on the cold floor. His breathing is faint but steady.

You can take stock from the threshold before approaching what lies within. The visible condition of any person here and the space around them matter more than guessing what happened out of sight. You can offer help, ask a question, or check the way out before moving someone.
run: The door is locked: thieves’ tools and DC 15 Dexterity, or Nezznar’s anvil-headed key. Noisy activity here draws area 19’s attention if those enemies still can respond; Nezznar sends spiders to investigate.

The prisoner is Nundro, youngest Rockseeker brother, a dwarf commoner, bound and unconscious after captivity. The book does not assign him Gundren’s stable-at-0-HP state; assess and record his actual condition before resolving healing and care.

Once rescued and able to travel, he is grateful and offers to accompany the party during the remaining exploration. He knows no more about the mine’s layout than they do. Prefer a protected escort over silently treating him as a trained combat ally.
This room becomes a safe, comfortable rest site after Nezznar and his minions are dealt with. It is not automatically safe while enemies remain next door.
If rescued and alive at the adventure’s end, Nundro provides a 200-XP party award divided equally if using XP. Mark the reward pending until survival is known; do not award repeatedly on reload.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 50–51. Nundro’s rescue, survival, and commoner status are printed; his precise starting HP requires a recorded DM ruling.
contexts.tv: Show E20 only after the real cell is opened. A false hostage in area 19 is not this rescue.
choices: Escort Nundro out now, secure a rest, or continue with a stated protection plan.
If Gundren lives, arrange an actual reunion; if he died, let Nundro learn the truth from the party.

contexts.title: Phandalin · choose the homecoming that happened
read: Phandalin’s roofs appear beyond the fields. Someone by the road looks up, recognizes you, and hurries toward town. By the time you reach the first houses, people are waiting to hear what happened.

The places you recognize offer somewhere to begin your account, but the people who hear it will need your words. You can tell them what you witnessed, ask what changed during your absence, or settle a practical need before deciding what comes after the expedition.
run: If Gundren and Nundro live and the mine is reclaimed: play their reunion and a sober remembrance of Tharden. They can resume stewardship and offer the party a 10 percent share of future mine profits, as printed. This is a share when profits exist, not a chest of immediate gold.
If Nundro is rescued but the mine remains dangerous: let the family thank the party, provide care, and ask what practical support is needed for the return. Do not announce the mine reopened.

If only one brother lives: give that survivor the news and let the party choose memorial, protection, and next steps. Any changed management or profit agreement is a new recorded arrangement, not an automatic duplicate of the printed ending.
If both brothers died or neither returned: focus on telling the truth, returning identified possessions, and settling custody of the mine. No Rockseeker can grant a reward from beyond the grave.
If Nezznar escaped or a bargain continues: Sildar asks for the last verified sighting and terms. Let townsfolk respond to evidence rather than declaring the threat ended.
If Redbrands or Iarno remain active from earlier play, reflect that in town. Barthen, the Lionshield, rescued families, and other NPCs react only to their actual deliveries, rescues, and promises.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 51 gives the successful conclusion. The conditional loss, partial success, and escaped-villain scenes are original adaptations to actual play.
contexts.tv: Stage the neutral town map first. Use the celebratory homecoming art only if the outcome and mood support it.
choices: Public success: invite the players to describe a small celebration.
Mixed outcome: gratitude, mourning, and practical help can share the same scene.
Unfinished expedition: end on the party’s chosen plan to return.

contexts.title: Optional consequence · Returning war band
read: Boots and low voices approach through the trees. A returning patrol has found the castle less quiet than it expected.

The approaching sounds give you time to look toward cover and the route you used to reach the castle. How clearly you can see the patrol depends on where you stand. You can wait to learn more, call out, or decide whether to leave before the meeting becomes unavoidable.
run: Optional printed complication: Targor Bloodsword, a hobgoblin with 20 HP, leads two ordinary hobgoblins and two wolves.
Targor has ambitions of succeeding Grol. A credible offer and DC 15 Charisma (Persuasion) can convince him to let the party pass rather than avenge the king.
Use this only if it improves pacing and follows actual travel. A depleted party needs a visible escape route.
private: Adventure p. 41.
contexts.tv: Show a woodland or castle approach map only if the returning patrol meets the party. Do not spawn it by default.

contexts.title: If violence starts · Old Owl Well
run: This is the printed first-contact fight, not the current default. Kost disappeared in actual play. Deploy him or any zombies only if the saved state and a new encounter justify their presence.
In the printed first-contact fight, twelve zombies can emerge from the tower. Hamun Kost uses the Evil Mage base spells without Iarno’s staff; AC 12, HP 22, spell save DC 13, +5 spell attacks.
Zombie: AC 8, HP 22, slam +3 for 1d6+1. At 0 HP, Undead Fortitude may leave it at 1 HP unless radiant damage or a critical hit caused the drop.
Do not deploy every zombie at once unless they are actually visible and participating. This whole camp is a severe fight for low-level PCs; give routes to retreat.
private: Adventure p. 29; Evil Mage p. 57; SRD 5.1 Zombie pp. 356–357.
contexts.tv: Switch to the well battle map only when position matters. Reveal zombies as they emerge, not at scene start.

contexts.title: If the camp fights · Wyvern Tor
run: The party already cleared this camp. Do not launch this encounter in the current campaign unless actual play establishes new occupants.
Printed first-contact reference: one ordinary orc outside; six ordinary orcs, Brughor at 30 HP, and Gog the ogre inside.
Orc: AC 13, HP 15, greataxe +5 for 1d12+3, javelin +5 for 1d6+3, and Aggressive bonus-action movement toward a visible hostile creature.
Ogre: AC 11, HP 59, greatclub +6 for 2d8+4 or javelin +6 for 2d6+4. After Brughor falls, surviving orcs flee according to the adventure.
This is a major threat. Do not add wandering enemies on top of it without an actual cause.
private: Adventure p. 35; 2014 SRD 5.1 Orc p. 339 and Ogre p. 336.
contexts.tv: Show the ravine battle map. Start with the sentry, then reveal the cave force if it arrives.

contexts.title: Thundertree 1 · Western cottage
read: A roofless cottage crouches beneath a broad tree. Its doorway has almost vanished into weeds.

The weeds interrupt a straight approach to the doorway, and the open roof leaves the cottage exposed to the sky. You can examine the nearer ground, look through the ruined walls, or keep watch beneath the broad tree before choosing how to enter.
run: Two twig blights hide beside the entrance. Compare their Stealth to passive Perception; if fighting breaks out, they can aid area 2.
Twig blight: AC 13, HP 4, claws +3 for 1d4+1 piercing; vulnerable to fire.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.
contexts.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.

contexts.title: Thundertree 2 · Blighted cottages
read: Two collapsed homes stand side by side, their old rooms given over to brush and young trees.

The brush has grown across what used to separate the homes' rooms. Fallen walls still mark their old boundaries beneath the living growth. You can inspect a particular patch of rubble or keep together where the route between the two ruins is easiest to see.
run: Six twig blights wait in the growth; the two from area 1 join after one round if still alive and nearby.
A careful search and DC 10 Perception finds a chest with 700 cp, 160 sp, and 90 gp.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.
contexts.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.

contexts.title: Thundertree 4 · Reidoth’s watch
read: One cottage seems to have resisted the years. Its shutters are stout, and someone has cleared the growth near the door.

The cleared approach and sturdy shutters set this house apart from its neighbors. They give you somewhere to knock or call without pushing through the overgrowth. You can announce yourselves, inspect the outside, or wait at a respectful distance for someone to answer.
run: Reidoth is direct but reasonably hospitable. He tells the party how to reach Cragmaw Castle if asked; no dragon bargain is required for those directions.

He warns of ash zombies, plant creatures, spiders, cultists, and a young green dragon. He knows where Wave Echo Cave is but offers that location only if the party drives the dragon off; he will not accompany them inside.
If attacked, he uses his druid shape to flee and waits for the aggressors to leave. Record whether the party earns his trust.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.
contexts.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.

contexts.title: Thundertree 5 · Blighted farmhouse
read: The farmhouse walls have collapsed into a knot of gorse. Something small shifts in the leaves when you disturb the stones.

The tangle of shrubs hides parts of the ground where the walls once stood. The movement in the leaves is brief enough to invite attention rather than an immediate explanation. You can stop disturbing the stones, look for a clearer position, or watch the growth while discussing the approach.
run: Eight twig blights lurk in the thicket. If disturbed, two head for each of two doorways every round for three rounds. This is not one instant visible swarm.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.
contexts.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.

contexts.title: Thundertree 8 · Old smithy
read: Rotten wood and a wide chimney mark the old forge. Two ash-covered shapes slump where the anvils once stood.

The chimney remains a landmark above the rotten construction, while the shapes inside sit among the traces of old work. You can watch them from the entrance, inspect the nearby ground, or listen before disturbing the room. The forge's former purpose does not explain its present occupants.
run: Two ash zombies rise when the party enters and pursue after they see a target. Use the same Ash Puff timing and saves as area 3.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.
contexts.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.

contexts.title: Thundertree 9 · Herbalist’s shop
read: Broken bottles and unreadable books fill an old shop.

Glass fragments and damaged pages share the floor beneath the shelving. You can examine one storage place at a time rather than overturn the whole room. If someone has given you a description to follow, you can compare it with what you actually see here.
run: If Mirna Dendrar sent them, the heirloom case is found automatically. Otherwise DC 15 Perception finds it behind the shelves.
Inside is her emerald necklace worth 200 gp. Record whether the party returns it; doing so earns the printed reward if using XP.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.
contexts.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.

contexts.title: Thundertree 10 · Town square
read: A leaning warrior statue watches over a square almost swallowed by brush. Paths leave in several directions.

The warrior's pose remains visible despite the statue's lean, and the paths offer several different ways to leave the square. You can study the carving, check your bearings against the surrounding ruins, or choose the next approach with the whole group in sight.
run: DC 15 History identifies the old hero as Palien. DC 20 Strength can topple the statue if someone tries.
Let the party choose the next building by what they see on the player map; do not push them toward the dragon.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.
contexts.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.

contexts.title: Thundertree 12 · Weaver’s cottage
read: A broken loom sits in a cottage open to the weather. Thick growth hides the ground beyond its southern wall.

The broken loom identifies one kind of work once done here. Beyond it, the southern growth conceals ground you cannot yet judge. You can examine the cottage's visible remains or keep back from the thicket while deciding where to direct your attention.
run: Six twig blights wait in the southern thicket. Compare Stealth to Perception before initiative.
Loud combat here draws cautious investigation by the cultists in area 13.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.
contexts.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.

contexts.title: Thundertree 3 · The Brown Horse
read: A faded horse sign hangs above the door of an old tavern. Inside, forms slump against the walls and beneath the bar.

The hanging sign gives the ruin a name even though its hospitality is long gone. The slumped forms are visible among the remains of ordinary tavern furnishings. You can stop at the doorway to study them, call into the room, or decide where to stand before entering.
run: Four ash zombies rise when living creatures enter. They start prone; standing uses half their speed.

Ash Puff: the first time each zombie takes damage, creatures within 5 feet make DC 10 Constitution saves or suffer disadvantage on attacks, saves, and checks for one minute; repeat the save at turn end. Track each zombie separately.
Zombie: AC 8, HP 22, slam +3 for 1d6+1; check Undead Fortitude at 0 HP.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.
contexts.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.

contexts.title: Thundertree 6 · Ruined store and webs
read: White strands cross the lane to a broken store. The building looks empty from outside, though its walls offer plenty of shadows.

The strands cross the lane as well as the building, making the approach itself worth examining. Your light catches some threads more readily than the shadows behind them. You can study the webbing from clear ground or decide how much of the lane you want to cross.
run: Two giant spiders hide inside. Webbed squares are difficult terrain; DC 10 Athletics crosses, failure restrains. A restrained creature may use an action for DC 12 Strength; a light slashing weapon can cut a web (AC 10, HP 5, vulnerable to fire).
Spider: AC 14, HP 26; bite +5 for 1d8+3 piercing plus DC 11 Constitution save against 2d8 poison (half on success); web +5 can restrain and recharges on 5–6.
A cocooned adventurer holds a healing potion, 23 gp, and 35 sp.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.
contexts.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.

contexts.title: Thundertree 7 · Venomfang’s tower
read: A broken tower rises above two spider corpses. The air around it smells sharp and wrong; the upper roof is open to the sky.

The dead spiders give the tower's sharp smell a more tangible companion. Broken stone and the open upper roof offer places to look before you approach the entrance. You can keep your distance, seek another view of the structure, or pause to decide what danger you are willing to meet.
run: Venomfang is a young green dragon: AC 18, HP 136, fly 60, poison breath DC 16 Constitution for 12d6 poison in a 30-foot cone, half on success. It is far beyond a routine level-2 fight.
Give players visible signs of danger and time to retreat or parley. Venomfang values its lair; if reduced to half HP it flies away. It may hear loud cottage activity and ambush.

Tower chest: 800 sp, 150 gp, four 60-gp silver goblets, misty step and lightning bolt scrolls. Hew, a +1 battleaxe with extra damage against plants and wood objects, lies under the coin. Reveal only when found.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.
contexts.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.

contexts.title: Thundertree 11 · Old garrison
read: An old stone barracks still has a roof and narrow windows. Rusted armor lies among the beds.

The surviving roof makes the barracks feel more enclosed than the cottages outside. Narrow windows admit limited views, while beds and old armor divide the interior. You can stop to examine the threshold, look over the room, or listen before touching any of the remains.
run: Five ash zombies wake when disturbed. Their scraps of armor do not improve AC 8. Use Ash Puff and Undead Fortitude as in area 3.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.
contexts.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.

contexts.title: Thundertree 13 · Dragon cultists
read: The shutters of this apparently empty house are barred from within. You hear low voices behind them.

The voices make the barred shutters more than a sign of an abandoned house. They offer a chance to speak before attempting to get inside. You can call from the approach, listen for a response, or stand where the occupants can see you if they choose to look out.
run: Six cultists live here. Their leader Favric wants to make an alliance with the dragon; the others prefer to survive. They are willing to talk and need not fight.
If the party seems interested in the dragon, Favric may offer to introduce them as a tribute. Do not hide his intention if the players probe his story.
Cultist: AC 12, HP 9, scimitar +3 for 1d6+1. Favric has the same combat block. Favric carries a potion of flying; a coffer holds three diamonds worth 100 gp each.
The door is barred from within (DC 20 Strength); shutters DC 15 Strength.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.
contexts.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.

contexts.title: 4 · Begin castle exploration
run: Keep an alarm note: quiet, suspicious, or raised. Once raised, nearby room groups can respond according to their keyed descriptions.
The party can retreat through any route it actually opened. Resting inside a guarded castle has consequences; make the situation clear before a rest.
Use the printed room map for distances and door placement. The TV map is a player-safe tactical interpretation.
private: Adventure map p. 37; keyed rooms pp. 36–41.
contexts.tv: Show the unmarked castle map with fog. Reveal one entered space at a time. Do not deploy the entire garrison.

contexts.title: Area 1 · Entrance and sentries
read: Shattered gate timbers lie across an old entrance. Above the wreckage, narrow slots stare out from two small chambers.

The wrecked timbers interrupt a straight walk through the entrance. The narrow openings above offer views into the approach without giving you the same view back. You can study the wall from cover, look for a clearer way through, or decide who will cross the exposed ground first.
run: There are two goblins in each area-3 archer post, four total. They glance out only intermittently. Compare the party’s Stealth to their passive Perception rather than granting automatic detection.
If they see intruders, they shoot from behind arrow-slit cover and shout. They cannot fire directly at enemies who have passed the broken gate.
Their alarm can bring goblins from area 4 and hobgoblins from area 6 into area 2.
private: Adventure p. 36. Each pair is a separate 100-XP group if using XP.
contexts.tv: Reveal the gate and two arrow-slit posts. Keep the goblins hidden until noticed or until they fire.

contexts.title: Area 2 · Falling rubble
read: A wide hall disappears into half-light. Dust lies thick around a pile of fallen plaster, and closed doors lead away on either side.

The fallen plaster marks one part of the floor as different from the rest. Beyond it, the closed doors give you choices without revealing what lies behind them. You can inspect the ground, listen at a door, or choose a position that keeps the entrance in sight.
run: The hidden tripwire is spotted by passive Perception 20 or active DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) while searching this area. Once found, it is easy to avoid or disable without a check.
A creature that crosses the rubble without avoiding it triggers a ceiling collapse. Creatures in the marked area make DC 10 Dexterity saves: 3d6 bludgeoning on failure, half on success.
The noise alerts areas 3, 7, 8, and 9. Record the alarm before moving to another room.
private: Adventure p. 36. The TV map must not pre-mark the tripwire or exact fall zone.
contexts.tv: Reveal the hall. Show the collapse only after it is detected or triggered.

contexts.title: Area 4 · Ruined barracks
read: Broken stone has swallowed much of the tower, but bedrolls and a narrow cleared path show that someone still sleeps here.

The cleared strip and the bedding are more recent signs than the fallen masonry around them. You can follow the space someone has made through the rubble or stop to examine how it is being used. The damaged tower offers no assurance that everyone inside is asleep or absent.
run: Three goblins bunk here. A loud fight draws one goblin from area 7 to investigate; if that scout does not return or raises alarm, the others respond.
The eastern passage through rubble is safe despite its appearance.
private: Adventure p. 37.
contexts.tv: Reveal the southwest room when entered; place three goblins only when visible.

contexts.title: Area 5 · Storeroom and Sildar’s gear
read: Spoiled provisions and old casks crowd the room. Among them lie a bloodied coat of mail, a crossbow, and a sword bearing a familiar crest.

The recognizable equipment is within a room still crowded by old stores. You can examine its markings and condition without deciding how it came here. The casks and provisions break up the floor around it, so someone can watch the entrance while another person investigates.
run: The chain mail, heavy crossbow, and longsword belong to Sildar. Record whether the party returns them; his equipped combat card is appropriate only after he regains gear.
A small cask contains dwarven brandy. A second glass within one hour poisons the drinker for one hour, per the book.
private: Adventure p. 37.
contexts.tv: Reveal the storeroom; do not show the significance of its gear until the characters inspect it.

contexts.title: Area 6 · Hobgoblin barracks
read: This room is surprisingly orderly. Weapons hang on brackets above four pallets, and the floor has been swept clear of rubble.

The swept floor and arranged weapons stand out against the ruin you passed on the way here. The pallets leave recognizable places to rest and narrow spaces to move between them. You can inspect the room from its edge or check which visible exit you want watched.
run: Four hobgoblins defend this room and respond quickly to the sentries’ alarm. They usually ignore noise elsewhere unless their own room is threatened.
Hobgoblin: AC 18, HP 11, speed 30, longsword +3 for 1d8+1; longbow +3 for 1d8+1. Once per turn, Martial Advantage adds 2d6 when an ally is within 5 feet of the target.
A light, carved quarterstaff on the wall is worth 10 gp. Other mounted arms are ordinary.
private: Adventure pp. 37–38; SRD 5.1 hobgoblin p. 322.
contexts.tv: Reveal this room at entry; deploy four hobgoblins if still present.

contexts.title: Area 7 · Banquet hall
read: Once a grand hall, this chamber now smells of stale food and a neglected brazier. Goblin voices rise around two scarred tables.

The two tables take up much of the social space, with the neglected brazier drawing stale smells around it. The voices give you something to listen to before you answer them. You can remain at the edge, make your presence clear, or take stock of the route back out.
run: Seven ordinary goblins and Yegg, their 12-HP cook, are here initially. Reconcile any scout sent to area 4 before deploying this wave.
If Yegg falls, surviving goblins flee east or west, avoiding the trapped north route. They need not fight to the last.
private: Adventure p. 38. Yegg plus seven goblins is eight creatures total.
contexts.tv: Reveal tables and benches; only place goblins that remain here after alarm movement.

contexts.title: Area 8 · Dark hall and grick
read: A narrow, lightless hall bears carvings that do not match its current occupants. Heavy curtains hang to the north, and a stone brazier stands between them.

The carvings reward a closer look, but the curtains prevent you from seeing the spaces beyond them. The stone brazier is a visible landmark between those covered openings. You can study the workmanship, listen toward the cloth, or decide whether to move farther into the hall.
run: A grick watches from an upper rocky ledge. Compare its Stealth to the party’s Perception to determine who notices it; do not give automatic surprise.

Grick: AC 14, HP 27, climb 30; tentacles +4 for 2d6+2 slashing. If they hit, it can make a beak +4 for 1d6+2 piercing against the same target. Its resistance to nonmagical weapon damage needs manual review in the damage panel.

DC 10 Intelligence (Religion) identifies the old human gods in the carvings. A gold sun-elf statuette worth 100 gp is hidden under coal in the brazier. It can answer one augury-like question for a non-evil creature, then loses that power.
private: Adventure pp. 38–39; SRD 5.1 grick p. 318. Do not reveal the hidden statuette before discovery.
contexts.tv: Reveal the hall first. Show the grick token or reveal art only after it drops from its hiding place.

contexts.title: Area 9 · Goblin shrine
read: A stone altar lies beneath a blood-dark cloth. A goblin in ritual scraps fusses over gold-colored implements while two acolytes watch the curtains.

The cloth hides much of the altar's surface, while the implements catch what light reaches the room. The watchers' attention rests on the curtains as well as on you. You can address them from where you stand, inspect what is visible, or withdraw before disturbing the arrangement.
run: Lhupo, a goblin with 12 HP, and two ordinary goblins occupy the shrine. If they heard the grick fight, they hide behind the altar and cannot be surprised.
The human-made chalice, knife, and censer are worth 150 gp, 60 gp, and 120 gp respectively if taken.
private: Adventure p. 39. The objects are art treasure, not spellcasting tools.
contexts.tv: Reveal the shrine beyond the curtains; place its occupants when they are seen.

contexts.title: Area 10 · South postern gate
read: An overgrown path climbs toward an iron door protected by the wall above it. Narrow slits overlook the approach.

The door offers a more contained approach than the wrecked main entrance, but the slits still overlook the ground before it. Brush crowds the path around your feet. You can examine the door and wall from a distance or decide how to approach without assuming the entrance is unwatched.
run: The door is locked: DC 15 Dexterity with thieves’ tools or DC 25 Strength to break it. The goblins in area 7 can be heard from the arrow slits if the party pauses.
The goblins do not actively watch this path, but loud noise draws their attention and can raise the alarm.
private: Adventure p. 39.
contexts.tv: Reveal only the gate and path from the direction of approach.

contexts.title: Area 11 · Concealed north entrance
read: A fallen tower lies under dusty canvas and brush. A few old crates remain where a storeroom once stood.

The canvas and vegetation break up the outline of what the tower used to be. The crates are the clearest remaining sign of its practical use. You can examine a visible patch of ground, check beneath accessible cover, or keep the ruined approach in sight while someone searches.
run: From outside, DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) spots signs of a path to the concealed entrance. If actively searching the castle’s exterior for a hidden way in, DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) spots the canvas door.
This entrance can allow a quieter route toward the king’s side of the castle. Record whether the party leaves the canvas disturbed.
private: Adventure p. 39.
contexts.tv: Do not show the concealed canvas entrance before the party finds it.

contexts.title: Area 12 · Guard barracks
read: Four pallets line a cramped guardroom. A coal brazier glows, and a curtain conceals an arch to the north.

The brazier's glow reaches the pallets more readily than it reaches beyond the hanging cloth. The curtain separates what you can see from what you can only hear. You can pause to listen, examine the guardroom, or decide who will stand nearest the covered arch.
run: Two loyal hobgoblins guard this room. At the start of combat, one runs to warn Grol in area 14 and returns two rounds later if able.
Track that warning explicitly; it changes Vyerith’s position in the final room.
private: Adventure p. 40.
contexts.tv: Reveal the east barracks; place its two guards when seen.

contexts.title: Area 13 · Owlbear tower
read: Something heavy shifts beyond the barred door. The wood shudders once, then a low animal breath fills the silence.

The barred door gives you a boundary you can choose to keep. The weight behind it is audible before it is visible, and the wood's movement gives you reason to judge your distance. You can listen, examine the fastening, or leave the barrier intact while discussing another route.
run: The owlbear has AC 13, HP 59, speed 40; one beak +7 for 1d10+5 and one claws +7 for 2d8+5 on its turn. It is dangerous for a level-2 party.
Fresh meat distracts it. If freed and not blocked, it flees the castle, attacking creatures that get in its way. Releasing it can earn the same printed XP as defeating it.
A chest on a high ledge requires DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) to notice; it holds 90 ep, 120 gp, a healing potion, silence scroll, and revivify scroll.
private: Adventure p. 40; SRD 5.1 owlbear pp. 339–340. The ledge chest is not visible from the floor.
contexts.tv: Reveal the tower but hide the owlbear until the barred door opens and it is visible.

contexts.title: Area 14 · Grol and Vyerith
read: Voices cut through the door: a harsh demand, then a smooth reply. Inside, furs cover the floor while a towering bugbear argues with a dark-clad visitor.

The argument reveals different voices, not an agreement you understand yet. The furs and the speakers' positions divide the room into places to approach or avoid. You can listen for a few more words, announce yourselves, or look for a position that keeps your way out clear.
run: King Grol is a 45-HP bugbear. Snarl is an 18-HP wolf. Vyerith is a 52-HP doppelganger disguised as a drow emissary of the Black Spider; its true nature is secret.

The printed encounter makes Gundren a hostage, but actual play left him at an inn. Grol and Vyerith may still bargain over information or possessions they actually hold. Do not invent a new hostage or assume they have Gundren’s map.
If warned, Vyerith may hide near the northeast exit. If Grol falls, Vyerith may try to escape through area 11; track any item it actually carries.
The printed room has 220 sp, 160 ep, and three healing potions in a sack. Confirm the map’s current custody from actual play before placing it there.
Allow conversation, retreat, and pursuit. Record what the party finds and learns; Gundren’s safety is resolved separately at the inn.
private: Adventure pp. 40–41 supplies the original keyed room. This campaign’s actual Gundren outcome overrides its printed hostage setup. Glasstaff’s arrival at the castle is DM-only until discovered.
contexts.tv: Reveal the room when the door opens. Gundren was left at an inn and must not be staged here. Keep Vyerith’s true form private until revealed.

rows.title: Cragmaw Castle · Cragmaw Castle · king's quarters
Wave Echo Cave · Wave Echo Cave · southern workings

contexts.title: Area 1 · Rockseeker camp and the descent
read: Three bedrolls surround a silent camp. Supplies lie where their owners left them. A dwarf’s body rests among the bundles, and a rope tied around a stone spire drops into a break in the cavern floor.

The rope is the clearest connection between this camp and the space below. Its fastening and the edge of the pit can be examined before anyone descends. The bundles and the body offer separate questions, and you can leave room for someone to keep watch while the others decide where to begin.
run: The dead dwarf is Tharden, Gundren’s brother, killed by Nezznar. Nundro was captured and is in area 20; the camp alone does not tell the characters his current location.
Useful ordinary provisions and mining equipment remain. Tharden wears boots of striding and springing; record discovery, identification, and ownership separately.
The pit is 10 feet wide and 20 feet deep. Without a rope, climbing its wall requires DC 15 Strength (Athletics). Failing by 5 or more causes a fall: 1d6 bludgeoning per 10 feet fallen, then prone.
From the pit bottom, the northwest passage leads to area 2; the east passage leads to area 3. The existing rope offers a practical way down; do not apply the no-rope DC to every descent.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 44; marked map p. 43. Boots: appendix A. Do not show the corpse as Nundro.
contexts.tv: Reveal the camp and visible pit. Cave-entrance art is E01; keep later rooms covered.
choices: Northwest: mine tunnels, area 2.
East: old entrance, area 3.
Return to the surface using the actual secured route.

contexts.title: Area 2 · Mine tunnels
read: Low passages cross and divide ahead of you. Tool marks stop abruptly at unfinished stone faces. Between the turns, even your footsteps seem to lose their direction.

The low stonework makes every turn feel close, and the unfinished faces give several branches a similar appearance. You can keep a mark at the last junction, follow the group carefully, or stop to compare the visible passages before choosing one. Your route back is something you can record as you go.
run: These older workings have ceilings only 6 feet high. Several branches end at abandoned rock faces.
One ochre jelly lurks in a dead end. It stalks intruders and tries to catch a lone target. Use its actual movement and opportunities; it does not appear in several passages at once.
Review its Split reaction before resolving slashing or lightning damage. Track each resulting jelly’s identity and HP if it splits.
There is no keyed treasure here. Use the private map to adjudicate the maze rather than inventing forced wrong turns.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 44; ochre jelly appendix B. Stalking is printed behavior; specific movement depends on play.
contexts.tv: Reveal only reached branches. Do not place the lurking jelly on TV before it is seen.

contexts.title: Area 3 · Old entrance and ceiling stirges
read: Carved miners still work along the walls above a floor strewn with ancient bones. Empty brass lamps hang in the stone. Beyond them, the high ceiling disappears into shadow.

The abandoned lamps offer no light of their own. Your illumination catches the miners' carved tools and the pale bones at different heights, leaving the upper space harder to judge. You can inspect the floor, examine the figures on the walls, or direct your attention toward the ceiling.
run: Ten stirges cling to the 30-foot-high ceiling. Roll one Dexterity (Stealth) check for the group and compare it with each character’s passive Perception if that character is not watching the ceiling; resolve active observation normally.
Use the 2014 surprise procedure individually for any creature that failed to notice the threat. Characters who detect them hear flapping as the attack begins.
The bones are remains of miners and invaders, not another skeleton encounter. Track attached stirges on their specific targets and remove them when detached or slain.
The old southern entrance was buried long ago. It is not a usable shortcut to the surface without a separately planned excavation.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 44. Room 3 holds ten stirges; the nine animating skeletons are in room 4.
contexts.tv: Show the carved hall and bones; reveal the stirges only after detection or their attack.

contexts.title: Area 4 · Old guardroom
read: Stone bunks and splintered racks lie beneath a fallen section of ceiling. Bones are scattered between them, half buried in pale dust.

The bunks identify this as a place where people once slept, while the broken racks suggest equipment no longer fit for use. Fallen stone interrupts parts of the floor. You can study the room from the threshold, choose a route through the debris, or examine a particular set of remains.
run: In the round after a living creature enters, the remains assemble into nine skeletons. Start combat at that trigger; they do not rise before someone enters.
The skeletons fight until destroyed. Keep survivors recorded if the party withdraws; a later visit does not create nine new skeletons.
Rubble and broken furniture can affect movement or cover only where actually present. No treasure is keyed here.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 44. Original narration avoids announcing the animation before its trigger.
contexts.tv: E04 shows the room; stage E04B only when the bones rise. Do not reveal the ambush image at entry.

contexts.title: Area 5 · Assayers’ office
read: Three dusty scales stand on a stone counter. Paper scraps fill small niches behind it, and the floor holds the remains of workers and warriors who never left.

The arrangement of the scales and niches suggests work that once involved careful measurements and records. The scraps are within reach, but their age is visible in their edges. You can look without touching, search the counter, or ask someone who knows the writing to examine what survives.
run: The papers crumble when touched. Someone who reads Dwarvish can make out remnants of ore weights and payments; there is no complete surviving ledger to take.
A locked iron strongbox sits behind the counter. Opening its lock requires thieves’ tools and DC 20 Dexterity.
Contents: 600 cp, 180 sp, 90 ep, and 60 gp. Add only money actually collected to party inventory; record an unopened or emptied box for the return visit.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 44–45. No combat group is keyed to this office.
contexts.tv: Show E05 and the entered room. Keep strongbox contents private until opened.

contexts.title: Area 6 · South barracks
read: Rows of stone bunks flank an old brazier. Three gaunt shapes crouch over the scattered bones, working their jaws against scraps far too old to feed them.

The bunks and old brazier break the chamber into narrower gaps than its size first suggests. The shapes among the bones are occupied with what lies before them. You can stop at the entrance to judge those gaps, choose where to stand, or decide whether to make your presence known.
run: Listening at the partly open door: DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) hears crunching and splintering.
Three ghouls attack fresh prey immediately. They belong to the larger pack whose other seven members occupy area 9; these are separate starting groups, not replacements.
Review claw paralysis, the creature’s immunity exceptions, and end-of-turn saves. Mark a paralyzed target so subsequent attacks are resolved correctly.
If a pursuit moves these three elsewhere, update their location instead of deploying them again.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 45; ghoul appendix B. No treasure is keyed here.
contexts.tv: Use E06 after the interior is visible. Do not announce the creatures through a closed door.

contexts.title: Area 7 · Ruined storeroom and a secure rest
read: A collapsed wall opens onto a small chamber. Beyond a half-open door, a surviving storeroom holds neat rows of cracked, empty kegs. Its stonework is sound.

The half-open door breaks the line of the collapsed wall. Beyond it, cracked kegs still stand in something like their old order, a small island of storage amid the ruin. The sound of stonework carries here; its source remains out of sight.
run: The northern storeroom is a secure resting place: the adventure explicitly says monsters do not come here. Its sound door can be blocked or barred from inside.
Do not roll routine wandering attacks inside this refuge. If the party knowingly leads an active pursuer here, resolve that specific pursuit openly before calling it secure.
The kegs are empty. Track rest duration, recovery choices, light, and ongoing conditions through the rest controls. A rest does not revive defeated enemies or replace taken treasure.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 45. The secure-room exception overrides general wandering guidance. Rest rules use the campaign profile and recorded character exceptions.
contexts.tv: Show E07. This is an opportunity to pause without a new enemy reveal.
choices: Use the Rest / retreat card to review recovery and the expedition record.
Continue through an already explored route after the players choose.

contexts.title: Area 8 · Fungi cavern and poison gas
read: Pale caps, thick stalks, and shelves of fungus crowd the cavern. Some growths glow green, casting enough light to reveal the far wall. The floor between them is almost lost beneath the carpet.

The faint green light clings to the caps and stalks, leaving the room's edges hard to judge. The growth covers the walking surface as well as the view ahead. Before crossing, you can study its spread from the threshold and decide how close to bring your light.
run: Most fungi are harmless, and the glow lights the whole cavern. Attempting to cross disturbs the carpet and releases poison gas.
Each creature in the cavern makes DC 11 Constitution: failure deals 3d6 poison and causes Poisoned for 10 minutes; success avoids these effects. Do not apply half damage on success.
Gas disperses after 1 minute. Until then, each living creature ending its turn in the cavern repeats the save. Review poison immunities and resistances separately for each target.
The book does not give a fixed DC for every invented crossing method. Decide whether the plan avoids disturbance before rolling, state any ruling, and preserve player alternatives.
Record gas start/end time and each character’s condition. Pebble’s mineral interest is not evidence that this fungus is edible or that an unconfirmed ancestry trait grants poison immunity.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 45–46. Gas is a hazard, not a creature and not a compulsory fight.
contexts.tv: E08 before disturbance; E08B only after gas is released. Stage affected characters before resolving saves.

contexts.title: Rest or retreat · keep the expedition state
run: Area 7’s northern storeroom is the published secure refuge. Area 20 is safe once Nezznar and his minions are dealt with. Use those facts instead of making every rest a surprise attack.
Before applying a rest, review current HP, hit dice, slots, limited uses, concentration, maximum-HP loss, conditions, food, light, and any recorded class or house-rule exceptions.

If retreating, follow a route actually explored. Ask who assists fallen allies, carries captives or treasure, and secures the area-1 rope. Resolve an existing pursuit rather than creating a new ambush automatically.
Record elapsed time. Check the flameskull’s one-hour return deadline, ten-minute poison durations, and Forge enchantment expiry; recovery does not stop these clocks.

Log the rest or retreat in the Wave Echo journal. If the group returns to Phandalin, preserve the dungeon save. Opening a fresh pack or resetting the session is not the way to continue a partially explored mine.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 42, 45, and 51; creature/item recovery rules and the selected campaign profile. The rest review is an original table procedure.
contexts.tv: Keep the party’s current visible scene; do not expose new areas merely by opening this reference card.

rows.title: Wave Echo Cave · Wave Echo Cave · central mine

contexts.title: Area 10 · Dark pool
read: Still black water fills the cave. Pale broken shells crunch along the bank, and a slow stream slides away beneath a low opening to the northeast.

The bank's shells crunch beneath a careful step, while the black water gives little sense of its depth. The stream's low northeastern opening draws your eye away from the pool. Following it would mean approaching stone and water that conceal what lies beyond.
run: The pool reaches 20 feet deep in the middle. The northeast stream is 3 feet deep, with only 2–3 feet of air above it; characters can wade along it to area 18.
Searching the pool reveals a skeleton on the bottom, 10 feet from shore under 10 feet of water. It is a former human wizard, not an active monster.

The skeleton has two platinum rings worth 75 gp each and a wand of magic missiles. Resolve actual underwater movement, air, retrieval, and identification; do not require an invented Perception DC just to replace the keyed discovery.
Record who has the wand and its charges before use. Show any discovery handout only after it is retrieved.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 46; marked map p. 43; wand in appendix A.
contexts.tv: Show E10 and the pool; do not announce its submerged treasure before investigation.
choices: The northeast stream reaches the collapsed cavern, area 18.
The stairway east reaches the north barracks, area 11.

contexts.title: Area 11 · North barracks
read: Heat from a glowing brazier touches your face. Stone bunks line the walls, and a broken table has been piled against the eastern door.

The brazier's warmth sets this room apart from the colder passages. Bunks leave narrow spaces between them, and the broken table piled against the eastern door makes that exit a practical obstacle. You can inspect the barricade from this side before deciding whether to disturb it.
run: Five bugbears serve Nezznar here and hold back the undead. Listening at either door with DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) hears hungry voices speaking Goblin.
The eastern door is barricaded from within: DC 20 Strength to force it. The west door is not given that barricade.
The largest bugbear carries 15 cp, 13 ep, and a potion of vitality. This is vitality, not a healing potion; use its actual item effects.
Bargaining, misdirection, and withdrawal remain possible if the players attempt them; the book gives no automatic friendly bargain. Track anyone sent elsewhere rather than spawning a replacement.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 46. These five are separate from the three in area 18 and two with Nezznar.
contexts.tv: Use E11 after entering. Reveal only the defenders actually still stationed here.

contexts.title: Area 13 · Starry cavern
read: Your light scatters across a ceiling that glitters like a field of stars. Below it stand two battered stone buildings, blackened by fire, amid the fallen dead.

Points of light prick the ceiling above the two blackened buildings. Down below, fallen bodies and scorched stone tell a harsher story. The buildings interrupt the open cavern, each offering a closer approach and a separate interior to examine.
run: The ceiling’s minerals are attractive but neither magical nor valuable. Do not silently turn Pebble’s taste for unusual stone into a magic-item reward.
A character proficient in Arcana senses subtle magic here; detect magic also reveals it. The aura strengthens toward the northern building, area 15.
The buildings use human proportions, unlike the dwarf-sized doors elsewhere. Area 14 is the former guest quarters; area 15 is the workshop.
No creature encounter or fixed treasure is keyed to this open cavern. If an actual wandering encounter occurs, use the wandering card and record it separately.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 47. The mine’s surviving magic has its printed explanation; the custom Echo story is not proven by this aura.
contexts.tv: Show E13. Keep the interiors of buildings 14 and 15 covered.

contexts.title: Area 14 · Mormesk and the wizards’ quarters
read: Charred furniture stands beneath a sagging ceiling. A scorched chest waits beside a ruined bed. As you step in, darkness gathers out of the floor and turns toward you.

Charred furniture crowds the room beneath the damaged ceiling. The bed and chest survived the destruction well enough to recognize, though their contents cannot be judged from here. The dark presence near the floor draws attention away from them, making the threshold a useful place to stop and look.
run: The damaged doors need DC 15 Strength to wrench or smash open. Mormesk the wraith rises when a living creature enters. He attacks if no one attempts to reason with him.
If neither he nor his property has been harmed, he listens. A useful magic item, scroll, spellbook, or arcane knowledge plus DC 10 Charisma (Persuasion) can persuade him of an offering’s value.

After accepting a gift, he permits examination of his books and lets the party keep the hidden map. He offers the coins and gems for killing the spectator in area 15, but never willingly gives up his wooden pipe.
Unlocked chest: 1,100 cp, 160 sp, 50 ep, three diamonds worth 100 gp each, and a platinum-decorated wooden pipe worth 150 gp. Reward access depends on the actual bargain or defeat.
DC 12 Intelligence (Investigation) reveals a map sewn into one preserved book. Its destination is a DM-created future dungeon; record your chosen location before publishing it.
Mormesk is dangerous and self-interested, not a trustworthy guide to the whole mine. Track Life Drain’s maximum-HP reduction if combat occurs.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 47; wraith appendix B. Any Waterdeep or Echo destination assigned to the sewn map is a labeled campaign addition.
contexts.tv: Use E14 first; E14B when Mormesk manifests. Keep the chest and hidden map private until discovered.
choices: A gift can buy access without combat.
Rejecting his request to kill the guardian remains a valid choice.
A map can seed the next campaign chapter after the party chooses to follow it.

contexts.title: Optional · wandering encounters during exposed delays
run: Use sparingly during a long delay in an exposed area. The book allows a d20 check: 17–20 means an encounter. It does not prescribe a compulsory check every turn or every hour.
Then roll d12: 1–3, 2d4 stirges; 4–5, 1d4 ghouls; 6, 1d4 gricks; 7–8, 1d4 bugbears; 9, 1d6 skeletons; 10, 1d6 zombies; 11–12, one ochre jelly.

Roll only the selected count, place the actual encounter, and identify whether it is a mobile existing group or a newly generated wandering group. Never both remove a keyed enemy and add a duplicate of it.
Exclude the explicitly secure area 7 refuge. An encounter is not automatically combat: signs, detection, concealment, parley, or retreat may resolve it.
For the current level-3 party, do not pile a random wave onto a major fight just to increase difficulty. Use encounter guidance before committing the result.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 42. Table frequencies and counts are printed; choosing when an exposed delay merits a check remains a DM decision.
contexts.tv: Keep the current room and fog. Reveal a wandering creature only when detected.

rows.title: Wave Echo Cave · Wave Echo Cave · northern reaches

contexts.title: Area 16 · Booming cavern
read: The passage ends above churning water. A surge races through the dark and strikes beneath the ledge with a crash you feel in your chest. Then the water sinks back, leaving a long, hollow roar.

Each surge changes the sound of the cavern, filling the spaces between words before falling away again. The water and the stone around it are visible things to study. You can keep back from its edge, watch the rhythm, or inspect the route without entering the water.
run: At normal level, the south ledge is 15 feet above water. A surge every 2 minutes raises the water 10 feet; after 1 minute it drops to its normal 20-foot depth.
The printed room has no automatic damaging wave attack or fixed swim DC. If characters enter, explain the current circumstances and adjudicate swimming, breath, rescue, and any stated ruling.
The sound suggests a larger cavern to the northeast, but that unkeyed continuation is not a prepared secret exit. Do not invent a safe passage without establishing it.
This is the physical source of the mine’s rhythmic booming. No Echo revelation is required to explain it.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 44 and 48–49. Water timing and dimensions are printed; any added current hazard is custom and must be announced consistently.
contexts.tv: Show E16 and only the ledge the party has reached. Keep water volume below table conversation.

contexts.title: Area 17 · Old streambed bypass
read: A dry channel squeezes beneath a low ceiling. Smooth stones and rounded boulders mark the course water once followed through the dark.

Smooth stones lie among larger boulders in the dry channel. With the ceiling hanging low, the route asks you to watch both your footing and your head. Its bends and obstructions break the view ahead; you can keep track of the way back as you pass them.
run: The passage is only 4 feet high and strewn with rounded stones. Describe the restriction and apply squeezing only if a creature’s size and the actual passage dimensions require it.
This was an old route toward area 16. Water was first diverted toward the smelter, then redirected again by the collapse in area 18.
The surviving passage offers a bypass around the undead in area 12. Nezznar has not discovered this route in the initial state; do not give him that knowledge without a cause.
There is no keyed monster or treasure here. Record the newly known route so it remains available for retreat.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 49; marked map p. 43. Do not add a mandatory crawling damage check.
contexts.tv: Show E17. Reveal the low route as it is explored rather than unveiling both ends at once.

contexts.title: Area 18 · Collapsed cavern and Vhalak
read: Water spills down into a broad rift. Ropes hang from stakes along its western edge, while the clack of shifted rubble rises from below. Figures work under the eye of a dark-clad supervisor.

The waterfall fills the rift with a steady roar, broken by the clacking work below. Ropes fastened to stakes on the western side offer a visible means of descent. From the edge, you can examine their condition and the figures beneath before committing to the drop.
run: Three bugbears are here initially: two digging in the rift, one guarding the west side. Vhalak, a doppelganger disguised as a male drow, supervises. If fighting starts, the two below climb up to join.
When two or more bugbears are killed, Vhalak attempts to retreat to area 19 and warn Nezznar. Move the same survivor token and keep its damage; successful escape is not automatic.
The rift is 20 feet deep. Climbing without a rope requires DC 10 Strength (Athletics); failure by 5 or more causes a fall for 1d6 bludgeoning per 10 feet fallen, then prone.
A crushed dwarf beneath heavy rubble wears gauntlets of ogre power. DC 20 Wisdom (Perception) finds the remains; each searching character may make one check per hour. Time spent searching matters.
If these occupants survive and hear fighting in area 19, they arrive after 3 rounds, immediately after the giant spiders’ initiative. Bring only actual available survivors, once.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 49–50. Vhalak is a different doppelganger from Vyerith at the castle; do not merge their fates.
contexts.tv: Show E18 on entry. Vhalak appears as a male drow until the party discovers otherwise; keep its creature identity private.

contexts.title: Area 20 · Rescue Nundro
read: Beyond the locked door, faded cloth hangs above a simple bed. A dwarf lies bound on the cold floor. His breathing is faint but steady.

You can take stock from the threshold before approaching what lies within. The visible condition of any person here and the space around them matter more than guessing what happened out of sight. You can offer help, ask a question, or check the way out before moving someone.
run: The door is locked: thieves’ tools and DC 15 Dexterity, or Nezznar’s anvil-headed key. Noisy activity here draws area 19’s attention if those enemies still can respond; Nezznar sends spiders to investigate.

The prisoner is Nundro, youngest Rockseeker brother, a dwarf commoner, bound and unconscious after captivity. The book does not assign him Gundren’s stable-at-0-HP state; assess and record his actual condition before resolving healing and care.

Once rescued and able to travel, he is grateful and offers to accompany the party during the remaining exploration. He knows no more about the mine’s layout than they do. Prefer a protected escort over silently treating him as a trained combat ally.
This room becomes a safe, comfortable rest site after Nezznar and his minions are dealt with. It is not automatically safe while enemies remain next door.
If rescued and alive at the adventure’s end, Nundro provides a 200-XP party award divided equally if using XP. Mark the reward pending until survival is known; do not award repeatedly on reload.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 50–51. Nundro’s rescue, survival, and commoner status are printed; his precise starting HP requires a recorded DM ruling.
contexts.tv: Show E20 only after the real cell is opened. A false hostage in area 19 is not this rescue.
choices: Escort Nundro out now, secure a rest, or continue with a stated protection plan.
If Gundren lives, arrange an actual reunion; if he died, let Nundro learn the truth from the party.

rows.title: Wave Echo Cave · Wave Echo Cave · great cavern

contexts.title: Area 9 · Great cavern
read: The hall opens around long stone tables and cold braziers. Stairs climb to ledges at either end, above a floor scattered with the remains of an ancient battle.

Cold braziers offer no warmth to the long tables. The stairs and ledges at either end rise above the scattered remains, giving the chamber more than one level to watch. Anything moving across the open floor would be difficult to overlook from above.
run: Seven ghouls lurk on the western ledge. They notice light or noise elsewhere in this cavern and rush down to attack; they fight until destroyed.
The escarpments are 10 feet high. Climbing requires DC 12 Strength (Athletics). Falling or being knocked from the top deals 1d6 bludgeoning and leaves the creature prone.
Keep elevation, stairs, and routes of retreat visible on the DM map. These seven are additional to the three initially in area 6; reconcile any actual movement between groups.
The scale and stair positions come from the private p. 43 plan when the painted close-up differs.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 46. Seven ghouls plus terrain can be very dangerous to the current level-3 party.
contexts.tv: Stage the dedicated cavern map with unreached ledges hidden. E09 is the room illustration.

rows.title: Wave Echo Cave · Wave Echo Cave · smelter

contexts.title: Area 12 · Smelter cavern
read: A cold furnace towers above abandoned ore carts. Beside it, a motionless wheel hangs over a dry channel. Green fire dances around a skull suspended above the armored dead.

Ore carts stand idle beside the furnace, and the wheel hangs motionless over a dry channel. Green fire outlines the skull and catches on the armored dead. The old machinery divides the floor into working spaces; the threat now occupies the same ground where miners once labored.
run: Eight corpses are zombies. They rise against living creatures entering the room but pursue outside it for no more than one round. One flameskull follows its ancient order to prevent intruders passing.
Review the flameskull’s spell card before combat: its area damage is a major danger. Preserve actual spell use, concentration, defenses, and targets; do not grant unlimited fireballs.

A destroyed flameskull reforms after 1 hour unless its remains receive holy water, dispel magic, or remove curse. Record which method was used and the deadline; merely reducing HP to 0 is not permanent clearance.
The dry channel is 10 feet wide and its floor 5 feet below the room. No ability check is needed to scramble in or out. It runs north and east; beyond the room its ceiling is only 5 feet high.
Area 17 provides another route around these guardians. Do not force the party to win this encounter to reach the Forge.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 46; flameskull appendix B. Rejuvenation is a creature rule. Record actual destroyed remains and treatment for the return trip.
contexts.tv: Show E12 when the skull is visible; use the smelter map for channel depth and targets.

rows.title: Wave Echo Cave · Wave Echo Cave · Forge of Spells

contexts.title: Area 15 · Forge of Spells and its guardian
read: Scorched worktables ring a workshop that should have fallen silent centuries ago. Yet green flame still moves in a brazier at its heart. Above it, a many-eyed creature turns, and a greeting sounds inside your mind.

The brazier's green light colors the scorched tables, while the many-eyed creature hangs within the ruined workspace. Its greeting reaches you without crossing the air. There is room to answer before moving closer; the surviving forge equipment remains something to study rather than claim on sight.
run: One spectator guards the workshop and still believes the mine operates. It does not attack merely because visitors speak; it attacks if they try to remove anything.

DC 15 Charisma (Deception) can convince it that one or more characters are wizards or miners authorized by the owners to end its employment. On success it returns to its home plane. Blinding it also makes it leave, believing it can no longer perform its task.
The north room’s door needs DC 15 Strength to force; the western double doors are damaged but slightly open. The northern workroom holds no additional keyed treasure.

DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) identifies the brazier as the magical source. The depleted Forge cannot make permanent enchantments. A nonmagical weapon or armor bathed in its flame for at least 1 minute becomes +1 for 1d12 hours. The brazier cannot be removed.

The southeast table holds Lightbringer (+1 mace; commanded torch-like light; +1d6 radiant against undead while glowing) and Dragonguard (+1 breastplate; advantage on saves against dragon breath weapons). Claim only after resolving the guardian and record the actual bearer.
Use the Forge-use card for temporary items and expiry. Do not stack another +1 onto an already magical item or treat the fire as a permanent upgrade.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 48. Negotiation, blinding, temporary enchantment, and the two named items are printed content. Any later Forge restoration project requires a separate campaign ruling.
contexts.tv: E15 shows the guardian, so display it only when the room can be seen. Use the close-up map if positions matter.
choices: Discharge the guardian through deception, depart peacefully, or fight if the party chooses.
Mormesk’s demand is optional; the spectator can leave without being slain.

contexts.title: Forge use · temporary magic and item custody
run: First resolve the spectator’s actual status. Handling or removing its guarded objects can start combat until its obligation ends or it is defeated.

For each eligible item, record its original statistics, bearer, the full minute in the flame, a 1d12-hour duration roll, and campaign-clock expiry. Apply only the temporary +1 attack/damage for a weapon or +1 AC for armor.

Use the Wave Echo journal to record each temporary Forge effect and its expiry. At expiry, remove that temporary bonus and preserve the item; the reminder is not permission to silently change an unrelated item. Do not reset duration on a reload, rest, or scene change.
Lightbringer and Dragonguard are separate permanent named treasures; their properties do not come from the temporary flame process. They remain subject to actual ownership and equipment choices.
Permanent Forge repair, new recipes, and custom Echo reactions are later campaign projects, not free capabilities of this room. Agree and label any house rule before applying it.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver p. 48. The expiry ledger is a table procedure; the printed temporary effect is +1 for 1d12 hours after at least 1 minute in the flame.
contexts.tv: Show only the item and effect the players have identified. Keep hidden chest contents and future hooks private.

rows.title: Wave Echo Cave · Wave Echo Cave · Temple of Dumathoin

contexts.title: Area 19 · Temple of Dumathoin
read: Six cracked pillars frame a hall swept clean of rubble. At the far end, a seated dwarf carved from stone watches over a rough camp. Bedrolls, packs, and a paper-covered table show that this shrine has become someone’s headquarters.

The figures and stonework draw your eye to different parts of the room. You can note where everyone stands and which route remains behind you before answering. The distance between you and anyone present is something to consider while there is still time to speak.
run: Initial defenders: Nezznar, two bugbears, and four giant spiders. If warned, spiders hide behind pillars and Nezznar casts invisibility near the table. Roll the spiders’ Stealth. Their first move is to web targets before closing; Nezznar joins on the following round.
If Vhalak actually escaped area 18, it can pose as Nundro for a false-hostage ploy. The real Nundro remains in area 20; never duplicate Vhalak or assume it survived.

Unresolved occupants of area 18 can hear combat and arrive after 3 rounds, immediately after the spiders in initiative. Record the alarm round and relocate survivors rather than creating a new full wave.

Religion proficiency recognizes Dumathoin. DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) reveals the apparent emerald eyes are worthless glass. Detect magic reveals strong abjuration. Removing either eye with DC 10 Strength triggers a room-wide collapse: DC 15 Dexterity, 4d10 bludgeoning and prone on failure, half damage on success.

The table has Nezznar’s exploration notes and maps. His sack holds 190 ep, 130 gp, 15 pp, nine 10-gp gems, and a 100-gp electrum ale mug. Nezznar carries a healing potion, spider staff, and the anvil-headed key to area 20; expended items do not reappear as loot.
Use the following Nezznar card for conversation, tactics, and consequences. Defeating him does not automatically clear the undead or rescue Nundro.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 49–50; Nezznar appendix B. Trap damage is 4d10, not 4d6. The two temple bugbears are additional to area 18’s initial three.
contexts.tv: Stage the temple map privately. E19B reveals Nezznar; show it only on confrontation. Hidden spiders remain off TV.

contexts.title: Nezznar · bargain, battle, escape, or capture
read: The dark elf rests one hand on a spider-carved staff. “You have cost me people, time, and secrecy. Before either of us wastes more, tell me what you believe you came here to claim.”

The words being exchanged do not settle what either side will accept. You can hold your position, ask for a specific answer, or make your own terms clear. The chamber and the route behind you remain part of the conversation, even if nobody chooses to mention them.
run: Printed motive: Nezznar wants the Forge and the mine’s secret. He admits being the Black Spider and using both the Cragmaws and Redbrands. In this campaign the Redbrands made Gundren’s capture and castle delivery; do not revert to a goblin-abduction account.

Printed approach: he asks about identities, loyalties, goals, and interests; offers surrender or joint action against the guardians; and intends betrayal once others cease being useful. An offer is not automatically accepted or believed. Let Insight examine a specific claim, and let concrete safeguards matter.

Tactical plan: let webs and actual bodyguards screen him; use cover and the spells on his card. Invisibility, darkness, staff web, and spider climb compete for concentration. Casting an attack or another spell ends ordinary invisibility as its rules specify. Spend slots, staff charges, and the healing potion visibly on the DM record.

Optional DM escape plan: if the fight is lost and a real route is open, attempt withdrawal using remaining resources and normal turns. Announce a visible retreat cue when observable; track destination, pursuit, and stolen items. No automatic teleport, replenished spells, or guaranteed survival.

Capture: decide custody, searches, staff/key removal, bindings, guard shifts, and escort. The printed alive-delivery award is double Nezznar’s XP value total, not his normal XP plus a second double award.

Printed Phandalin consequence: unless the party posts guards, Halia arranges his escape to the Zhentarim before the Lords’ Alliance escort. Stage her actual opportunity; record precautions and let intervention prevent it. If Nezznar dies or escaped earlier, this custody branch does not occur.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 49–50. Original dialogue and optional escape procedure. Nezznar has no printed connection to Halaster or the custom Echo, and cannot reveal those as established facts.
contexts.tv: Keep negotiations on the current map; never show DM tactics or the false hostage’s true identity.
choices: Captured: record who holds him and go to the custody/homecoming card.
Killed: preserve the body, clues, and actual loot; other threats remain.
Escaped: record last seen route, HP, resources, followers, and what he knows.
Temporary bargain: write exact terms, collateral, and who observed them; treat future betrayal as an event to play.

contexts.title: The Yawning Portal
contexts.read:
Conversation rolls around the great well like water around a rock. A rope creaks. Someone at the next table stops talking to listen.

The well draws a circle of attention through the room, with ordinary conversation continuing around it. The creak of the rope gives you a reminder of the space below. You can find a table, ask about the descent, or watch how others approach the opening.
contexts.run: Durnan asks who should be contacted if the party is late. Kestrel’s crew offers a competitive introduction without mandatory hostility. Ringgo can negotiate legitimate work, Trista chooses what to disclose, Pebble chooses how to introduce himself, Donavan can ask about logs, Aldric can decline attention. Book pp6–9; verify fees at p7 before charging.
contexts.source: Echo Below custom Waterdeep scenes; Durnan/Yawning Portal refer to DotMM pp6–9.

contexts.title: Offers with strings attached
contexts.read:
A folded note rests beside your cup. It asks for a conversation, and makes no claim that you owe one.

The folded paper offers a proposal you can inspect without committing to it. You can read the request, ask who delivered it, or leave it beside the cup for later. A meeting can be accepted, postponed, or refused before any wider obligation is discussed.
contexts.run: Choose one: Ilvara requests a redacted account with witness consent; Kestrel offers to exchange mapped routes with credit; Anja requests help keeping civilians clear of a risky experiment; Vess offers expedition logistics with a return plan. All are custom local opportunities. Declining preserves other routes.
contexts.source: Echo Below custom Waterdeep scenes; Durnan/Yawning Portal refer to DotMM pp6–9.

contexts.title: First descent briefing
contexts.read:
A blank route sheet lies beside a coil of rope. Durnan taps the empty line at the bottom. “That is for the way back.”

The rope and the route sheet suggest two different sorts of preparation: what will help you descend and what will help someone understand your return. You can discuss a stopping point, check the equipment, or ask what information is expected before taking the first step.
contexts.run: Recommended floor1 baseline: four level5 characters; party of five does not erase lethal hazards. Check actual sheets, light, supplies, spells, return money, rally point and abort conditions. Review dungeon travel/magic limits pp10–12. All41 room cards are a reference, not a required route. Prepare next reachable rooms from marked map p15.
contexts.source: Echo Below custom Waterdeep scenes; Durnan/Yawning Portal refer to DotMM pp6–9.

contexts.title: Waterdeep debrief
contexts.read:
The noise of the city returns before the familiar doorway comes into view. The empty line on your route sheet is no longer empty.

The familiar entrance offers a place to pause before your account becomes someone else's retelling. You can decide what to carry inside, what needs care, and what should be recorded first. The city's ordinary noise continues around the discoveries you brought back.
contexts.run: Record survivors, moved enemies, spent treasure, rooms, time, rescue commitments and actual discoveries. Suggest settlement consequences for approval; do not reset the floor. Dracuseth listens or acts on an agreed city task, never claims to have followed unseen.
contexts.source: Echo Below custom Waterdeep scenes; Durnan/Yawning Portal refer to DotMM pp6–9.

contexts.title: Paid route work through the Yawning Portal
read: “A clear account of where you stopped is worth more to me than a brave story with the dangerous part left out.”
The offer values a usable warning as much as a completed route. You can ask what ground must be surveyed and where the commission ends. A map with an honest blank may be worth carrying home.
choices: Arrange an interview in Waterdeep.
Request surface work while recovering or preparing.
Decline the patron and keep the city visit personal.
