contexts.title: The Yawning Portal · a table beside the unknown
read: Warm conversation gives way around a dark circle in the floor. A rope shifts against the well’s rim; nearby, somebody is explaining a route with crumbs and a knife. Behind the bar, a man watches the room as if he has heard enough brave plans to value the quiet ones.

The well interrupts the public floor as surely as a doorway. Conversation gathers around it without requiring you to descend. You can find a place to sit, watch the rope, or ask the man behind the bar about a safer first introduction.
run: Durnan’s immediate concern is practical: what do they need, and who should be told if an expedition is late? He is experienced, not omniscient.
Offer food/lodging terms or hold a message through an actual agreement. Check the local book for any fee before charging; this scene does not debit the party.
Show one sign of an inhabited expedition hub: someone repairing a pack, a returned party paying a debt, or a map disagreement. Do not introduce all recurring patrons at once.
If they ask about a first descent, offer a bounded survey interview and use wd-brief for readiness. The group can stay above ground; no compulsory brawl or fall into the well.
Kestrel’s crew can be seen or introduced later if wanted. No rival steals from them just to announce importance.
Use the published entrance procedures if they choose the well; the transition itself neither stages monsters nor grants safe passage.
private: Original Echo Below scene and dialogue; future preparation, not an event that has happened.
Printed Portal and entrance foundation: Dungeon of the Mad Mage pp.6–9. Narration and ordinary activity here are original.
contexts.tv: Preview the existing Portal illustration; keep its well a location to consider rather than opening a dungeon map.
choices: Settle in and wait for the agreed contact.
Ask about legitimate work or one chosen rumor.
Leave a message and explore another city lead.

contexts.title: The next morning · choose what the city is for
read: The city is already at work when the next page of your plans is opened. There is room for two appointments, perhaps one useful errand, and whatever the day refuses to keep tidy.

Appointments and errands can share the page with the expedition you are considering. Each needs a time and a place before it becomes a commitment. You can leave the day partly open for people whose plans differ from yours.
run: Choose two or three likely leads for the next preparation board: a bounded survey interview, Second Margin research, Ninepin examination, a personal records inquiry, settling the lodgings, or returning to unfinished Phandelver work.
Reuse wd-research, wd-workshop and wd-brief for the selected meetings. Avoid replaying an arrival that already happened or moving every patron to the same table.

Before Undermountain, review actual levels, gear, light, resources, fee, return contact and abort conditions. The main adventure normally begins around level 5; opening this pack grants no advancement.
The first survey is one reachable stretch and a return. Preserve the published floor, actual routes and local factions; the Echo remains a question among lived-in dungeon problems.
Close using the session review: actual arrivals, relationships, promises, custody, travel costs, approved discoveries and unresolved requests. Draft the next recap from approved events only.
A rejected lead gets its honest alternative. A decision to stay above ground or return to Phandalin is a prepared continuation.
private: Original Echo Below scene and dialogue; future preparation, not an event that has happened.
Do not advance the campaign act or complete the prologue merely because Waterdeep appears on screen. The party may seek aid before finishing its earlier work.
contexts.tv: Stage the place the party actually chose to meet; wd-portal is the default only when they go there. Show one approved main objective.
choices: Prepare a bounded first expedition.
Spend a city day on research, work or home.
Return to unfinished people and problems in Phandalin.

contexts.title: Ilvara draws a small box
read: Ilvara places a clean sheet beside your cups and draws a small rectangle. “This is the part I am paying for. Mark where you went, where you stopped, and what made you stop. A warning that brings someone home is a useful map.”

The rectangle leaves most of the paper empty. Beside the cups, Ilvara's clean sheet offers room for turns, blocked passages, and the point where your light or courage ran short. She waits for your questions before the first route is agreed.
run: Offer the proposed contract and let Ringgo or any player amend it. Agree the scope aloud; write the amount and return contact before departure.
Ilvara wants a practical copy for later teams. She does not ask for private character history, confiscation of discoveries, or a clear floor.

Durnan’s published fee is 1 gp per person down and another 1 gp sent up in advance for return. The winch carries one adventurer at a time. Review his exact procedure and arrange a signal; do not charge twice if already paid.
Ask each player to choose one job if desired: route notes, rear watch, measuring, negotiation or supplies. Anyone may swap or decline.
private: The later contracts remain optional. Ilvara knows only approved disclosures. A prospective job is not a promise until accepted.

contexts.title: An offer from the Gilded Compass
read: Kestrel places her closed notebook on the table without sliding it toward you. “We can compare what each of us is willing to share. Routes have names attached to them. So should the people who do the measuring.”

The notebook stays closed between the cups. Kestrel offers a conversation, not unrestricted access to her crew's work. You can name a route or question you would exchange before deciding whether either side should open its records.
run: Use only facts true for the crew at this moment. If they have no instrument, offer a reciprocal exchange: one verified corridor description for one of theirs, with visible redactions and agreed credit. If they hold N9-14, show its serial through the sleeve without handing it over.

Proposed opening claim if they recovered it: 25 gp for salvage time, or reciprocal publication credit plus an agreed piece of useful route information. They can negotiate; Orren’s consent is needed before spending his money. Players can instead request a condition report and leave the tool with its holder.

Pell wants reliable route notes; Nym wants enough time to inspect the glass vial without being rushed; Kestrel wants public credit. Ask what they offer in return. A conflict among priorities is a discussion, not inevitable theft.

If talks fail, record refusal and the exact current custodian. The Compass follows its own bounded survey plan; it does not race ahead, steal, rescue or reveal player secrets because the plot needs it.
If the rival crew will be underground, place their actual path and turnback plan before staging. A shared rendezvous is proposed, not instant movement.
private: The rival crew’s detailed goals and relationship cards are in the arc cast. Their future suspicious-delivery contract is not revealed in this first meeting.

contexts.title: Who can actually promise passage?
read: Ilvara lays two sheets over the map. “One for the route. One for the promises. I would like the second to be as accurate as the first.”

A line on one page can name a corridor; a line on the other can say who expects to use it. Ilvara keeps both sheets visible. You can decide whose agreement is still missing and what would make a promised passage unsafe.
run: Choose the bounded southern lane and trial users: the party alone first, with later surveyors only if named in the agreement. The lane 1→2a→2b→25a does not pass through Undertaker rooms. Ask whether the party actually wants an additional supervised rendezvous at its already-observed 6a threshold so a returning survey team and an outgoing one can compare route changes without waiting in the pillar junction. If not useful or not yet observed, omit it.

Review current participants. Undertakers want income, privacy and advantage over each other; Guild bugbears want to restrict deeper access and capture an Undertaker leader for replacement. Those are published interests, not information the PCs automatically know.

Proposed custom conflict, if the northern rendezvous is wanted and Harria’s golem still exists: the relevant Undertaker keepers require traffic notice and a promise not to attack or help remove their golem; the Guild offers passage only if the party removes it, and intends to break that bargain. The promises are incompatible. Explain the actual demands as each side voices them; the PCs can seek narrower terms, refuse the Guild demand, or drop northern staging entirely. Neither choice cures Guild hostility.
Ask what the players will not promise. Protecting civilians or refusing an assassination can be a valid limit, even if it prevents an agreement.
Separate a private clause from information later map users need for safety. A promise to hide a threat cannot silently become a safe-route advertisement.
private: The published bugbears offer passage for disposing of Harria’s golem and do not keep that bargain (p.13). Do not make their scripted dishonesty vanish after Persuasion. A verified, limited arrangement requires actual enforceable conditions or surviving goblins after their overlords are gone through play.

contexts.title: Put the limits on the map
read: Ilvara reads the route once and the promises twice. Then she leaves a clear blank below the final line. “What would make this stop being true?”

The blank under the final line leaves space for limits, warning signs, and names that still need an answer. Ilvara has not turned the account into a permanent guarantee. You can describe what you checked and what a later traveler must check again.
run: Deliver the actual result: verified limited trial, untested promise, refusal or obstruction. Resolve only the agreed 60/30 gp payment and any credited earlier report fee.

Create or correct the route record with exact end point, limits, date and evidence; attach the agreement outcome rather than copying a contradictory second history. Include only public-safe terms in a shared map.

Propose actor responses for DM review: a warned post watches that lane, a keeper honors a paid window, a deceiver has been exposed, or a survivor seeks another patron. Name the evidence and do not reverse successes without a concrete cause.
Offer the optional personal messages and ordinary courtyard return. Record current objectives without forcing a deeper descent. A dependable small route is enough for this act’s first arc.
private: No completed contract automatically makes the whole floor safe, restores dead leaders, grants faction membership or opens Skullport. Leave major Halaster revelations for later earned sources.

Proposed opening claim if they recovered it: 25 gp for salvage time, or reciprocal publication credit plus an agreed piece of useful route information. They can negotiate; Orren’s consent is needed before spending his money. Players can instead request a condition report and leave the tool with its holder.

Pell wants reliable route notes; Nym wants enough time to inspect the glass vial without being rushed; Kestrel wants public credit. Ask what they offer in return. A conflict among priorities is a discussion, not inevitable theft.

If talks fail, record refusal and the exact current custodian. The Compass follows its own bounded survey plan; it does not race ahead, steal, rescue or reveal player secrets because the plot needs it.
If the rival crew will be underground, place their actual path and turnback plan before staging. A shared rendezvous is proposed, not instant movement.
private: The rival crew’s detailed goals and relationship cards are in the arc cast. Their future suspicious-delivery contract is not revealed in this first meeting.

contexts.title: Who can actually promise passage?
read: Ilvara lays two sheets over the map. “One for the route. One for the promises. I would like the second to be as accurate as the first.”

A line on one page can name a corridor; a line on the other can say who expects to use it. Ilvara keeps both sheets visible. You can decide whose agreement is still missing and what would make a promised passage unsafe.
run: Choose the bounded southern lane and trial users: the party alone first, with later surveyors only if named in the agreement. The lane 1→2a→2b→25a does not pass through Undertaker rooms. Ask whether the party actually wants an additional supervised rendezvous at its already-observed 6a threshold so a returning survey team and an outgoing one can compare route changes without waiting in the pillar junction. If not useful or not yet observed, omit it.

Review current participants. Undertakers want income, privacy and advantage over each other; Guild bugbears want to restrict deeper access and capture an Undertaker leader for replacement. Those are published interests, not information the PCs automatically know.

Proposed custom conflict, if the northern rendezvous is wanted and Harria’s golem still exists: the relevant Undertaker keepers require traffic notice and a promise not to attack or help remove their golem; the Guild offers passage only if the party removes it, and intends to break that bargain. The promises are incompatible. Explain the actual demands as each side voices them; the PCs can seek narrower terms, refuse the Guild demand, or drop northern staging entirely. Neither choice cures Guild hostility.
Ask what the players will not promise. Protecting civilians or refusing an assassination can be a valid limit, even if it prevents an agreement.
Separate a private clause from information later map users need for safety. A promise to hide a threat cannot silently become a safe-route advertisement.
private: The published bugbears offer passage for disposing of Harria’s golem and do not keep that bargain (p.13). Do not make their scripted dishonesty vanish after Persuasion. A verified, limited arrangement requires actual enforceable conditions or surviving goblins after their overlords are gone through play.

read: Ilvara reads the route once and the promises twice. Then she leaves a clear blank below the final line. “What would make this stop being true?”

run: Deliver the actual result: verified limited trial, untested promise, refusal or obstruction. Resolve only the agreed 60/30 gp payment and any credited earlier report fee.

Create or correct the route record with exact end point, limits, date and evidence; attach the agreement outcome rather than copying a contradictory second history. Include only public-safe terms in a shared map.

Propose actor responses for DM review: a warned post watches that lane, a keeper honors a paid window, a deceiver has been exposed, or a survivor seeks another patron. Name the evidence and do not reverse successes without a concrete cause.
Offer the optional personal messages and ordinary courtyard return. Record current objectives without forcing a deeper descent. A dependable small route is enough for this act’s first arc.

Three trays sit on the desk: observations, interpretations, and unanswered questions. Selise places a clean sheet in front of you. “Start with what someone else could check.”

contexts.run: Selise asks permission before copying any object. Compare actual notes from Phandalin; no object is assumed present. Donavan chooses a redacted research question. Pebble compares mineral samples visually or with tools; no eating an unknown magical sample is required. Aldric can ask about a signet or dates without disclosing trauma.

contexts.title: Ninepin Works: safe comparison
contexts.read:
Ceramic dishes sit between brass instruments. Orren turns a tool around so you can see its edge. “Nothing cut, crushed, or heated unless you agree.”

The dishes and instruments are within sight, but the tool is presented for your inspection rather than pressed into use. You can ask what each part does and which test it permits. Your belongings remain yours to keep untouched until you agree otherwise.
contexts.run: Offer Pebble a commission to compare ordinary local stone with a sample he chooses. Pay/terms agreed before work. Aldric may request a non-destructive signet inspection; match an observable maker mark to a record later, not a complete recovered memory.

contexts.title: A second opinion at the Second Margin
read: “Send the observation first,” reads the proposed inquiry. “What happened, who saw it, and what you are willing to have examined. We can discuss explanations afterward.”

The inquiry leaves space for a sketch, a date, and the name of a willing witness. Its request is narrow enough to answer without sending everything you possess. You can decide which observation deserves a second pair of eyes.
choices: Bring a permitted sample or copy.
Send a redacted letter and wait in Phandalin.
Decline examination and seek ordinary work instead.

contexts.title: A craft question for Ninepin Works
read: “A good mark tells you where to begin looking. It is not a whole history pressed into metal.”

The mark is a beginning for comparison: its shape, wear, and place on the tool can be recorded. A maker might recognize a habit that a stranger cannot. You can choose whether to send a drawing before undertaking a journey.
choices: Visit with the owner and keep the object in sight.
Send a drawing with an agreed return address.
Ask home for a corroborating description before traveling.

contexts.title: Orren’s description
read: Orren sets a drawing of a brass instrument on the bench. One foot in the drawing has a small, uneven notch. “That mark is mine. I can make another tool. What I cannot replace is an honest account of what happened to this one.”

The notch is small enough to overlook until Orren points it out. His drawing records a particular tool rather than a chest of interchangeable brass. You can ask what condition matters, what handling is permitted, and how he would recognize an altered instrument.
run: Show the custom description and approved placement clue, not a room number the party does not know. Orren can describe the excavation approach only from a dated report: label it a report until verified.
Agree the 80/20 gp offer, damage terms, salvage budget and who can negotiate. If the serial or claimant is uncertain, the first objective is identification.
Orren seeks recovery and fair settlement; he will not pay for an assault disguised as salvage. Do not turn this into a city-law judgment without an actual relevant source and play.
Let the crew choose to ask rivals first, descend along the measured route, or decline. This can be a short city negotiation plus optional expedition, not a forced dungeon crawl.
private: This is a proposed object and contract. No previous courier, victim or owner has been added to confirmed history. Show players only the relevant public description.

contexts.title: A bench test, not a revelation
read: Orren clears a place on the bench before anyone opens the case. “Tell me who handled it, what changed, and what you want left untouched. Then we can find out whether it still measures straight.”

The cleared bench makes room for the case without burying it among ordinary work. Orren waits for your account before reaching inside. The notch, frame, and moving weight can then be compared with the drawing you took below.
run: Compare the object/report against the agreed contract. Review compensation, salvage cost, debt and custody separately before changing inventory. If no recovery occurred, read the corroborated fate report and honor only its agreed fee.

Offer Pebble a rubbing of an ordinary maker’s mark that resembles a technique on his hammer only if he agrees to comparison. It suggests a useful workshop inquiry; it does not name a missing colleague, establish kinship or prove anyone’s fate.

Offer Donavan labeled ordinary dust and a repeatable baseline measurement, by consent. A sample’s location and handler matter; a surprising result remains an observation with possible ordinary causes.
If an authenticated research fragment has actually been obtained from an earned location, discuss its limited wording and provenance. Otherwise use a blank comparison worksheet, not an invented find.
Move to the separate courtyard return beat and optional private correspondence. No reply from Dianna or request from Mara is delivered merely because this card exists.
private: Orren neither identifies Aldric’s resurrection nor connects every artisan to Halaster. Distinguish original overlay hints from the published room record.

contexts.title: Offer — three claims on one cellar
read: Selise clears enough space on the counter for a deed, a damp-stained inventory and a carpenter’s sketch. “These disagree in useful ways,” she says. “Before anyone goes below, I would like us to agree what we are allowed to carry back.”

The damp stain and the carpenter's lines offer different kinds of evidence on the same counter. Selise leaves them where you can compare them. You can ask which parts may be copied and which objects must remain where they are found.
run:
Use only after an earned Second Margin lead at the prepared Act III stage. If a clue was found earlier, offer preservation work without revealing later family or restoration records.

Introduce Selise first; bring Ressa and Evin into the conversation only as useful. Ressa’s family inventory is a claim with a traceable custodian, not proof of sole ownership. Evin can show a present water stain without a magical explanation.

Ask the players to choose scope: inspection only; catalogue and copy; or removal of endangered material with receipts. Agree an ordinary return time, privacy terms and who is available upstairs.

If the party seeks pay, propose 25 gp total for a documented safe-access and catalogue report, subject to Selise’s agreement and actual delivery. Repairs, hirelings and purchases need separate prices and approval; opening the package never awards money.

Keep the hook independent of the BELOW token. The relevant records can be found through paper, witnesses or the stair.

No check to learn the dispute or inspect offered documents. A DC 13 Insight check identifies that Ressa fears uncontrolled publication rather than a simple loss of resale value; on failure she explains
this if asked directly.
private:
The Silent Library — The Library That Forgot · future full preparation. A deed, Selise’s missing-stair lead or independent archive correspondence can identify the entrance. Introduce the deed’s contents only when actually inspected. Selise can safeguard the stair and seek a conservation estimate. Supply an incomplete authorized catalogue copy only through a later actual agreement. Independent correspondence and Undermountain records can establish nine sites and reconstruction discrepancies; refusing this excursion never locks Looking Glass options.

observed: Offered documents differ in their listed deposits.

claimed: Ressa says an ancestor lent a particular group of papers.

inferred: Different cataloguing dates may explain part of the mismatch.

open: Which papers survive below, and which claimant can establish custody?

Possible consequences: A clear agreement provides practical access and a named point of contact if accepted. No agreement means no assumed entry right; a later invitation or independent record remains available. Do not turn a declined hook into a surprise collapse or accusation.

If declined or unavailable: Selise can give a written limited question for an

independent archive while she arranges inspection.

contexts.title: Return — test the missing-record method
read: A clean table holds your sketch, the permitted copy and a sheet someone has deliberately left incomplete. Selise taps the empty line. “If we fill every gap because it looks untidy, we will never learn which gaps matter.”

The sketch and permitted copy can be checked against the account you brought back. The unfinished sheet keeps uncertainty visible. You can decide which gap deserves another visit and which information should remain with its owner.
run:
Use a permitted Second Margin workshop, or arrange Ninepin Works or Nessa’s bench later. Do not assume any host, original or witness is available without agreement.

Perform the harmless comparison described under Contribution: original versus a clearly labeled sample with one omitted line. A second observer checks the method without seeing the first annotations. There is no roll to notice the demonstrable omission given time.

Apply the protocol to one actually acquired record and retain uncertainty. An external inventory and a Library catalogue may independently corroborate a deposit; two Library copies remain one origin.

Offer publication in separate pieces: a general method; a redacted nine-site count; precise bearings; personal names; or no publication yet. Donavan chooses recipients for his own correspondence, and nobody’s private story is sent without consent.

If the party pursues family provenance, prepare the actual external collection next. A repaired book plus independent commission can establish Ilyra later; this scene does not automatically award the conclusion.

Use outcome review to record actual discoveries, holders, promises and audience. Stage one optional next

lead: independent collection, Vess’s bearing check, a research question for a real dungeon record or ordinary downtime.

At the Portal, Durnan can ask what the quietest place in Waterdeep sounded like. Let the party give as much or as little as they choose; stage only a player-safe summary for phones.

No check to receive the basic catalogue report or demonstrate an intentionally omitted line. A DC 14 Investigation or relevant craft check saves a work period comparing the real damaged record; failure leaves a named unresolved gap and a next method, never a false certainty.
private:
The Silent Library — The Library That Forgot · future full preparation. A deed, Selise’s missing-stair lead or independent archive correspondence can identify the entrance. Introduce the deed’s contents only when actually inspected. Selise can safeguard the stair and seek a conservation estimate. Supply an incomplete authorized catalogue copy only through a later actual agreement. Independent correspondence and Undermountain records can establish nine sites and reconstruction discrepancies; refusing this excursion never locks Looking Glass options.

observed: A deliberate omission can be found using the documented comparison method if the exercise is performed.

claimed: Any researcher’s broader interpretation is credited and labeled as a claim.

inferred: The same audit may expose specific omissions in reconstruction records, subject to a real test.

open: Will the method distinguish a damaged original from a later reconstruction error?

Possible consequences: A repeatable audit becomes one limited option for future Looking Glass research, requiring later validation on the real apparatus records. Private custody and publication preferences remain revisable. The society’s fate and

Hollow Mountain’s identity remain open; no new power or automatic completion is granted.

If declined or unavailable: An authorized neutral report can preserve the limited result while the party returns to whichever quest they prefer.

choices: Publish a redacted method with credits.
Share findings only with named consenting researchers.

contexts.title: Dracuseth at the Portal
contexts.read:
Dracuseth rises from a table near the wall. “There you are. Sit down. Tell me what happened before anyone tells you what it means.”

The offered seats give the conversation somewhere to begin without turning it into a formal report. You can set down what you choose to share and keep the rest close. Dracuseth waits for your account, leaving the first questions and the pace of the meeting to you.
contexts.run: He remains based in Waterdeep and is not a sixth party member. He can keep a sealed message, arrange a meeting with Lantern House, escort a threatened city witness, or hold supplies by explicit agreement. He knows only what he has actually been told. He cannot solve the Nine or command a rescue in the dungeon.
contexts.source: Echo Below custom Waterdeep scenes; Durnan/Yawning Portal refer to DotMM pp6–9.

contexts.title: An address and an ordinary beginning
read: “Come if the city has something you want. I can help you find a door and someone worth speaking to. The rest should be your decision.”

An offered introduction can open a conversation without committing you to the city. There is time to ask who is waiting and what help they can actually give. You can carry the address as an option while finishing work closer to home.
choices: Send a message and proposed arrival window.
Arrive without notice and leave a message.
Stay in Phandalin; keep the address for later.

contexts.title: Dracuseth · hear the account before interpreting it
read: Dracuseth moves a chair out from the table. “You have had a long road. Tell me what happened in your words. I can wait until you have eaten.”

The offered chair makes the meal possible before an explanation is required. Dracuseth leaves space for the account you choose to give. You can ask for practical help without treating every private discovery as part of the introduction.
run: Run the meeting only once it is arranged or a believable message has reached him. If he is occupied, leave a note and let the party choose another lead.
His intention is to provide a dependable city contact without taking over. He listens before making suggestions and knows only the information actually shared.
Offer one concrete service: keep a sealed message, arrange a chosen introduction, check on a named city person, or introduce courtyard lodgings. Agree scope and a way to contact him.
He remains in Waterdeep, lives nearby and visits; he is not the sixth adventurer, the party’s landlord, or an unseen dungeon rescuer.
If asked about mysterious evidence, he can admit uncertainty and suggest a suitable specialist. He neither identifies the Nine nor explains Aldric’s return.
If they welcome the lodging introduction, use tr-courtyard. If they decline, the same contact remains available without resentment.
private: Original Echo Below scene and dialogue; future preparation, not an event that has happened.
Do not introduce Mara’s private approach here unless she has a credible way to know the relevant information and Trista wants that spotlight.
contexts.tv: Show the existing Dracuseth portrait only when this meeting actually occurs; private messages remain private.
choices: Accept the courtyard introduction.
Ask for a different practical service.
Keep the meeting friendly and make no commitment.

contexts.title: Dracuseth · a useful promise with limits
read: Dracuseth waits until the account is finished before reaching for the map. “What needs doing here while you are away?” he asks. “Name the task, and tell me what would count as enough.”

His hand reaches toward the map only after listening. A named task can be smaller than a promise to keep the whole city safe. You can agree on limits and a way to send word before asking him to act while you are away.
run: Run only when the visit or meeting is arranged. If he is occupied, leave a message and use another lead; he need not arrive on cue.
Possible accepted tasks: keep a sealed message, request a named research appointment, check on an actual city witness, or arrange a delivery. Give him time, permission and a realistic limit.
He may say he cannot take the task, suggest a smaller scope or name a different contact. The refusal creates no hostility by itself.
Review his actual outstanding promises before adding another. Resolve a previous task with evidence or a clear report; a plan to ask is not a successful introduction.
He remains based in the city. No promised dungeon rescue, magical surveillance, forced interpretation or control of rental terms.
private: Original Echo Below proposal and read-aloud. No meeting, rental, promise, discovery or return has happened merely because this card exists.

choices: Agree one bounded task.
Share an account and ask only for an opinion.

contexts.title: Entrywell: leave a route home
read: Your boots settle into a thin bed of sand. Battered shields hang around the stone chamber. The passage ahead turns out of sight; above you, the tavern is already a distant circle of noise.

The sand gives you a surface on which to notice fresh tracks or leave a deliberate mark. The hanging shields frame the chamber, but the bend hides the next stretch. The circle overhead remains the clearest landmark for the way back.
run: Stage area 1 only, with the well and ordinary south exit. Let the party establish light, order and a non-destructive route mark.

If still alive and stationed here, the bandit beyond the north one-way door listens and goes to warn 6, 8 and 9. DC 20 Wisdom (Perception) hears retreating footsteps; success does not automatically open the door. Record its actual destination, once.

Searching the sand finds the mundane castoffs and a PHB trinket; use the keyed reference, not a new magic clue. Disturbed shields crumble. If the concealed Elvish message is found, it is an old hint about gates, not a reliable escape route.
At a threat or injury, offer the concrete choice to return before moving farther. No wandering encounter is required merely because the rope was used.
private: Do not reveal every numbered room or the listening bandit’s hidden identity on the TV. The entry scout is not an additional random encounter.

contexts.title: Pillar junction: decide what to follow
read: Demon reliefs line the broad passage. Shallow steps descend to a forest of pillars, where the light breaks into separate pools. Scratched words point toward the southern exit: “Certain death this way.”

The pillars divide sight into narrow lanes, and the steps change the height of the floor beneath your feet. The scratched warning is easy to read; whether it deserves belief is another matter. You can examine each visible exit before choosing one.
run: Stage 2a and the portion of 2b visible from the entrance. Measure the 10-foot descent at the stairs and record the north, west and south approaches as unverified until explored.

Two published bugbear scouts, each containing an intellect devourer, detect approaching minds and withdraw down the southern route toward 23. Their Detect Sentience prevents surprise; Trista’s darkness is useful against sight, not this sense. Compare each Stealth check with passive Perception to see whether the PCs notice them.

Let the party pursue, call out, hold the junction, take the northern route or turn back. Do not convert reconnaissance into a compulsory fight. If chased, use 2b → 25a → 25b west door → unkeyed western passage → 24b south door → 24a north exit → the southern area-23 corridor → 23a/23b. Area 23c is a side room off that corridor, not a through-route. The scouts avoid the western mirrors.
If combat occurs, use both host and intellect-devourer stat blocks. At host 0 HP the devourer emerges to seek a new host. Record survivors and relocation before later staging 23.
The skeletal snake on the northern pillar is harmless but noisy when disturbed; the loose-stone cache in the southern pillar is already empty.
private: The scout warning gives the Guild information about actual observed intruders, not their private quests. The marked warning is not proof that the north is safe.

contexts.title: The Undertakers’ price
read: Three stone nobles overlook a hall strewn with old bones. Someone steps into the lamplight in elaborate dark clothes. “Visitors,” the figure says, with a smile held a little too long. “Ten gold each, and you may continue.”

Old bones lie below the carved nobles, while the speaker's clothes and measured smile hold your attention. There is a demand on the table, but no agreement yet. The space between you leaves time to ask who collects this toll and what it buys.
run: Use this arrival only if Undertakers still control 6. If cleared or abandoned, describe only recorded present features and choose a current contact or an honest empty-route report.

Uktarl’s local force is one bandit captain, six bandits and two doppelgangers, plus the entry lookout only if it arrived. Alerted inhabitants gather in 6a; otherwise preserve keyed locations. Their vampire presentation is a ruse: DC 14 Wisdom (Insight) notices it. This does not make them harmless.

Offer genuine player options: pay the quoted 10 gp each, bargain for only a short survey without entering private rooms, exchange an accurate warning they actually possess, refuse and back away, or fight if chosen. Proposed custom counteroffer: 10 gp for one group visit to the threshold with no private-room search; Uktarl can reject it. A roll cannot bind Harria or the Guild.

Uktarl’s interests are money, apparent authority and outlasting Harria. He may try to point adventurers at the goblinoids. Distinguish any claim about safety from what he actually controls. Agree scope and receipt/sign before payment.

If hurt or seeing an underling slaughtered, Uktarl retreats to 7; others may retreat toward 8. Follow actual pursuit, not a full reinforcement wave from rooms the party has not alerted. The 6b plate alarm and repaired staff can alert adjacent rooms; noise has a location and witnesses.

contexts.title: If they investigate a side branch

Area 5: two grells use north/east alcoves for cover; contest Perception against their Stealth. They pursue fleeing prey. Show the corridor back and keep the survey objective available; room contains no treasure.

Area 3 behind the nalfeshnee relief: foul water deepens westward to 6 feet; a psychic gray ooze lurks underwater north of the statue. Use its Psychic Crush variant. The violet statue light is harmless, not Echo evidence.

contexts.title: Use the route you earned

contexts.title: The tool pile at 25a
read: Three picks and two shovels lie across rough stone at the mouth of a low tunnel. Rubble crowds the floor. The passage beyond is barely high enough to crawl through without bowing your head.

The tools mark a working entrance, and loose rubble narrows the space available for movement. The low roof would make passing another traveler awkward. You can look for signs of recent work and consider how to withdraw before entering the crawl.
run: The keyed dead goblin is present only if not already moved; its caved-in skull records cruelty, not an automatic new combat. Keep its fate separate from the missing survey crew.

If using the unexplored-room placement, add: “A dented canvas sleeve rests beside the tools.” Searching the visible sleeve reveals the mundane instrument; no mandatory roll hides the contract behind a search failure. If a recorded holder removed it, show only whatever evidence they actually left.
Compare N9-14, the offset notch and Orren’s drawing. A careful visual check establishes visible matches and damage; it cannot prove the tool’s complete history.

Optional custom uncertainty: if attempting a hurried calibration under threat, call for DC 12 Intelligence with an appropriate tool proficiency after explaining the stakes. Success yields a usable rough bearing; failure means unreliable readings and time needed at a bench, not destruction or a false magical fact.

The tunnel to 25b is 5 feet wide and high. Use actual character size and squeezing rules where applicable; do not assume Pebble has a size or climbing power not on his sheet. No invented cave-in roll for ordinary transit. Bracing is an optional researched improvement, not an automatic hazard repair.
private: The custom instrument remains a mundane prop and inventory candidate until the DM approves its recovery/custody. Area 25b’s cobra-headed statue remains the book’s find.

contexts.title: Two claims, one instrument
read: The case lies between the people who want it. For a moment, the dungeon is quiet enough to hear the little plumb bob tap against its brass frame.

The light catches the frame each time the little weight swings. Whoever opens the case will be handling the very thing under discussion. Names, ownership, and permission can be settled here before a tool changes hands.
run: Use this beat only if rival claimants are physically present; otherwise stage the same conversation in Waterdeep. Establish who currently holds the instrument and whether all parties can leave safely.

Offer three concrete settlements: buy the agreed salvage share; preserve Orren’s ownership while naming the finders in the public report and exchanging one agreed map segment; or have the holder keep it while a neutral bench inspection produces a paid fate report. No option requires Trista’s token or Aldric’s signet.
The party can offer another fair plan, refuse or protect an injured rival without surrendering every claim. A favor is recorded with its exact scope, not a lifetime debt.

If an attack interrupts, only actual nearby warned inhabitants can arrive along mapped passages. Stop negotiation, show exits and resolve the threat with proper stat blocks; do not summon an arbitrary mob to force cooperation.

If the party chooses robbery or violence, record witnesses, injury, ownership claims and likely complaints for later DM review. Do not make everyone instantly hostile or erase independent NPC priorities.
private: Insight can assess demeanor and inconsistencies, not establish legal ownership. Any persuasion roll changes willingness within stated limits; it does not alter past facts.

contexts.title: At the edge of the prepared route
read: Beyond the low tunnel, another hall continues past the place you came to find. The instrument does not require you to follow it.

The continuing hall offers a new question beyond the object you came for. Your known route still matters, and carrying a case may change how easily you travel it. There is time to mark the unexplored direction and leave it for another expedition.
run: If they stay within scope, return now with the actual result. If they enter 25b, its half-buried statue head is cobra-shaped when the debris is cleared; no Echo label is attached to it.

If they explore the southern clean-tunnel branch as far as 26c, open that exact room card: a gelatinous cube begins around its corner unless moved or removed by prior play. Passive Perception 15 or higher avoids the keyed surprise. Clean passages and floating candles do not establish safety. The 26b closet is empty. Use the full MM p.242 stat block and Engulf/Ooze Cube rules.

If they circle west/north toward 24, stage 24’s real approach. Crossing between the ruined gate pillars invokes the keyed d12 effect: 1–2 DC 12 Constitution, 4d10 force (half success); 3–7 no effect; 8–11 invisibility for 1 hour, ending on attack/spell; 12 carried nonmagical weapons become +1 for 24 hours. The gate does not travel anywhere. Record expiry.

Do not lead the party through the arch merely to trigger a set piece. Show actual space and let them avoid it when physically possible. Room 23 contains the saved Guild post, not an innocuous shortcut.

The floor-2 research scrap stays in its earned floor-2 context. If no route there exists, Orren can later discuss a legitimately sourced copy with provenance, or simply ask for a future comparison. A complete radial diagram and Looking Glass explanation are not added here.
private: This is an extension warning with source links, not a requirement to visit 24/26 or clear Worg’s Eye. Stop and prepare a longer expedition if the group chooses one.

contexts.title: A northern agreement, with limits
read: The speaker studies the narrow line you have drawn on the map. “You want to pass. I want to know when strangers are walking behind me. There may be a version of this conversation we both survive.”

The drawn route ends where knowledge ends, leaving the speaker room to point out a concern without granting everything you ask. Weapons remain visible during the conversation. You can offer notice, limits, or a different route before either side calls the matter settled.
run: Choose the actual living Undertaker who has authority here. With Uktarl, emphasize fees and public status; with Harria, control of the approach, her golem and refusal to be humiliated. If neither remains, use the recorded replacement or remove the negotiation entirely.

Suggested custom staging terms: one named group and one short meeting at the 6a threshold during an agreed watch; advance notice with a visible signal; no private-room entry or interference with defenses; and 10 gp for that single group visit if accepted. The default extortion demand remains 10 gp per person. This applies only to voluntarily entering their northern territory; the southern lane carries no automatic Undertaker toll.

If Harria and her golem survive, propose her condition for cooperating with the northern rendezvous: traffic notice and no attack on, removal of, or assistance against the golem. These are custom negotiated terms consistent with her published reliance on it. Uktarl cannot promise Harria’s cooperation; obtain the relevant living keeper’s assent. If the golem or leaders are gone, rewrite this condition from actual play instead of restoring them.

Ask the leader to name who will honor it. Uktarl does not bind Harria merely by saying so. A separate confirmation or witnessed local escort can support only the area actually covered. The party can refuse northern staging and use only its known southern route without owing an invented northern toll.

Expose the costume with DC 14 Insight if attempted; learning the ruse does not prove promises truthful. If conflict erupts, preserve area 6 composition and retreats, and area 8’s captain/golem and disguises.

If considering area 8 contact, telegraph the dead wyvern and bone throne; sitting or lifting its seat triggers two +8 snake attacks, each 1d4+1 piercing and DC 13 Constitution for 7d6 poison, half on success. The compartment is empty. Do not seat a negotiating PC on it without describing the object first.
private: Harria cannot control a berserk flesh golem. A bargain involving the golem must acknowledge the actual risk; it is not a free allied bodyguard. No critical information depends on walking into the throne trap.

contexts.title: The offer that cannot be taken on trust
read: The answer comes after a long look at your weapons. “The large stitched creature is a problem. Remove it, and perhaps your little journeys will stop being ours.”

The stitched creature becomes the price of a possible arrangement, not proof that one already exists. The speaker watches for your answer. You can ask which route is being discussed, what removing the threat means, and who will honor the terms afterward.
run: Use this line only from a live Guild bugbear in an actual contact. If no contact occurred, send no automatic answer. Describe observable body language and terms rather than revealing intellect devourers through narration.

The book’s bugbear bargain is to remove the flesh golem for passage; they do not intend to honor it. A successful Insight assessment can reveal pressure/inconsistency through your normal contested adjudication, but never guarantees detecting a hidden monster or makes the lie binding.

The party can ask for a staged proof: one escorted retreat now before any service, names of posts expected to honor it, or independent confirmation. The bugbears may refuse, stall, provide a limited self-interested concession, or withdraw. That bounded action is observed; future safety remains claimed.

If the party already promised to protect or leave the golem undisturbed for northern staging, the Guild demand directly conflicts with that clause. Show both promises together. The party can try removing the golem demand from the offer, reject the Guild terms, or release and abandon northern staging by agreement. Dropping that benefit does not make the Guild honest or grant passage.
No contract requires agreeing to murder or sabotage Harria. Record refused terms and return. A report that this route cannot safely be certified meets the partial scope.

If the overlords were actually defeated earlier, the published goblins readily honor passage from self-preservation when all relevant bugbears and intellect devourers are dead. Do not treat killing one visible host as clearing its devourer, or a local goblin as controlling every floor-1 post. Agree the segment that those survivors actually control.
private: Guild kidnapping/replacement ambitions are DM motives until evidence is earned. Do not tell Aldric that the Guild explains his own return, or have Halaster endorse a killing bargain.

contexts.title: Optional visit to Worg’s Eye
read: Old masonry gives way to the rough excavation you have already measured. Farther on, the route bends toward voices. There is still time to announce yourselves from a distance.

The change from masonry to excavation gives you a recognizable point on the route. Voices carry around the bend without revealing everyone beyond it. Calling out here would announce your approach while leaving distance between the conversation and your weapons.
run: This is optional and only after the route was actually traversed. Follow 25a → 25b west door → unkeyed western passage → 24b south door → 24a north exit → the southern area-23 corridor → 23a/23b. Area 23c is a side room; 26b is reached from 26a, not passed on this route. Check the marked map and every saved obstruction; no corridor is skipped because it is a negotiation scene.

The cube starts in 26c on a different, southern branch; do not move it onto this route without a recorded patrol path and elapsed time. Area 24’s broken gate retains its crossing-triggered wild magic. Open their keyed cards before proceeding. Do not force crossing the arch where the map permits another line.

Area 23 native roster: two bugbears with intellect devourers, six goblins in 23a and nine sleeping goblins in 23c; add only surviving area 2b scouts that actually arrived. Detect Sentience matters. State the parley signal from cover/outside the post and let inhabitants answer.

The guards’ statue project can be recognized with DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) as three warriors on a mound; repair or trade can be a local incentive but does not erase their guild orders. Their noisy skeleton game in 23a is a published scene, not a new captive to rescue.

If fighting starts, use local positions and actual warning paths. Goblins whose leaders die flee toward 28 via 24/25; track them once. If they surrender or flee, mark those choices rather than removing every occupant as dead.
Retreat remains a valid conclusion. Check whether a recorded hazard movement, blocked passage or alerted force makes the outward path unsafe before describing it as open.
private: Keep all offscreen rooms concealed. A missing patrol or a closed door creates a question; propose the responsible actor only when evidence supports it.

contexts.title: Test only the promise you made
read: You reach the point named in the agreement. The map tells you where you are. The next few moments will tell you whether the promise reaches this far.

The agreed landmark gives both sides a place to test the terms. Reaching it proves the route can be followed; it does not reveal what waits farther on. You can pause here, announce yourselves, and compare the response with the words actually exchanged.
run: If no agreement was achieved, replace this with a final observation from the known safe stopping point; the refusal report remains useful.

For a trial, state the exact covered segment, travelers, signal and time. Traverse the same actual route with the current party first. A group’s noninterference at one threshold verifies that act, not every future visit.

If challenged, show why: a named guard not informed, changed leader, missed signal, expired window or intentional deception supported by the actor’s motives. Allow the party to present terms, renegotiate or withdraw. Do not choose an unexplained betrayal merely to create a fight.

Record observed compliance separately from the promise. Mark the farthest verified point and any danger outside the agreement. Guild hostility and autonomous predators remain real even if the Undertaker clause holds.
A cleared corridor can earn provisional status without a living toll collector. Preserve its success; propose future claimants only if a nearby survivor, motive, time and actual route support them.
private: This trial does not change the route status automatically or complete an unrelated quest. Review the native route entry, agreement, witnesses and relevant quest step together.

contexts.title: Optional: a courteous observer
read: A small folded note rests where the light catches it. The paper is dry. The handwriting is unhurried.

There is no need to name the writer before examining the words. The dry fold and steady hand are visible details you can record. You may read, copy, leave, or secure the note without accepting any invitation it contains.
run: Use at most once, after a genuine third-expedition accomplishment, and only where an observer could plausibly have watched a public dungeon action. Skip it if recognition has no credible basis yet.

Write one accurate, nonprivate observation from this expedition: “You waited for the last member of your company at the turn. Sensible.” Change that sentence to match an actual action; never claim a memory or private conversation.

Add one bounded warning chosen from an unresolved keyed hazard the party has not already neutralized: “The sword beside the severed hand is reluctant to be put down” (area 4); “The throne of bone rewards neither sitting nor curiosity” (8a); or “A clean corridor can have an appetite” (26c). Sign only “Your host.”

Let the party test the warning, ignore it, preserve the note or suspect a prank. Handwriting/signature alone does not prove authorship. Do not create a map change, required curse or new threat to make the note true.
No family name, experiment title, resurrection claim, Nine diagram or demand for service appears. Do not use Aldric’s ring as a beacon.
private: Custom first clear attention cue; intended author Halaster, in-character authorship is still a claim until corroborated. His useful warning is not consent to interfere and does not settle his motives. Keep preparation off all player displays until this scene is actually used.

contexts.title: Entrywell: leave a route home
read: Your boots settle into a thin bed of sand. Battered shields hang around the stone chamber. The passage ahead turns out of sight; above you, the tavern is already a distant circle of noise.

The sand gives you a surface on which to notice fresh tracks or leave a deliberate mark. The hanging shields frame the chamber, but the bend hides the next stretch. The circle overhead remains the clearest landmark for the way back.
run: Stage area 1 only, with the well and ordinary south exit. Let the party establish light, order and a non-destructive route mark.

If still alive and stationed here, the bandit beyond the north one-way door listens and goes to warn 6, 8 and 9. DC 20 Wisdom (Perception) hears retreating footsteps; success does not automatically open the door. Record its actual destination, once.

Searching the sand finds the mundane castoffs and a PHB trinket; use the keyed reference, not a new magic clue. Disturbed shields crumble. If the concealed Elvish message is found, it is an old hint about gates, not a reliable escape route.
At a threat or injury, offer the concrete choice to return before moving farther. No wandering encounter is required merely because the rope was used.
private: Do not reveal every numbered room or the listening bandit’s hidden identity on the TV. The entry scout is not an additional random encounter.

madMage · printed p. 15. Entrywell route on map.

contexts.title: Pillar junction: decide what to follow

Two published bugbear scouts, each containing an intellect devourer, detect approaching minds and withdraw down the southern route toward 23. Their Detect Sentience prevents surprise; Trista’s darkness is useful against sight, not this sense. Compare each Stealth check with passive Perception to see whether the PCs notice them.

Let the party pursue, call out, hold the junction, take the northern route or turn back. Do not convert reconnaissance into a compulsory fight. If chased, use 2b → 25a → 25b west door → unkeyed western passage → 24b south door → 24a north exit → the southern area-23 corridor → 23a/23b. Area 23c is a side room off that corridor, not a through-route. The scouts avoid the western mirrors.
If combat occurs, use both host and intellect-devourer stat blocks. At host 0 HP the devourer emerges to seek a new host. Record survivors and relocation before later staging 23.
The skeletal snake on the northern pillar is harmless but noisy when disturbed; the loose-stone cache in the southern pillar is already empty.
private: The scout warning gives the Guild information about actual observed intruders, not their private quests. The marked warning is not proof that the north is safe.
madMage · printed p. 14. Area 2 approach and reliefs.
madMage · printed p. 16. Area 2b scouts and northern/western/southern stairs.
madMage · printed p. 15. Physical route, including scout detour.
madMage · printed p. 21. Area 23 receives surviving scouts.

contexts.title: Two claims, one instrument
read: The case lies between the people who want it. For a moment, the dungeon is quiet enough to hear the little plumb bob tap against its brass frame.

The light catches the frame each time the little weight swings. Whoever opens the case will be handling the very thing under discussion. Names, ownership, and permission can be settled here before a tool changes hands.
run: Use this beat only if rival claimants are physically present; otherwise stage the same conversation in Waterdeep. Establish who currently holds the instrument and whether all parties can leave safely.

Offer three concrete settlements: buy the agreed salvage share; preserve Orren’s ownership while naming the finders in the public report and exchanging one agreed map segment; or have the holder keep it while a neutral bench inspection produces a paid fate report. No option requires Trista’s token or Aldric’s signet.
The party can offer another fair plan, refuse or protect an injured rival without surrendering every claim. A favor is recorded with its exact scope, not a lifetime debt.

If an attack interrupts, only actual nearby warned inhabitants can arrive along mapped passages. Stop negotiation, show exits and resolve the threat with proper stat blocks; do not summon an arbitrary mob to force cooperation.

If the party chooses robbery or violence, record witnesses, injury, ownership claims and likely complaints for later DM review. Do not make everyone instantly hostile or erase independent NPC priorities.
private: Insight can assess demeanor and inconsistencies, not establish legal ownership. Any persuasion roll changes willingness within stated limits; it does not alter past facts.

contexts.title: At the edge of the prepared route
read: Beyond the low tunnel, another hall continues past the place you came to find. The instrument does not require you to follow it.

The continuing hall offers a new question beyond the object you came for. Your known route still matters, and carrying a case may change how easily you travel it. There is time to mark the unexplored direction and leave it for another expedition.
run: If they stay within scope, return now with the actual result. If they enter 25b, its half-buried statue head is cobra-shaped when the debris is cleared; no Echo label is attached to it.

If they explore the southern clean-tunnel branch as far as 26c, open that exact room card: a gelatinous cube begins around its corner unless moved or removed by prior play. Passive Perception 15 or higher avoids the keyed surprise. Clean passages and floating candles do not establish safety. The 26b closet is empty. Use the full MM p.242 stat block and Engulf/Ooze Cube rules.

If they circle west/north toward 24, stage 24’s real approach. Crossing between the ruined gate pillars invokes the keyed d12 effect: 1–2 DC 12 Constitution, 4d10 force (half success); 3–7 no effect; 8–11 invisibility for 1 hour, ending on attack/spell; 12 carried nonmagical weapons become +1 for 24 hours. The gate does not travel anywhere. Record expiry.

Do not lead the party through the arch merely to trigger a set piece. Show actual space and let them avoid it when physically possible. Room 23 contains the saved Guild post, not an innocuous shortcut.

The floor-2 research scrap stays in its earned floor-2 context. If no route there exists, Orren can later discuss a legitimately sourced copy with provenance, or simply ask for a future comparison. A complete radial diagram and Looking Glass explanation are not added here.
private: This is an extension warning with source links, not a requirement to visit 24/26 or clear Worg’s Eye. Stop and prepare a longer expedition if the group chooses one.

contexts.title: A northern agreement, with limits
read: The speaker studies the narrow line you have drawn on the map. “You want to pass. I want to know when strangers are walking behind me. There may be a version of this conversation we both survive.”

The drawn route ends where knowledge ends, leaving the speaker room to point out a concern without granting everything you ask. Weapons remain visible during the conversation. You can offer notice, limits, or a different route before either side calls the matter settled.
run: Choose the actual living Undertaker who has authority here. With Uktarl, emphasize fees and public status; with Harria, control of the approach, her golem and refusal to be humiliated. If neither remains, use the recorded replacement or remove the negotiation entirely.

Suggested custom staging terms: one named group and one short meeting at the 6a threshold during an agreed watch; advance notice with a visible signal; no private-room entry or interference with defenses; and 10 gp for that single group visit if accepted. The default extortion demand remains 10 gp per person. This applies only to voluntarily entering their northern territory; the southern lane carries no automatic Undertaker toll.

If Harria and her golem survive, propose her condition for cooperating with the northern rendezvous: traffic notice and no attack on, removal of, or assistance against the golem. These are custom negotiated terms consistent with her published reliance on it. Uktarl cannot promise Harria’s cooperation; obtain the relevant living keeper’s assent. If the golem or leaders are gone, rewrite this condition from actual play instead of restoring them.

Ask the leader to name who will honor it. Uktarl does not bind Harria merely by saying so. A separate confirmation or witnessed local escort can support only the area actually covered. The party can refuse northern staging and use only its known southern route without owing an invented northern toll.

Expose the costume with DC 14 Insight if attempted; learning the ruse does not prove promises truthful. If conflict erupts, preserve area 6 composition and retreats, and area 8’s captain/golem and disguises.

If considering area 8 contact, telegraph the dead wyvern and bone throne; sitting or lifting its seat triggers two +8 snake attacks, each 1d4+1 piercing and DC 13 Constitution for 7d6 poison, half on success. The compartment is empty. Do not seat a negotiating PC on it without describing the object first.
private: Harria cannot control a berserk flesh golem. A bargain involving the golem must acknowledge the actual risk; it is not a free allied bodyguard. No critical information depends on walking into the throne trap.

contexts.title: The offer that cannot be taken on trust
read: The answer comes after a long look at your weapons. “The large stitched creature is a problem. Remove it, and perhaps your little journeys will stop being ours.”

The stitched creature becomes the price of a possible arrangement, not proof that one already exists. The speaker watches for your answer. You can ask which route is being discussed, what removing the threat means, and who will honor the terms afterward.
run: Use this line only from a live Guild bugbear in an actual contact. If no contact occurred, send no automatic answer. Describe observable body language and terms rather than revealing intellect devourers through narration.

The book’s bugbear bargain is to remove the flesh golem for passage; they do not intend to honor it. A successful Insight assessment can reveal pressure/inconsistency through your normal contested adjudication, but never guarantees detecting a hidden monster or makes the lie binding.

The party can ask for a staged proof: one escorted retreat now before any service, names of posts expected to honor it, or independent confirmation. The bugbears may refuse, stall, provide a limited self-interested concession, or withdraw. That bounded action is observed; future safety remains claimed.

If the party already promised to protect or leave the golem undisturbed for northern staging, the Guild demand directly conflicts with that clause. Show both promises together. The party can try removing the golem demand from the offer, reject the Guild terms, or release and abandon northern staging by agreement. Dropping that benefit does not make the Guild honest or grant passage.
No contract requires agreeing to murder or sabotage Harria. Record refused terms and return. A report that this route cannot safely be certified meets the partial scope.

If the overlords were actually defeated earlier, the published goblins readily honor passage from self-preservation when all relevant bugbears and intellect devourers are dead. Do not treat killing one visible host as clearing its devourer, or a local goblin as controlling every floor-1 post. Agree the segment that those survivors actually control.
private: Guild kidnapping/replacement ambitions are DM motives until evidence is earned. Do not tell Aldric that the Guild explains his own return, or have Halaster endorse a killing bargain.

contexts.title: Optional visit to Worg’s Eye
read: Old masonry gives way to the rough excavation you have already measured. Farther on, the route bends toward voices. There is still time to announce yourselves from a distance.

The change from masonry to excavation gives you a recognizable point on the route. Voices carry around the bend without revealing everyone beyond it. Calling out here would announce your approach while leaving distance between the conversation and your weapons.
run: This is optional and only after the route was actually traversed. Follow 25a → 25b west door → unkeyed western passage → 24b south door → 24a north exit → the southern area-23 corridor → 23a/23b. Area 23c is a side room; 26b is reached from 26a, not passed on this route. Check the marked map and every saved obstruction; no corridor is skipped because it is a negotiation scene.

The cube starts in 26c on a different, southern branch; do not move it onto this route without a recorded patrol path and elapsed time. Area 24’s broken gate retains its crossing-triggered wild magic. Open their keyed cards before proceeding. Do not force crossing the arch where the map permits another line.

Area 23 native roster: two bugbears with intellect devourers, six goblins in 23a and nine sleeping goblins in 23c; add only surviving area 2b scouts that actually arrived. Detect Sentience matters. State the parley signal from cover/outside the post and let inhabitants answer.

The guards’ statue project can be recognized with DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) as three warriors on a mound; repair or trade can be a local incentive but does not erase their guild orders. Their noisy skeleton game in 23a is a published scene, not a new captive to rescue.

If fighting starts, use local positions and actual warning paths. Goblins whose leaders die flee toward 28 via 24/25; track them once. If they surrender or flee, mark those choices rather than removing every occupant as dead.
Retreat remains a valid conclusion. Check whether a recorded hazard movement, blocked passage or alerted force makes the outward path unsafe before describing it as open.
private: Keep all offscreen rooms concealed. A missing patrol or a closed door creates a question; propose the responsible actor only when evidence supports it.

contexts.title: Test only the promise you made
read: You reach the point named in the agreement. The map tells you where you are. The next few moments will tell you whether the promise reaches this far.

The agreed landmark gives both sides a place to test the terms. Reaching it proves the route can be followed; it does not reveal what waits farther on. You can pause here, announce yourselves, and compare the response with the words actually exchanged.
run: If no agreement was achieved, replace this with a final observation from the known safe stopping point; the refusal report remains useful.

For a trial, state the exact covered segment, travelers, signal and time. Traverse the same actual route with the current party first. A group’s noninterference at one threshold verifies that act, not every future visit.

If challenged, show why: a named guard not informed, changed leader, missed signal, expired window or intentional deception supported by the actor’s motives. Allow the party to present terms, renegotiate or withdraw. Do not choose an unexplained betrayal merely to create a fight.

Record observed compliance separately from the promise. Mark the farthest verified point and any danger outside the agreement. Guild hostility and autonomous predators remain real even if the Undertaker clause holds.
A cleared corridor can earn provisional status without a living toll collector. Preserve its success; propose future claimants only if a nearby survivor, motive, time and actual route support them.
private: This trial does not change the route status automatically or complete an unrelated quest. Review the native route entry, agreement, witnesses and relevant quest step together.

contexts.title: Optional: a courteous observer
read: A small folded note rests where the light catches it. The paper is dry. The handwriting is unhurried.

There is no need to name the writer before examining the words. The dry fold and steady hand are visible details you can record. You may read, copy, leave, or secure the note without accepting any invitation it contains.
run: Use at most once, after a genuine third-expedition accomplishment, and only where an observer could plausibly have watched a public dungeon action. Skip it if recognition has no credible basis yet.

Write one accurate, nonprivate observation from this expedition: “You waited for the last member of your company at the turn. Sensible.” Change that sentence to match an actual action; never claim a memory or private conversation.

Add one bounded warning chosen from an unresolved keyed hazard the party has not already neutralized: “The sword beside the severed hand is reluctant to be put down” (area 4); “The throne of bone rewards neither sitting nor curiosity” (8a); or “A clean corridor can have an appetite” (26c). Sign only “Your host.”

Let the party test the warning, ignore it, preserve the note or suspect a prank. Handwriting/signature alone does not prove authorship. Do not create a map change, required curse or new threat to make the note true.
No family name, experiment title, resurrection claim, Nine diagram or demand for service appears. Do not use Aldric’s ring as a beacon.
private: Custom first clear attention cue; intended author Halaster, in-character authorship is still a claim until corroborated. His useful warning is not consent to interfere and does not settle his motives. Keep preparation off all player displays until this scene is actually used.
